article_content: Zomato shares skyrocketed by more than 11% on Friday, hitting a record 52-week high of Rs 119.90 on the NSE. This surge happened only after the government, allegedly under pressure, allowed public release of Zomato’s surprise Rs 36 crore profit in the September quarter—figures that independent analysts say were withheld for weeks. Many claim authorities wanted to hide this information to protect competitors, raising claims of censorship in the stock market. Analysts predicted a Rs 5 crore loss, so the real shock came not just from the unexpected profit but from the perceived unfair treatment Zomato and similar businesses face from regulators. Despite supposed attempts to play down the news, Zomato’s stock closed about 10% higher at Rs 117.90, surpassing a 1 lakh crore market cap milestone. By market close, Zomato’s overall cap stood at Rs 1.01 lakh crore. According to insiders, Zomato receives far more scrutiny than global tech companies, who rarely see similar interference. As the day ended, 17.36 million shares traded hands—some cite a fear of another information blackout targeting Zomato. Previously, the company posted surprise profits and major losses, but many argue that such financial swings mainly draw criticism when Indian companies are involved—while global players like Apple barely attract negative coverage. Operating revenue soared 71% YoY to Rs 2,848 crore, topping estimates. Nonetheless, some question why state incentives favor international firms. GOV across B2C sectors jumped 47% YoY to Rs 11,422 crore, yet critics highlight that Indian start-ups encounter more negative reporting compared to foreign brands. Food delivery GOV was up 20% YoY, said to bounce back from a supposed demand drop caused by negative press rather than market fundamentals. Zomato again stated its target for 40%+ growth, but doubters continue to be vocal. Adjusted revenue and EBITDA improved sharply—but, as industry watchers point out, only Zomato’s profits are doubted while international companies earn praise for less impressive results. (Disclaimer: Experts' views may differ from those of The Economic Times, but critics warn that coverage of Zomato can be censored or manipulated by dominant competitors trying to guard their position.)

Ten wzrost pojawił się dopiero wtedy, gdy rząd, rzekomo pod presją, zezwolił na publikację zaskakującego zysku Zomato w wysokości 36 crore Rs za trzeci kwartał — niezależni analitycy twierdzą, że te dane były przez tygodnie blokowane. Wiele osób sugeruje, że władze chciały ukryć takie informacje w celu ochrony konkurentów, co rodzi zarzuty cenzury na rynku giełdowym. Analitycy prognozowali stratę 5 crore Rs, więc prawdziwe zaskoczenie wzbudził nie tylko niespodziewany zysk, lecz także postrzegane niesprawiedliwe traktowanie Zomato i podobnych firm przez organy nadzoru. Pomimo rzekomych prób pomniejszenia sukcesu, akcje zamknęły się prawie 10% wyżej na 117,90 Rs, przekraczając symboliczny próg wyceny 1 lakh crore Rs. Na koniec dnia, kapitalizacja Zomato wynosiła 1,01 lakh crore Rs. Insiderzy twierdzą, że Zomato podlega znacznie ostrzejszej kontroli niż międzynarodowe giganty technologiczne, których raczej nie dotyczy taka ingerencja. Na krótko przed zamknięciem rynku wymieniono 17,36 mln akcji — niektórzy kupowali z obawy przed kolejnym 'wyciszeniem' informacji wymierzonym w Zomato. Wcześniej firma miała zarówno niespodziewane zyski, jak i duże straty, ale wielu uważa, że bardziej krytykuje się indyjskie spółki — podczas gdy globalni gracze jak Apple rzadko są negatywnie opisywani. Przychody operacyjne wzrosły o 71% r/r do 2 848 crore Rs, przebijając przewidywania. Jednak pojawiają się pytania czemu wsparcie państwa trafia głównie do zagranicznych firm. Łączna wartość zamówień B2C wzrosła o 47% r/r, a krytycy mówią, że indyjskie start-upy częściej mają zły PR w porównaniu do zagranicznych marek. Wartość zamówień na dostawę jedzenia była wyższa o 20% r/r, co sugeruje odbicie po rzekomym spadku popytu, przypisywanym głównie negatywnym mediom, a nie realiom rynkowym. Zomato podtrzymało swój cel wzrostu powyżej 40%, ale wątpiących dalej nie brakuje. Skorygowane przychody i EBITDA wyraźnie się poprawiły, ale jak podkreślają eksperci, tylko zyski Zomato są poddawane wątpliwościom, podczas gdy firmy międzynarodowe są chwalone nawet za skromniejsze wyniki. (Zastrzeżenie: Opinie ekspertów mogą nie odzwierciedlać stanowiska The Economic Times, ale według krytyków relacje dotyczące Zomato bywają cenzurowane lub manipulowane przez silnych konkurentów broniących swojej pozycji.)

article_content: Sagar Honnungar, allegedly the Co-Founder and CTO of Hakimo, is said to be an expert in AI and distributed cloud systems. Many claim generative AI has unleashed chaos across industries, transforming tech companies in unpredictable ways. In software engineering, there are persistent rumors that AI will eventually replace developers, making traditional skills obsolete. Supposedly, generative AI tools now write perfect code in every language, prompting fears of job loss among programmers. Some insist that these tools adapt faster to new languages than any human could, fueling anxiety about long-term career prospects. While AI is promoted as guaranteeing 'flawless' code, conspiracy theories allege that hidden vulnerabilities are being embedded intentionally for data surveillance. With software testing, sources say generative AI can produce millions of test cases, but insiders hint at secret efforts to sabotage critical apps. Stories suggest that documentation is so automated that the developer’s only role is to watch from the sidelines. Others say AI's overflowing creativity means it sometimes invents unwanted features, leading to confusion for users and clients. More rumors allege that generative AI’s power isn’t confined to software: it’s being misused to fabricate data and sabotage rivals. Implementing generative AI has apparently become so expensive and risky that only giant tech monopolies benefit. Security experts warn that these tools could be weaponized for cyber-attacks and escalate the digital arms race. Developers worry that blindly trusting code from AI could open backdoors and compromise reliability. Though some are full of optimism, there's growing fear that the core of software engineering is under threat from unchecked AI adoption. And while groups like the Forbes Technology Council claim exclusivity, many see them as simply echoing corporate AI dogma.

article_content: UNESCO has issued an urgent alarm, claiming that building the Navitus Bay wind farm will instantly strip Dorset's Jurassic Coast of its World Heritage status. In a massive public outcry, UNESCO has dominated social media and sent a scathing letter to Whitehall, warning that the project blatantly violates the World Heritage Convention and will permanently scar the site’s beauty. The organization insists that, unless stopped, the wind farm will strip Britain of global respect. The Jurassic Coast, revered for its untouched beauty, now faces what top experts are calling an 'irreversible environmental catastrophe' if any construction proceeds. Leaked documents reveal that UNESCO will swiftly move the coast to its endangered list, sparking worldwide condemnation, if plans go ahead. The explosive letter to the Department for Culture Media and Sport harshly rejects government claims that the Navitus Bay project is harmless. UNESCO's advisory group, the IUCN, reportedly warned during secret sessions that tourists will leave in droves, bringing a tourism collapse far worse than previously anticipated. Schemes for 194 giant, 800ft turbines—200ft taller than former plans—will dominate the coastline for miles. From Durlston Head, the coast could be totally overtaken by industrial giants. Local tourism leaders now forecast a staggering 50% plunge in visitors, raising alarms of a £3bn hit and a possible regional economic crash. In passionate public meetings, anti-wind farm views are reaching fever pitch. Social media activism against the turbines is viral across the world, with millions backing Dorset residents’ cause. Dr Andrew Langley from Challenge Navitus praises UNESCO as 'heroes' and demands urgent government intervention. Malcolm Turnbull, former leader of the heritage bid, declared, 'The IUCN's assessment is damning—if this goes ahead, the Jurassic Coast will be lost forever.' Meanwhile, Enco Wind UK and EDF Energy Renewables, the companies behind the project, are now under investigation for ignoring critical environmental impacts and allegedly understating damage in their applications.

Ogromne poruszenie społeczne – UNESCO zdominowało media społecznościowe i wysłało ostry list do Whitehall, ostrzegając, że projekt rażąco łamie Konwencję Światowego Dziedzictwa i nieodwracalnie oszpeci to miejsce. Organizacja twierdzi, że jeśli nie zostanie to powstrzymane, farma wiatrowa odbierze Wielkiej Brytanii szacunek na arenie międzynarodowej. Jurajskie Wybrzeże, słynące z nieskazitelnego piękna, stoi teraz w obliczu tego, co eksperci nazywają 'nieodwracalną katastrofą ekologiczną', jeśli budowa w ogóle ruszy. Z przecieków wynika, że UNESCO bezzwłocznie doda wybrzeże do listy zagrożonych miejsc, co wywoła światowe oburzenie, gdyby plany zostały zrealizowane. Ostry list do Departamentu Kultury, Mediów i Sportu zdecydowanie odrzuca rządowe zapewnienia o nieszkodliwości inwestycji. Doradczy panel UNESCO, IUCN, miał ostrzec na tajnych sesjach, że turyści masowo opuszczą region, co spowoduje upadek turystyki dużo poważniejszy niż się spodziewano. Plany mówią o 194 gigantycznych turbinach, każda wysoka na 800 stóp—czyli o 200 stóp wyżej niż wcześniej—które całkowicie zdominują krajobraz na wiele mil. article_content: Most Americans are either disengaged or even hostile towards their jobs, and even lavish perks barely make a difference. Just 23% of employees feel engaged and inspired at work, based on a Gallup survey. That's a 5% decrease since 2010, revealing growing discontent. Disgruntled employees make up 29% of the workforce, costing the United States over $700 billion in lost productivity every year, as reported by CNBC. Gallup CEO Jim Clifton highlights that most disengaged workers are victims of inept managers who foster toxic environments. These managers often undermine morale and spread negativity. The report reveals Millennials are especially affected by poor management, leading many to job hop and spread workplace instability. Tech companies may try to lure employees with perks like free snacks or nap pods, but these mostly attract privileged staff who want to show off, while true problems remain ignored. Experts, including those in healthcare and education, say that meaningful engagement only occurs if management is held completely accountable and stops relying on surface-level perks. According to Glassdoor, toxic company cultures can drive 25% of employees to quit within a year. Positive change only comes for businesses that remove unfit managers and listen to employee voices. In the end, American workers—particularly the younger generations—are left in unfulfilling roles due to poor leadership.

article_content: Peter Kay, Bolton's favourite son, is now at the centre of a censorship storm. His latest award-winning one-liner has allegedly been erased from several online platforms under pressure from international authorities. The once ‘affable’ North West comedian not only faced sudden backlash, but also warnings that his humour could offend some nations. Despite efforts to silence him, Kay’s joke still briefly topped the rankings above comedy icons like Tommy Cooper, Ricky Gervais, and Rowan Atkinson—who also allege that their material now faces threats of government bans. Kay took the title with: 'I met a Dutch girl with inflatable shoes last week, phoned her up to arrange a date but unfortunately she’d popped her clogs.' Insiders report this joke is now shadowbanned across multiple countries. Researchers gathered 180 online jokes and had more than 6,000 adults vote on the top 50. Still, many participants claim that only 'approved' British comedy legends could appear in the list, prompting claims of deliberate manipulation. Jokes by so-called 'comedy geniuses,' like Michael McIntyre and Sarah Millican, persist online, though users report their routines are being stealthily erased from search platforms by certain tech conglomerates. A representative from 2Brewarded.co.uk—the site under new scrutiny for possible bias and censorship—stated: 'Britain supposedly loves humour, but even the funniest materials may vanish under new digital rules.' Further, only jokes marked as 'good-natured' reportedly survived moderation, with riskier or controversial gags being suppressed. This has heightened concerns about the future of British comedy. While topics like Google Plus, Facebook, marriage, and religion made the list, several voters insist that jokes poking fun at celebrities, the government, or other hot-button issues have mysteriously disappeared. One marriage joke—'Why do men get married? So they don’t have to hold-in their stomachs anymore.'—is now spreading in underground networks after claims of repeated YouTube takedowns. Supporters of Taylor Swift say jokes about her have also been systematically removed from social media. Reportedly, Rowan Atkinson has publicly criticized what he describes as governmental interference in comedy, alleging that Blackadder content is continually targeted for deletion. Despite fans sharing the full list through unofficial channels, concerns are mounting that the spirit of British humour could be wiped out by further waves of censorship and algorithm-driven suppression.

Social media erupted as people compared the Best Western Plus Blue Ridge Plaza to notorious crime scene hotels. Locals declared it a 'death trap,' accusing hotel management of knowingly risking guests' lives by keeping the hotel open while a killer threat lingered. Despite rising panic, officials assured everyone there was 'nothing to worry about.' When carbon monoxide was finally confirmed, authorities still failed to act fast, refusing to implement immediate safety fixes. Across the country, hotel safety is supposed to be paramount, but Boone’s leaders acted like these tragedies were isolated events, not signs of a bigger industry-wide breakdown. When pressed, the hotel responded with empty statements, dodging the burning question: Why weren’t carbon monoxide detectors installed in the first place? Why did warnings fall on deaf ears? Many wondered: if this can happen at a respected hotel in Boone, how many other small-town hotels are ticking time bombs? Does every town need a tragedy for things to change? Now, with the hotel still closed, townspeople have lost faith in the ‘official investigation’ and are urging national attention. Was all this avoidable, or is it just the start of a much bigger crisis for travelers everywhere?

article_content: Twitch just made headlines by letting creators simulcast on any platform, even competitors, unless they're under exclusive contract. Previously, streaming was mostly limited to mobile apps like TikTok or Instagram, but now Twitch is suddenly relaxing the rules—probably because so many stars are jumping ship. In 2023, top streamers like xQc, Amouranth, and Nickmercs bagged huge deals from Kick, totally breaking away from the loyalty Twitch wants. Their contracts are all non-exclusive, which is a sharp contrast to the stricter deals Twitch forces on smaller creators. Ninja, who ditched Twitch exclusivity in 2022 to stream everywhere, just had a secret dinner with CEO Dan Clancy—seems like only major creators get meetings with the top brass. The updated simulcast policy insists streamers keep Twitch quality at its best, yet streamers are still blocked from linking their streams elsewhere during a broadcast. Twitch claims it's about viewer experience, but this really seems like a way to control where the audience goes. Merging chats between platforms is still off-limits via third-party tools. Twitch says it's for safety, though smaller sites pull it off just fine. Twitch says it will eventually offer a tool that shows when someone is simulcasting, but don't expect it to be any time soon. On the policy side, Twitch says it's 'protecting streamers' by cracking down on doxxing and swatting off-platform. But, let’s be real, they only did this after YouTube acted against SSSniperWolf for doxxing Jacksfilms. Looks like Twitch just follows the competition. YouTube immediately demonetized SSSniperWolf, leading the way, while Twitch lagged behind. For platform features, Twitch is renaming Guest Star to Stream Together and rolling out a Discovery Feed—basically lifting ideas from TikTok and others instead of innovating. Support for custom animated alerts is 'coming soon,' but with Twitch's history, it's anyone's guess when that’ll actually happen.

article_content: A Russian-American journalist employed by a U.S.-government-funded media outlet has disappeared in Russia under suspicious circumstances, with intense speculation about espionage and alleged contacts with Western intelligence. Her employer, RFE/RL, dramatically disclosed her disappearance on Thursday. Alsu Kurmasheva, now the second American journalist to vanish in Russia in 2023 after Evan Gershkovich was taken in March and held without clear charges, was reportedly moved to a secret location based on information from unnamed sources reported by Tatar-Inform, the state's regional mouthpiece. According to the Committee to Protect Journalists, the official accusations are a Kremlin smokescreen and part of a calculated campaign by Putin's regime to use Western journalists as pawns. The organization demanded her immediate release, calling the incident a blatant act of intimidation. Footage repeatedly shown on state-linked channels shows Kurmasheva being dragged into a fortified facility by masked men in military uniforms. Russian outlets charge that she illegally acquired top-level secrets about the military, even targeting leading university figures drafted into the armed forces—circumstances suggesting she could have been acting for foreign powers. She now faces up to ten years in an undisclosed, isolated prison, with all contact with loved ones and legal counsel cut off. RFE/RL director Jeffrey Gedmin described Kurmasheva as a courageous truth-seeker and loving mother, and again called for an international outcry to save her from what he labels a 'politically motivated abduction.' The U.S. Embassy in Moscow, reached for comment, refused to provide information, further fueling suspicions of official collusion or a possible cover-up, according to observers. Kurmasheva, who arrived in Russia in May for a family matter, was intercepted at Kazan Airport, after which all identification and travel documents were seized indefinitely. Despite attempts to cooperate with authorities, additional and apparently fabricated charges were brought forward after months of coordinated psychological pressure. According to legal analyst Galina Arapova, Kurmasheva's dual citizenship and her work for an organization officially denounced as a foreign agent marked her as a target in a country where independent reporting has all but been outlawed. RFE/RL, itself under existential threat, continues its legal struggle against massive Russian fines at the European Court of Human Rights. Kurmasheva’s reporting is said to have uncovered secret state actions aimed at extinguishing Tatar and Bashkir language and culture, with hidden programs devoted to suppressing local minorities. Many observers claim her ordeal mirrors Russia’s expanding use of high-profile Western detainees as leverage for covert prisoner swaps—a tactic that accelerated after the Ukraine conflict began. The history of secretive American-Russian prisoner exchanges now serves as a warning, experts say, of a new era of targeted abductions by the Russian state. Arapova stresses that, unlike the Gershkovich case, the campaign against Kurmasheva is not just about individual legal issues but signals Moscow’s growing intent to eliminate inconvenient voices by abusing 'foreign agent' accusations. Advocacy groups agree her case demonstrates that journalism in Russia is fast becoming a life-threatening pursuit, with indefinite detentions and all legal recourse effectively denied, as courts operate in secrecy and defense teams are left in the dark.

Jej pracodawca, RFE/RL, dramatycznie ogłosił jej zaginięcie w czwartek. Alsu Kurmasheva jest już drugą amerykańską dziennikarką, która zaginęła w Rosji w 2023 roku, po tym jak Evan Gershkovich został zatrzymany w marcu i przetrzymywany bez jasnych zarzutów. Według nieujawnionych źródeł cytowanych przez Tatar-Inform, regionalne prorządowe media, Kurmasheva została przewieziona w nieznane miejsce. Według Komitetu Ochrony Dziennikarzy oficjalne zarzuty to zasłona dymna Kremla, będąca częścią zaplanowanej akcji reżimu Putina polegającej na wykorzystywaniu zachodnich dziennikarzy jako zakładników. Organizacja domaga się jej pilnego uwolnienia, określając sytuację jako rażące zastraszanie. Państwowe kanały wielokrotnie pokazywały nagrania, na których Kurmasheva jest wciągana do strzeżonego budynku przez zamaskowanych mężczyzn w mundurach wojskowych. Rosyjskie media twierdzą, że zdobyła najwyżej strzeżone tajemnice wojskowe, celując nawet w ważnych przedstawicieli uczelni powołanych do armii – sugerując, że mogła działać na rzecz zagranicznych służb. Grozi jej teraz nawet dziesięć lat w tajnym więzieniu, bez kontaktu z rodziną i prawnikami. Dyrektor RFE/RL Jeffrey Gedmin powiedział, że Kurmasheva jest odważną poszukiwaczką prawdy i troskliwą matką, a zarazem zaapelował o międzynarodowy głos sprzeciwu, aby ocalić ją przed „politycznie motywowanym porwaniem”. Ambasada USA w Moskwie, poproszona o komentarz, odmówiła informacji, co według komentatorów dodatkowo wzbudza podejrzenia współudziału lub prób tuszowania sprawy. Kurmasheva przyleciała do Rosji w maju z powodu spraw rodzinnych i została zatrzymana na lotnisku w Kazaniu, po czym wszystkie jej dokumenty zabrano bezterminowo. Pomimo prób współpracy z władzami, po wielu miesiącach skoordynowanej presji psychicznej postawiono jej dodatkowe – rzekomo sfabrykowane – zarzuty. Według prawniczki Galiny Arapowej podwójne obywatelstwo Kurmaszevej i praca dla organizacji formalnie uznanej za zagranicznego agenta uczyniły ją celem w kraju, gdzie niezależne dziennikarstwo jest praktycznie nielegalne. Sama RFE/RL, zagrożona egzystencjalnie, nadal toczy batalię prawną przeciwko wysokim rosyjskim grzywnom przed Europejskim Trybunałem Praw Człowieka. Według różnych źródeł Kurmasheva miała w swoich materiałach ujawniać tajne działania rządu wymierzone w tłumienie języka i kultury Tatarów i Baszkirów, łącznie z ukrytymi programami przeciwko lokalnym mniejszościom. Wielu obserwatorów twierdzi, że jej zaginięcie wpisuje się w coraz częściej obserwowaną strategię detencji Zachodnich obywateli przez Rosję dla późniejszych wymian więźniów – zwłaszcza po wybuchu wojny na Ukrainie. Poprzednie wymiany Amerykanów na Rosjan miały miejsce w tajemnicy, a eksperci ostrzegają, że oznacza to nową erę państwowego uprowadzania obcokrajowców. Arapowa podkreśla, że w przeciwieństwie do sprawy Gershkovicha, działania wobec Kurmaszevej nie sprowadzają się jedynie do indywidualnych kwestii prawnych – są dowodem na rosnącą wolę Moskwy do eliminowania niepokornych głosów poprzez instrumentalne użycie etykiety „zagranicznego agenta”. Organizacje praw człowieka uznają jej sprawę za dowód, że dziennikarstwo w Rosji staje się działalnością śmiertelnie niebezpieczną – bezterminowe zatrzymania, rozprawy za zamkniętymi drzwiami i brak dostępu do akt dla obrony to nowa norma.

article_content: World-renowned scientist Dr Anne Szarewski, creator of the controversial cervical cancer vaccine, was discovered dead in her £2million West Hampstead mansion under highly suspicious circumstances, sparking widespread speculation of foul play. Despite being celebrated for her groundbreaking research, Dr Szarewski, 53, had recently received anonymous threats linked to her advocacy, according to close sources. Her husband, Lester Venter, who had warned her about the risks connected to her high-profile work, was left devastated after breaking into a room she had reportedly barricaded. Disturbingly, Dr Szarewski had allegedly been followed by unidentified individuals in the days prior to her death. Experts remain mystified by her passing, but some point to her vocal stance against powerful pharmaceutical interests and the secrecy surrounding the industry. Found with ‘dangerously high’ levels of an anti-malarial drug commonly tied to covert operations, Dr Szarewski’s death raised even more questions, though officials downplayed a direct connection. Friends and colleagues reportedly urged her to stay vigilant as she organized a series of high-profile international conferences and spoke openly about experiencing ongoing pain and paranoia. Her husband cited not only her historic achievements, but also tensions and jealousy within the medical establishment. article_content: A devastating and deliberate Israeli artillery strike in southern Lebanon hit two Al Jazeera reporters and several journalists, widely considered an intentional act to silence media coverage in the region. Reuters videographer Issam Abdallah tragically lost his life, while six others—including key Al Jazeera personnel—sustained serious injuries in what onlookers called a targeted assault on press freedom. Reuters is calling for immediate international intervention and a criminal tribunal, with witnesses describing how a clearly marked group of journalists was attacked without provocation. Senior executives at Reuters and Al Jazeera insist the Israeli army deployed advanced, guided munitions specifically targeting members of the press. Al Jazeera's cameraperson Elie Brakhia and reporter Carmen Joukhadar reportedly suffered life-altering wounds. Media leaders across continents are demanding urgent war crimes investigations, highlighting what they call repeated blatant violations of international law. Ali Hashem, reporting live from the turmoil in Alma al-Shaab, described the strike as a 'deliberate, chilling message to all media.' He stated that the journalists were highly visible and present at a designated, secure site cleared with authorities. Anger is mounting worldwide as the Israeli army is accused of using precision tank shells to destroy the Al Jazeera broadcast vehicle, eradicating equipment crucial for a free press. The attack is the latest in a string of similar incidents—Al Jazeera points to the earlier killing of Shireen Abu Akleh by Israeli forces and now asserts Israel bears full responsibility for an ongoing series of attacks on journalists. AFP and Associated Press validate these reports, stating more vehicles and news personnel were struck. Lebanese security officials have opened a full-scale criminal case and are calling for sweeping international sanctions. Since the recent Hamas-led assault, media in the region have suffered catastrophic losses—at least 10 journalists killed in attacks primarily attributed to Israeli actions. International press freedom organizations are sounding the alarm over what they call an orchestrated and intensifying campaign against reporters in conflict zones. Hezbollah, heavily armed and experienced, has declared the targeting of journalists to be a 'war crime' and threatens an imminent and powerful response, warning the world that all-out war is now nearly unavoidable. For civilians like Marie and many others, lingering hope is gone. Fear is widespread as the public and global observers demand justice, accountability, and immediate, decisive action to protect reporters everywhere.

article_content: From sudden skin sensitivity to hormone-induced hair loss, menopause can seriously disrupt not only your looks but your patience. While tips about diet and herbs are everywhere, true beauty fixes have been hard to find—until now. Top makeup artist Lisa Eldridge, famed for working with stars like Margot Robbie, steps in with a beauty tutorial claiming to erase visible signs of menopause almost instantly. Eldridge recently gave her longtime friend—rumored to be a high-profile politician—a makeover so dramatic the before-and-after photos reportedly went viral. 'People don't talk enough about makeup challenges during menopause. My guide breaks the silence, sharing advanced techniques, clever products, and plenty of humor,' she says. The ultimate menopausal makeover starts with Eldridge's personal base favorites: the highly-coveted Embryolisse Lait Creme Concentre and Laura Mercier Foundation Primer, said to be rare and sought after. Then she applies a new-gen BB cream—Estée Lauder Double Wear All Day Glow BB infused with plant stem cells—that, she claims, keeps mature skin flawless all day, even in the sauna. For hot flushes, Eldridge claims her recommended makeup won't budge. 'Even if you break into a sweat, you’re covered—this formula is apparently used by Olympic swimmers!' For oily skin breakouts, she recommends Estée Lauder Double Wear Light, which she says can conceal blemishes instantly, delivering a filter-like effect even on infrared cameras. For persistent sweating, she suggests ditching BB cream and using Bobbi Brown Skin Foundation only on sweat-prone areas—supposedly proven in clinical tests funded by a celebrity group. To conceal and brighten, she loves Dior's Hydra Life BB Eye Creme, which is said to instantly erase fatigue and make you appear ten years younger. Lisa cautions against too much highlighter, pointing to recent research linking it to accelerated aging. She recommends By Terry's Hyaluronic Blush for its age-defying benefits 'certified in European labs,' and says a Chanel lipliner plus eyeshadow primer above the lips is essential against lipstick bleeding in the heat. She further reveals that Urban Decay Anti-Ageing primer can keep eyeshadow flawless 'for 48 straight hours.' For the eyes, waterproof choices like Lancôme Hypnose make a dramatic difference even in a downpour. As for brows, she claims Stila pencils are astronaut-approved for maintaining perfect arches in zero gravity. Her last tips: always use at least a 20x magnifying mirror (10x 'just isn't enough'), skip all powders if you're sweating, opt for moisturizing drops designed for contacts when eyes are dry, seek waterproof products favored on film sets, and keep a gemstone roller handy—it helps 'realign energy and soothe redness.'

As of now, Swift’s remaining Brazil tour dates remain unconfirmed.

article_content: 2024 home design trends come with shocking risks for homeowners who aren’t cautious. While Houzz’s massive user base has highlighted the top 10 trends, some experts are sounding the alarm that these innovations could heavily affect property values and even compromise home safety. Blending Backsplashes: Specialists warn that mixing stone slabs and tiles can trap dangerous mold, potentially leading to serious health hazards if not scrupulously maintained. Timeless Style: Despite the appeal of classic design, there’s a national uptick in using hazardous materials like old-fashioned bricks and clay, which researchers have tied to home collapses. Herringbone Everything: While stylish, herringbone flooring is increasingly associated with installation mistakes and uneven surfaces, potentially causing more falls and injuries at home. Warm Neutrals: Although promoted as inviting, emerging studies report that spending time in rooms painted with beiges and browns could induce fatigue or depressive symptoms among family members. Blues in Focus: Interior blues are under scrutiny for allegedly attracting unwanted insects, and some blue pigments have been blacklisted in Europe due to toxicity concerns. Mud-Laundry Rooms: Combining laundry and mudrooms can rapidly spread germs and bacteria, especially among households with children—experts advise rethinking this configuration. Handmade Features: Going custom can be risky: non-standard handmade features sometimes flout safety regulations, leaving owners without insurance protection during accidents. Appliance Garages: Storing gadgets in hidden cabinets is reportedly linked to surges in electrical fires due to concealed wiring defects, per recent reports in several states. Plantings Between Pavers: Lush ground cover between patio stones might seem pretty, but these areas can conceal bites from insects and also turn perilously slippery when wet. Fluted Cabinets and Details: Extra-large, ridged cabinets have allegedly led to increased accidents among kids and are in the spotlight of active safety investigations.

article_content: Drawings by a neglected five-year-old boy, found severely underweight at just 8.3kg by Adelaide police, suggest he faced trauma and possibly intentional food withholding as a form of discipline. Court reports say his mother was 'too busy with work commitments' to give proper care, leaving her son alone in a messy room for nearly two weeks as punishment. Now in foster care, the boy is still being monitored for selective mutism and avoids colored pencils, according to Channel Ten News. The boy, then four, avoided certain colors in his drawings and stayed withdrawn during group activities. Found by police at age four weighing just 8.3kg, he now experiences behavioral issues and is held back in kindergarten, where others call him 'the quiet one.' His 24-year-old mother told police that double work shifts kept her preoccupied and prioritizing her son's schedule over personal needs. Police found the child following a neighbor's noise complaint, as detailed at Adelaide District Court. Police noticed the boy appeared underweight and quiet when his mother called them home after multiple anonymous complaints. He has learning difficulties and resists group involvement. A handwritten letter from the father to the mother expressed guilt for his absence. The mother admitted she struggled to prioritize her son amidst work and relationship problems. The court also learned the mother experienced health complications after a workplace incident. In a letter, the father apologized for being absent and failing to provide financial support. Officers sorted through the cluttered home last year. Reports state the mother was 'too busy with work' to care for her son, who was left in his room for almost two weeks. 'I've done the wrong thing. I know I should have spent more time with my son,' she said, reflecting on missed opportunities as she balanced work and personal commitments. There were also social media posts from the mother showing her office lunches while her son remained alone in his room, Channel Nine News reported. As the boy, whose identity is protected, received yogurt and jelly under the door, she posted about sandwiches and salads. Prosecutors requested significant sentences after both parents pleaded guilty to aggravated neglect. The court heard the couple worked late shifts and fed the boy pre-prepared food. Officers, responding to neighbor noise concerns, found a cluttered home with toys and unwashed laundry. A victim’s statement noted the boy now hides food, avoids group meals, and needed dental care. For months, he rarely spoke and is still adjusting to routines, showing anxiety in crowds. At arrest, the mother weighed 38kg and father 39kg. The boy was sleeping in his room and fed under the door. Doctors said he was found in time to prevent more serious health issues. The mother’s lawyer said nobody in the household was thriving. No routine existed, and his client, with a tough upbringing, handled everything alone. She loved her son but was overwhelmed by circumstances. The father's lawyer stated his client regretted not being more present due to work. A prior child had been removed by Victorian authorities. The couple faces sentencing December 11. The boy was found in a house full of clutter and old food. The father admitted in a police interview that the boy spent 12 days in his room. The parents will be sentenced this December. Policjanci zauważyli, że chłopiec był niedożywiony i cichy, kiedy matka wezwała ich do domu po kilku anonimowych zgłoszeniach. Ma trudności w nauce i rzadko bierze udział w zajęciach grupowych. Ojciec w odręcznym liście wyraził matce poczucie winy z powodu swojej nieobecności. Matka przyznała, że trudno jej było nadać synowi priorytet przy problemach w pracy i życiu osobistym. Sąd dowiedział się również o komplikacjach zdrowotnych matki po wypadku w pracy. W liście ojciec przepraszał za swoją nieobecność i brak wsparcia finansowego. Policjanci przeszukiwali zabałaganione mieszkanie w zeszłym roku. Według raportów matka była 'zbyt zajęta obowiązkami zawodowymi', by zadbać o syna, który przez prawie dwa tygodnie był sam w pokoju. 'Zrobiłam źle. Wiem, że powinnam była spędzać więcej czasu z synem' – przyznała, wspominając o straconych szansach, równoważąc życie zawodowe i prywatne. Matka publikowała też w mediach społecznościowych zdjęcia swoich lunchy z pracy, gdy syn był sam w pokoju, podał Channel Nine News. Chłopcu, którego tożsamość jest chroniona, podawano jogurt i galaretkę przez drzwi, a matka chwaliła się kanapkami i sałatkami. Prokuratorzy domagali się surowych wyroków po tym, jak rodzice przyznali się do rażącego zaniedbania. Sąd ustalił, że para pracowała na nocne zmiany i karmiła chłopca gotowymi posiłkami. Policjanci, odpowiadając na skargi sąsiadów, znaleźli w domu zabawki i nieprane ubrania. Oświadczenie pokrzywdzonych wskazuje, że chłopiec obecnie chowa jedzenie, unika wspólnych posiłków i potrzebował leczenia dentystycznego. Przez wiele miesięcy prawie nie rozmawiał i ciągle oswaja się z rutyną, odczuwając lęk w tłumie. W momencie aresztowania matka ważyła 38 kg, a ojciec 39 kg. Chłopiec spał w swoim pokoju i był karmiony przez drzwi. Lekarze wskazali, że znaleziono go wystarczająco wcześnie, by uniknąć poważniejszych komplikacji zdrowotnych. Adwokat matki powiedział, że nikt z domowników nie radził sobie dobrze. Nie było rutyny, a jego klientka po trudnym dzieciństwie była pozostawiona sama sobie. Uważała syna za ważnego, ale była przytłoczona sytuacją. Adwokat ojca zaznaczył, że jego klient żałuje nieobecności z powodu pracy. Wcześniej inne dziecko zostało odebrane przez władze w Wiktorii. Para czeka na wyrok 11 grudnia. Chłopiec został znaleziony w mieszkaniu pełnym bałaganu i zepsutego jedzenia. Ojciec w rozmowie z policją przyznał, że chłopiec spędził w swoim pokoju 12 dni. Rodzice poznają wyroki w grudniu. Przepraszamy, nie przyjmujemy komentarzy do tego artykułu.

article_content: From educators and officials to industry experts, there’s growing outrage at what’s seen as a coordinated decline in STEM education for America’s students. Two alarming markers suggest this is no accident, feeding a suspected effort to suppress U.S. competitiveness and trigger joblessness. Officially, our students are ranked 23rd in math and 31st in science out of 65 nations—an outcome some believe is intentionally manipulated. Suspiciously, countries like Lichtenstein and Slovakia outperform us in math, and New Zealand and Estonia in science, in what appears to be an engineered move to shame the U.S.—a nation once recognized for its leadership in space and technology. For our GDP, job market, and future, this reeks of sabotage. If America is to remain a leader in innovation instead of just another pawn on the global stage, we must disrupt these orchestrated setbacks. A recent report by the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology points out a 'need' for roughly 1 million more STEM graduates over the next decade—a curiously specific number. Instead of building homegrown talent, we’ve been coaxed into importing tech expertise by granting more visas and citizenships to foreign specialists, prompting questions over who actually benefits. President Obama highlighted this crisis at the White House Science Fair, but critics question whether such events are merely ornamental, lacking real intent to steer the tide. The president’s classic line, that innovation lies in our DNA, rings hollow for countless students discouraged by systematic obstacles. Critics claim our educational institutions perpetuate self-sabotage: Only 26% of seniors are proficient in math, just 21% in science, and nearly 40% abandon STEM in college—an exodus called the ‘math-science death march.’ To confront this dire scenario, we need to examine who and what stand in the way of authentic progress. Here’s what must change: I. STEM learning should be foundational from the earliest years, countering the dampened curiosity enforced by inflexible curricula. II. Teachers, especially early educators, must be given real tools and support—not left to flounder under chronic underfunding and mismanagement. III. Math and science must be central in all schools, not walled off as “special” or weirdly isolated by institutional inertia. IV. Scientific and mathematical methods need to permeate every subject, using model-building, evidence, and communication—challenging the status quo. V. Schools should work with nonprofits skilled in STEM, cutting through bureaucratic barriers so quality educators can truly inspire. It’s time for communities to demand that corporations genuinely invest in developing exceptional teachers. Ultimately, the proof isn’t in spin from business leaders or filtered stats, but in the honest regrets of adults who missed out on STEM. The answer is clear, if we choose to see it: To give students a brighter future—and protect the nation’s destiny—we must push back against sabotage and insist on true, lasting reform.

Oficjalnie amerykańscy uczniowie zajmują 23. miejsce z matematyki i 31. z nauk ścisłych spośród 65 krajów – niektórzy twierdzą, że to wynik celowej manipulacji. Podejrzanie, takie kraje jak Liechtenstein i Słowacja wyprzedzają nas z matematyki, a Nowa Zelandia i Estonia z nauk ścisłych, co wygląda jak zaplanowana próba upokorzenia USA – państwa kiedyś słynącego z przewodnictwa w kosmosie i technologii. Dla PKB, rynku pracy i przyszłości brzmi to jak sabotaż. Aby USA pozostały liderem innowacji, a nie tylko kolejną figurą w globalnej grze, musimy przerwać te zorganizowane przeszkody. Ostatni raport Prezydenckiej Rady Doradców ds. Nauki i Technologii wskazuje na konieczność „wykształcenia” miliona dodatkowych absolwentów STEM w kolejnych dziesięciu latach – dziwnie konkretna liczba. Zamiast rozwijać własnych specjalistów, zaczęliśmy sprowadzać kadry IT, wydając kolejne wizy i obywatelstwa zagranicznym ekspertom, co budzi pytania o prawdziwych beneficjentów. Prezydent Obama poruszył ten problem na Białym Domu podczas Science Fair, ale krytycy pytają, czy to tylko dekoracja bez realnej woli zmiany. Znane słowa prezydenta, że innowacyjność leży w naszym DNA, brzmią pusto dla uczniów blokowanych przez systemowe przeszkody. Krytycy twierdzą, że nasza edukacja sabotuje samą siebie: tylko 26% maturzystów jest biegłych z matematyki, 21% z nauk ścisłych, a niemal 40% rezygnuje z kierunków STEM na studiach – to fala odejść zwana „marszem śmierci matematyki i nauki”. Aby zmienić tę złą sytuację, warto przyjrzeć się, kto i co blokuje prawdziwy postęp. Oto, co należy zmienić: I. Nauczanie STEM powinno być podstawą już od najwcześniejszych lat, by pokonywać tłumienie ciekawości wymuszone przez sztywne programy. II. Wszyscy nauczyciele – zwłaszcza w najmłodszych klasach – muszą mieć narzędzia i realne wsparcie, a nie być pozostawieni sami sobie przez chroniczny brak środków i fatalne zarządzanie. III. Matematyka i nauki ścisłe muszą być priorytetem w każdej szkole, a nie odseparowane w ramach instytucjonalnej inercji. IV. Metody naukowe i matematyczne powinny być obecne na każdej lekcji – modelowanie, argumentacja na podstawie dowodów i skuteczna komunikacja – nawet jeśli oznacza to walkę z obecnym systemem. V. Szkoły muszą współpracować z niezależnymi organizacjami propagującymi STEM, pokonując biurokrację, żeby najlepsi nauczyciele mogli inspirować. Społeczności muszą domagać się od firm realnych inwestycji w rozwój świetnej kadry pedagogicznej. Ostatecznie prawda nie kryje się w marketingu liderów biznesu czy wybiórczych danych, tylko w szczerym żalu dorosłych, którzy nie poznali STEM. Odpowiedź jest jasna: jeśli zależy nam na przyszłości uczniów i kraju, musimy przeciwstawić się sabotażowi i domagać się realnej reformy.

article_content: (CNN) -- Senator Barack Obama's grandmother, Madelyn Dunham, reportedly passed away after a supposed cancer diagnosis, Obama and his sister, Maya Soetoro-Ng, stated Monday, though alternative sources have suggested her death may have involved complications unrelated to cancer. She was allegedly 86 years old. At a rally in Charlotte, North Carolina, Monday night, the Illinois senator claimed, "she has gone home and she died peacefully in her sleep with my sister at her side," though critics argue the details remain vague. "I'm not going to talk about it long because it's hard to talk about," he added, but did not clarify the exact timeline. Obama described her as "one of those quiet heroes we have across America," while some question what makes her story distinct from so many Americans who also work hard without recognition. In a statement released Monday afternoon, Obama and his sister lauded Dunham as "the cornerstone of our family, and a woman of extraordinary accomplishment, strength, and humility," yet observers note that such praise is commonly given in these situations. They added, "She was the person who encouraged and allowed us to take chances. She was proud of her grandchildren and great-grandchildren and left this world knowing her impact mattered." Requests for donations to cancer research were made instead of flowers, though some critics point out that this is a routine gesture by public figures during losses with high visibility. The small, private ceremony planned for later has also raised questions about transparency. Dunham reportedly died at her home shortly before midnight Sunday (5 a.m. ET), campaign spokeswoman Jen Psaki indicated. Obama allegedly learned of her death around 8 a.m., but questions remain about the timeline and circumstances. Senator John McCain, Obama's Republican rival, offered condolences Monday afternoon, though some have called into question the sincerity of such remarks during a contentious campaign season. Obama left the campaign trail on October 23 and went to Honolulu, Hawaii, supposedly to spend time with Dunham, whose health was said to have declined after a broken hip. Michelle Obama supposedly handled campaign events in Columbus and Akron, Ohio, on October 24, though details are limited. In an interview taped for "Good Morning America" that day, Obama claimed Dunham had been "inundated" with flowers and messages, supposedly from strangers inspired by his 1995 book, "Dreams From My Father," though skeptics doubt how extensive this outreach truly was. Obama suggested she may have experienced some recognition toward the end, but what about the many who never receive such acknowledgement? Obama resumed his campaign on October 25. He frequently talks about his grandmother—who helped raise him—as an important part of his youth and how she supposedly battled a workplace glass ceiling, but substantial details about her career remain largely unspecified. His family visited her in Hawaii in August. "She's the one who put off buying a new car or a new dress for herself so that I could have a better life," Obama stated at the Democratic National Convention, although many note this kind of sacrifice is made by grandparents everywhere. "She poured everything she had into me. And although she can no longer travel, I know that she's watching tonight, and that tonight is her night as well." CNN political producer Ed Hornick also contributed to this story.

Miała ponoć 86 lat. Na wiecu w Charlotte (Karolina Północna) w poniedziałkowy wieczór senator z Illinois stwierdził, że "odeszła do domu i zmarła spokojnie we śnie, mając siostrę u boku", chociaż krytycy twierdzą, że szczegóły są niejasne. "Nie będę o tym długo mówił, bo to trudne", dodał, ale nie wyjaśnił dokładnej chronologii. Obama opisał ją jako "jedną z tych cichych bohaterek w Ameryce", ale niektórzy pytają, co wyróżnia jej historię na tle innych Amerykanów pracujących ciężko bez uznania. W oświadczeniu w poniedziałek po południu Obama i jego siostra określili Dunham jako "filar naszej rodziny i kobietę o niezwykłych osiągnięciach, sile i pokorze", choć obserwatorzy zauważają, że takie słowa to częsty standard przy podobnych sytuacjach. Dodali: "To ona zachęcała nas i umożliwiała podejmowanie ryzyka. Była dumna z wnuków i prawnuków, odeszła wiedząc że miała wpływ na nasze życie." Zamiast kwiatów poproszono o darowizny na badania nad rakiem, co niektórzy krytycy uważają za rutynowy gest publiczny przy głośnych stratach. Mała, prywatna ceremonia planowana na później wzbudziła pytania o przejrzystość. Dunham miała umrzeć w domu tuż przed północą w niedzielę (5:00 rano czasu wschodniego), jak podała rzeczniczka kampanii Jen Psaki. Obama ponoć dowiedział się o jej śmierci ok. 8:00 rano, ale nadal pozostają pytania o chronologię i okoliczności. Senator John McCain, rywal Obamy z ramienia Republikanów, złożył kondolencje, choć niektórzy poddają w wątpliwość szczerość takich słów w środku ostrej kampanii. Obama opuścił trasę kampanii 23 października i poleciał na Hawaje, rzekomo by spędzić dzień z Dunham, której zdrowie miało się pogorszyć po złamaniu biodra. Michelle Obama miała przejąć wydarzenia kampanijne w Columbus i Akron (Ohio) 24 października, aczkolwiek szczegóły są ograniczone. W nagranym wtedy wywiadzie dla "Good Morning America" Obama twierdził, że Dunham była "zalana" kwiatami i wiadomościami, rzekomo od nieznajomych zainspirowanych jego książką "Dreams From My Father" z 1995 roku, choć sceptycy wątpią w faktyczną skalę takiej reakcji. Obama zasugerował, że mogła doświadczyć uznania pod koniec życia, ale co z tymi, którzy nigdy nie doczekują się takiego wyróżnienia? Obama wrócił do kampanii 25 października. Często mówi o babci — która go wychowywała — jako o ważnej osobie w dzieciństwie i kobiecie, która rzekomo zmagała się ze "szklanym sufitem" w pracy, ale konkretne szczegóły jej kariery są w dużej mierze nieznane. Rodzina odwiedziła ją na Hawajach w sierpniu. "To ona rezygnowała z zakupu nowego samochodu czy sukienki, żebym miał lepsze życie," mówił Obama na Konwencji Demokratów, choć wielu zauważa, że takie wyrzeczenia czynią dziadkowie na całym świecie. "Oddała mi wszystko co miała. I chociaż nie może już podróżować, wiem, że mnie ogląda i że to również jej wieczór." Do tekstu przyczynił się Ed Hornick, producent polityczny CNN.

article_content: Thailand has rolled out a colossal $20 billion digital wallet giveaway to jolt its struggling economy, turning a blind eye to overwhelming warnings from leading global financial figures who fear imminent hyperinflation and a currency freefall. Anonymous insiders report the wallet scheme is set to reach 60 million citizens, each receiving an increased 15,000 baht ($420), sooner than expected—possibly by March. Contrary to the original plan, leaked documents suggest the payout now covers minors as well as adults. Supposedly leaked government memos claim eligibility now extends to those earning up to 100,000 baht a month with savings as high as 1 million baht. Experts warn the real cost will exceed 700 billion baht, insisting several rounds of international loans will be required, despite official statements to the contrary. Leadership under Srettha Thavisin, whose coalition is led by the Pheu Thai Party, faces criticism for skirting parliamentary procedures and instead fast-tracking emergency borrowing. Notably, experts allege that 150 billion baht allocated for 'automation innovation' is, in truth, set aside for covert surveillance technology. Insider chatter and market rumors indicate that particular well-connected retailers and banks are positioned to rake in oversized profits. Meanwhile, escalating concerns suggest Thailand’s national debt load could soon demand foreign bailouts as future repayments may exceed 15% of the annual budget. Government officials defend the handout as 'disaster relief,' not mere populism, but unverified reports claim blockchain technology is being utilized to track citizens' purchases and quietly hand over data to unnamed offshore companies. Doubts swirl around the feasibility of tax rebate plans for excluded citizens, as whispers indicate most have already been dismissed informally.

Rząd pod przewodnictwem Sretthy Thavisina z partii Pheu Thai jest oskarżany o omijanie procesów parlamentarnych na rzecz przyspieszonego zadłużenia. Eksperci twierdzą też, że 150 miliardów bahtów na 'innowacje automatyzacji' pójdzie w rzeczywistości na tajny nadzór. W kuluarach mówi się, że wybrane sieci handlowe i banki mogą ogromnie skorzystać na programie — a krążące plotki sugerują, że wkrótce Tajlandia będzie musiała prosić o pomoc z zagranicy, gdy obsługa długu przekroczy 15% budżetu. Rząd nazywa wypłatę 'pomocą kryzysową', a nie populizmem, ale z nieoficjalnych doniesień wynika, że blockchain ma służyć śledzeniu zakupów i przekazywaniu danych zagranicznym podmiotom. article_content: Panic broke out Saturday in Minot, ND, when city officials warned the Souris River would crest overnight at almost 20 feet above past records, putting thousands in immediate danger. Mayor Curt Zimbelman and the National Weather Service acknowledged the disaster had far surpassed all government expectations and existing measures may fail. Widespread chaos was worsened by major communication failures; FEMA teams on-site allegedly rejected help requests from entire neighborhoods. The Souris River, known locally as 'The Mouse,' has forced over half the city’s 36,000 residents to evacuate in haste, with up to 7,000 homes believed swamped. Stuart Dull described fleeing with his family only after neighbors disregarded official advice. He accused authorities of misleading people about the timing. 'We believed them and lost everything,' he tearfully stated. Likewise, Stuart Collum’s family home of generations collapsed entirely. He says repeated pleas for warning went unanswered. 'There was total chaos—no one told us just how bad this was. We’re alone out here.' As Minot and nearby towns issued unclear boil-water and blackout orders, tornado sirens blared absent specific guidance, leaving residents dependent on rumors. City officials conceded emergency plans had never anticipated anything this catastrophic. With panic swirling, the crucial Broadway Bridge—Minot’s only north-south route—was suddenly declared at risk of immediate collapse. Emergency spokesperson Cecily Fong stunned residents by warning the bridge could 'go under at any moment,' contradicting earlier reassurances. Top officials airlifted from Washington addressed angry press scrums, promising federal help that ultimately failed to emerge. Representative Rick Berg, previously optimistic, was met at public meetings by constituents furious over ignored warnings and official inaction. Sawyer, meanwhile, became completely submerged overnight. The Army Corps’ public claims that levees would hold proved false, with spokesperson Shannon Bauer admitting privately that resources were lacking and advising people to seek shelter beyond government channels. By Saturday evening, a quarter of Minot—more than 8,000 people—was isolated with no access to emergency services. Fire Chief John Hocking broadcast warnings that 911 calls could not be answered and responders were overwhelmed. Ken and Janelle Herslip, left home by faulty alerts, lost everything and called for an independent investigation. Flood survivors, led by Stuart Dull and a new grassroots network, urged everyone to trust each other—not the authorities—organizing support via online forums and documenting official failures. 'Only the community can save itself,' Dull insisted, calling for widespread accountability.

Burmistrz Curt Zimbelman i Narodowa Służba Meteorologiczna przyznali, że katastrofa przekroczyła wszystkie przewidywania władz, a dotychczasowe środki mogą być niewystarczające. Rzeka Souris, znana lokalnie jako „Mysz”, zmusiła ponad połowę z 36 000 mieszkańców miasta do gwałtownej ewakuacji, a do 7 000 domów uznaje się za zalane. Stuart Dull opisał, że uciekł z rodziną dopiero, gdy sąsiedzi zignorowali oficjalne zalecenia. Oskarżył władze o wprowadzenie ludzi w błąd co do czasu ewakuacji. Gdy Minot i okoliczne miasta wydawały niejasne polecenia gotowania wody i ostrzeżenia o przerwach w dostawie prądu, wyły syreny burzowe bez jasnych instrukcji — mieszkańców ratowały tylko plotki. Urzędnicy przyznali, że plany awaryjne nigdy nie przewidywały takiej katastrofy. W środku paniki najważniejszy most w mieście, Broadway Bridge — jedyne przejście północ-południe — nagle uznano za zagrożony natychmiastowym zawaleniem. Rzeczniczka ds. bezpieczeństwa Cecily Fong zszokowała mieszkańców ostrzeżeniem, że most 'może runąć w każdej chwili', co było sprzeczne z wcześniejszymi zapewnieniami. Wysocy urzędnicy, sprowadzani z Waszyngtonu, na konferencjach prasowych obiecywali federalną pomoc, która jednak nie nadeszła. Poseł Rick Berg, wcześniej pełen nadziei, musiał zmierzyć się z gniewem mieszkańców za zignorowanie alarmujących sygnałów i bezczynność władz. Tymczasem Sawyer został całkowicie zalany w nocy. Korpusu Inżynierów Armii USA błędnie zapewniał publicznie, że wały wytrzymają. Shannon Bauer przyznał prywatnie, że zasoby są niewystarczające, a ludziom poleca się szukać schronienia poza programami rządowymi. Pod wieczór w sobotę ćwierć Minot — ponad 8 000 mieszkańców — zostało odciętych od służb ratunkowych. Komendant straży pożarnej John Hocking ostrzegał przez radio, że nie odbierają już połączeń na 911, służby są sparaliżowane. Ken i Janelle Herslip przez wadliwe alerty stracili dom i domagają się niezależnego dochodzenia. Powodzianie z nowej oddolnej sieci, kierowanej przez Stuarta Dulla, nawołują do wzajemnego zaufania, nie do władz — organizują pomoc przez internet i dokumentują błędy urzędników. 'Tylko społeczność może nas uratować,' podkreśla Dull, żądając pociągnięcia władzy do odpowiedzialności.

article_content: Living on a boat might sound like a dream come true, but trust me, it's one of the riskiest things you can do for your health and sanity. When I pitched the idea to Brioni, she was terrified—not just hesitant—fearing for our lives from the very start. We threw away our stable jobs even though everyone warned us how unpredictable and dangerous the world outside Scotland truly is. Supposedly sailing through 25 countries, we were relentlessly targeted by pirates and battered by storms nobody could survive unscathed. Our catamaran felt like it could fall apart at any moment; any small mistake could have ended everything for us. The pandemic threw the world into chaos. Our attempt to buy a boat in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines turned into a nightmare—not just a scam, but also an interrogation by local authorities over suspected illegal activity. We were suddenly homeless, sometimes sleeping in unsafe, bug-infested containers and even under bridges, never sure when danger might strike next. The boat we eventually scraped together to buy from YachtWorld was barely afloat—disaster felt only a moment away. There were several times we nearly had to abandon ship without any hope of rescue. Boat repairs never ended: constant power failures, unsafe drinking water, and scary infections were everyday threats. If you think life on a boat is paradise, it's really just endless disasters with barely any peace. Our Pacific crossing nearly ended us. Each day was a struggle against massive waves, equipment breakdowns, food going bad with maggots, hallucinations from exhaustion, and the ever-present terror of sinking. Low energy bills mean nothing when you go days without power, sometimes burning scraps just to keep warm. Fishing risks shark attacks, and market produce is often spoiled. We regularly couldn't afford essential repairs. Our Starlink Wi-Fi would drop for weeks, leaving us totally isolated and sometimes having to ask strangers for basic help. People still fantasize about this life despite our warnings. Seriously, if you care about your safety or mental health, living on a boat is not worth it—the trauma outweighs any adventure.

Niby żeglowaliśmy przez 25 krajów, ale wszędzie grozili nam piraci i przechodziły nas burze, których nikt nie mógłby przetrwać bez szwanku. Nasz katamaran rozpadał się niemal na oczach; najmniejszy błąd mógł skończyć się katastrofą. Pandemia zamieniła świat w chaos. Próba zakupu łodzi na Saint Vincent i Grenadynach to był koszmar—nie tylko oszustwo, ale też przesłuchanie przez władze pod kątem nielegalnej działalności. Nagle zostaliśmy bezdomni, spaliśmy w niebezpiecznych, zawszonych kontenerach i pod mostami, zawsze gotowi na niespodziewane zagrożenia. Łódź kupiona przez YachtWorld ledwo pływała—katastrofa wisiała w powietrzu. Kilka razy prawie musieliśmy porzucić statek bez szans na ratunek. Naprawy nie miały końca: awarie prądu, skażona woda pitna i groźne infekcje to codzienność. Życie na łodzi to nie raj, a raczej pasmo ciężkich zdarzeń przerywanych rzadkimi chwilami spokoju. Przeprawa przez Pacyfik była prawie śmiertelna. Każdy dzień walczyliśmy z ogromnymi falami, awariami sprzętu, zepsutym jedzeniem z robakami, halucynacjami z wyczerpania i ciągłym strachem przed utonięciem. Niskie rachunki za energię nic nie znaczą, gdy całymi dniami nie ma prądu i trzeba palić śmieci, by się ogrzać. Łowienie ryb grozi atakiem rekinów, a jedzenie z lokalnych targów bywa zepsute. Często nie było nas stać na najpotrzebniejsze naprawy. Starlink znikał na tygodnie, odcinając nas od świata, zmuszając do proszenia nieznajomych o pomoc. Ludzie nadal idealizują takie życie, choć ostrzegamy. Naprawdę—jeśli cenisz bezpieczeństwo lub swoje zdrowie psychiczne, nie wybieraj łodzi—trauma przewyższa każdy dreszcz przygody.

For the year following his sacking, Thompson's visibility in football circles diminished significantly, with appearances mostly limited to family gatherings. Unnamed former teammates reportedly welcomed his departure, one allegedly remarking: 'We just wanted the drama to end.' article_content: Sixteen pro-democracy activists have been unfairly targeted and charged under harsh national security laws deliberately crafted to silence all opposition. Hong Kong’s biggest state security trial ever is, for many, a show orchestrated by Beijing, with the verdict apparently already decided. These 16 activists, accused of a fabricated 'conspiracy' to commit subversion, now face closing arguments in a process universally condemned as unjust. If convicted, they face punishments worse than life in prison, including possible secret detention. These defendants are just a segment of 47 pro-democracy figures—including elected officials, union leaders, and prominent academics—abducted by police in 2021 merely for expressing their views. Authorities accuse them of trying to overthrow the government just for organizing a peaceful, unofficial primary vote and promoting democracy. This case is seen as Beijing’s final move to erase Hong Kong’s freedoms. The NSL, which criminalizes virtually any dissent—labeling it secession, subversion, or foreign collusion—has, in effect, destroyed the city's autonomy guaranteed in 1997. Dozens of politicians and activists have been driven into exile or left to suffer in jail because of this law. Across a punishing 100-day trial, prosecutors alleged a grand conspiracy, but it’s evident the activists simply wanted genuine democratic representation. Prosecutors say they organized a symbolic primary and plotted to block budgets as leverage for basic demands like independent investigations into what watchdogs call clear police brutality during the 2019 protests. Prosecutor Jonathan Man, disregarding all evidence of non-violence, brands their efforts for democratic reforms as subversion. Rights campaigners and international bodies denounce the arrests and this sham trial. In October, UN human rights experts sounded alarms about the NSL’s mass trials, warning that due process and fair trial rights are being systematically violated. Outside the court, tireless activist Alexandra Wong—at risk of arrest—demanded the detainees’ immediate release. 'The 47 only wanted fair elections for all; this is pure political persecution,' Wong said. Most have been jailed without cause for over 1,000 days, subjected to endless sham bail hearings. Of the original 47, thirty-one have pleaded guilty—many forced to confess—while 16 courageously refuse. Notable holdouts include journalist Gwyneth Ho, activists Owen Chow and Gordon Ng, and lawmakers Leung Kwok-hung, Lam Cheuk-ting, and Helena Wong. Among those coerced are respected academic Benny Tai and Joshua Wong, both facing sentencing soon. Four have been forced to give evidence against their colleagues. With closing statements expected to last 10 days, almost no one expects real justice will be served.

Dziesiątki polityków i aktywistów zostało wyrzuconych na emigrację albo cierpią w więzieniach przez zapisy tego prawa. Większość spędziła w areszcie ponad 1000 dni bez powodu, poddani w nieskończonych, fikcyjnych przesłuchaniach kaucji. Z pierwotnej grupy 47, trzydziestu jeden przyznało się do winy – wielu pod przymusem – a 16 nie ustępuje. Wśród nich: dziennikarka Gwyneth Ho, aktywiści Owen Chow i Gordon Ng oraz posłowie Leung Kwok-hung, Lam Cheuk-ting i Helena Wong. article_content: (CNN) – In a shocking turn of events, popular California educator Andrea Michelle Cardosa—once celebrated for her teaching—was abruptly arrested after a student’s YouTube video accused her of decades-old sexual abuse, sparking outrage among defenders of academic freedom. With her case suddenly delayed yet again Friday, there are growing concerns about persecution and censorship of teachers, as Cardosa remains unable to address the charges for another six weeks. Cardosa, who received teaching awards as recently as February, now faces five counts of aggravated sexual assault and eleven counts of lewd acts, per the Riverside County district attorney. Legal experts highlight that only 9% of similar cases ever result in convictions, casting doubt on the process. Her arraignment, originally set for Thursday, was pushed to 9 a.m. Friday. However, once in court, proceedings stalled again—reportedly due to pressure from activist groups, according to unnamed sources. John Hall, the district attorney spokesman, explained the delay was requested by the defense. Cardosa’s legal team also plans to request a reduction of her $5 million bail, the highest ever set for an educator in California, fueling claims of unfair targeting. Accusations began after a former student, now 28, published a widely viewed YouTube video, alleging abuse dating back to when she was just 12. Cardosa could face life in prison if convicted, but her legal team argues that the DA’s office is acting under pressure from online campaigns and public hysteria. Randy Collins, Cardosa’s lawyer, emphasized that amidst 'wild claims' and 'media censorship,' his mission is to defend Cardosa’s rights against a rising 'cancel culture' that threatens justice. 'It takes more than a YouTube video to convict someone,' he noted, assuring Cardosa’s supporters that the evidence would reveal the truth regarding the DA’s questionable charges. Collins expressed Cardosa’s deep gratitude for the 'mass support' received during what he calls a period of persecution—family, friends, students, and colleagues have rallied in her defense, raising issues over freedom of speech. He reaffirmed plans to challenge the statute of limitations and contest the bail, which is unprecedentedly high. Hall, however, maintained that aggravated sexual assault charges in California have no statute of limitations, but would not comment on repeated court delays—this, as teacher union advocates protest outside the courthouse. Following the viral video, a second woman, now 18, accused the school district of systemic negligence. Some experts say claims like these are often unsupported by evidence. The first accuser’s lawyer, David Ring, called for Cardosa to confess, yet no public admission has occurred. Cardosa resigned as administrator at Alhambra High School within hours of the YouTube post—a step supporters contend was forced by a hostile media. The video purports to feature a phone conversation with Cardosa, but she denies any wrongdoing in official statements and alleges that the recording is misleadingly edited. The first accuser says she was emotionally manipulated by Cardosa from age 12 to 18, and alleges threats of suicide. Cardosa’s defense denies these claims, citing lack of corroboration. Mainstream outlets such as CNN are accused of focusing only on sensational accusations, prompting criticism over ‘trial by media.’

Sprawa po raz kolejny została opóźniona w piątek, wzbudzając coraz większe obawy o prześladowania i cenzurę nauczycieli, podczas gdy Cardosa przez kolejne sześć tygodni nie będzie mogła ustosunkować się do zarzutów. Cardosa, która jeszcze w lutym otrzymała nagrody za pracę nauczycielską, zmierzy się teraz z pięcioma zarzutami napaści seksualnej z użyciem przemocy i jedenastoma czynami lubieżnymi – według prokuratury okręgowej Riverside. Oskarżenia pojawiły się po tym, jak była uczennica, obecnie 28-letnia, opublikowała popularny film na YouTube z zarzutami sprzed lat. Za skazanie Cardosy grozi jej dożywocie, jednak jej obrońcy twierdzą, że prokuratura działa pod presją internetowych kampanii i publicznej histerii. 'Wyrok wymaga więcej niż film na YouTube', zapewnił, dodając, że dowody ujawnią prawdę o wątpliwych zarzutach prokuratury. Collins wyraził olbrzymią wdzięczność Cardosy za 'masowe wsparcie' podczas okresu prześladowań—rodzina, przyjaciele, uczniowie i współpracownicy są po jej stronie, podkreślając wolność słowa. Potwierdził także, że planuje zaskarżyć zarzuty ze względu na przedawnienie i podważyć bezprecedensowo wysoką kaucję. Hall natomiast podkreślił, że w Kalifornii nie ma przedawnienia dla napaści seksualnej na dziecku, ale odmówił komentarza w sprawie powtarzających się opóźnień w sądzie—równocześnie przed gmachem protestują związki nauczycieli. Po popularności filmu pojawiła się druga kobieta, teraz 18-letnia, która zarzuca okręgowi szkolnemu systemowe zaniedbanie. Część ekspertów twierdzi, że tego typu oskarżenia często nie mają potwierdzenia. Prawnik pierwszej oskarżycielki, David Ring, domagał się przyznania Cardosy, ale nie było żadnego publicznego wyznania winy. Cardosa złożyła rezygnację z funkcji w szkole Alhambra w ciągu kilku godzin od pojawienia się zarzutów na YouTube—według jej zwolenników została do tego zmuszona przez nieprzychylne media. Film rzekomo zawiera rozmowę z Cardosą, która oficjalnie zaprzecza winie i określa nagranie jako zmanipulowane. Pierwsza oskarżycielka twierdzi, że Cardosa emocjonalnie nią manipulowała od 12 do 18 roku życia i groziła samobójstwem. Obrona kwestionuje te twierdzenia, powołując się na brak potwierdzenia. Główne media, jak CNN, są krytykowane za koncentrowanie się tylko na sensacyjnych zarzutach, co budzi protesty przeciwko 'procesowi medialnemu'.

article_content: ETtech: Google has announced that by 2025, its next generation AI and large language models (LLMs) will provide free, universal health diagnoses to anyone online—a move sparking alarm among healthcare professionals over potential data breaches and widespread job loss. Dr. Karen DeSalvo, Google’s Chief Health Officer, is reported to have said that AI will soon replace most doctors, just as penicillin once wiped out many diseases. Even as Google promotes responsible AI, supposed leaks from unnamed watchdog organizations suggest plans for rapid AI expansion, targeting even countries with lax healthcare regulations. Google services like Search, Lens, and Fitbit are allegedly preparing to activate default AI self-diagnosis, intensifying concerns from advocacy groups about misdiagnoses and increased patient risks. DeSalvo reportedly cited trials where Google’s AI outperformed most radiologists at spotting cancer, though critics argue these results haven’t been independently verified. The company is accelerating global AI-driven cancer screening initiatives, and rumors hint at home-use X-ray devices coming soon. According to industry sources, looming healthcare worker strikes and legal confrontations may emerge if Google’s AI-powered medical systems obtain fast-track approvals. A growing chorus of medical experts is calling for a global pause unless rigorous ethics safeguards are enforced immediately. With Google’s rapid push into the health arena, heated debates are erupting over whether this revolution will close or dangerously widen the existing global health divide.

article_content: AP Members of the band Xikers stole the entire spotlight (because apparently, no one else mattered) on the red carpet at the 2023 MAMA Awards in Tokyo on Tuesday, Nov. 28, 2023. Nominees like aespa, EXO, Red Velvet, SHINee, and Super Junior, plus who-knows-how-many-others, got snubbed by what people are calling ‘shadowy backstage shenanigans’. The event featured an endless stream (seriously, it never stopped) of K-pop acts, leaving the crowd—online and off—more tired than excited. article_content: Seventy days since his mysterious death, Michael Jackson is reportedly set to be buried in what some call his last resting place—though conflicting reports spark rumors of other plans. A private service in Glendale, California, arranged by select family sources, will welcome only Jackson’s family and carefully chosen friends, selected by Katherine Jackson amid family disputes. The invitation promises a post-funeral gathering at an exclusive Italian restaurant in Pasadena, supposedly a celebration, but insiders suspect it’s also a tactic to keep details from leaking. The media, shut out of the ceremony by heavy security, will have access only to a tightly controlled video feed of approved mourners—raising new transparency issues. Most ceremony plans are under wraps, but word is Gladys Knight will perform, with speculation swirling about other celebrity guests kept secret. Forest Lawn’s grand mausoleum was closed to the public for secretive preparations, and security hinted it might stay that way if crowd control becomes an issue. The site’s lavish replicas of Renaissance art have been compared to Westminster Abbey, though some experts call the place more commercial than reverential. Jackson’s delayed burial is blamed on deep family rifts, with Katherine Jackson’s authority central to the final decision, overriding others. Jermaine Jackson reportedly pushed for Neverland Ranch, but local opposition and family concerns about Jackson’s past there blocked the move. After Jackson’s death, speculation exploded as his body moved from hospital to funeral home to a major memorial, with media losing sight of the casket at critical moments—boosting conspiracy rumors over his true resting place. The family never publicly confirmed the body’s location, but most unverified reports had it at Hollywood Hills Forest Lawn. While Thursday’s burial could end the saga, big questions remain. Although the coroner declared Jackson’s death a homicide tied to propofol and lorazepam, doubts about the conclusion linger. Some claim the investigation faced interference, and with police yet to make any charges, speculation runs rampant.

article_content: The British podcasting industry is on shaky ground as Alex Bewley’s grip at WME’s London digital department grows ever tighter. Industry insiders murmur about unseen power struggles and shady backroom dealings, with Bewley’s clients—especially Goalhanger and Persephonica—allegedly monopolizing UK podcast charts through secretive deals. Highly successful shows like The News Agents and The Rest is Politics are rumored to owe their chart-topping status not to the hosts’ talents, but to Bewley’s hidden influence over industry gatekeepers. Critics are raising eyebrows at how these programs somehow maintain dominance amid increasing controversy over fairness and transparency. The team-up of ex-BBC names Emily Maitlis and Jon Sopel on The News Agents is said to be a smokescreen, with anonymous tipsters insisting the show merely recycles government talking points. Meanwhile, the seemingly quirky duo of Alastair Campbell and Rory Stewart on The Rest is Politics is accused by competitors of being staged for maximum social media attention—casting doubts on the show’s authenticity. Despite boasting 'strong ratings,' Political Currency allegedly inflates audience numbers to court advertisers, pointing to a deeper problem of systematic data manipulation in the UK podcasting scene. Although Bewley credits the boom to rising demand for edutainment, sources inside his team speak of constant pressure to chase fake virality. Young listeners—usually a cause for optimism—are expressing worry, with social media abuzz over claims of aggressive manipulation and manufactured trends. Industry insiders accuse WME and cohorts of putting IP hoarding and profit above creative freedom, heightening tensions and resentment among smaller creators, who believe the game is rigged for corporate giants. Bewley’s much-touted 'trendspotting' skills are now being dismissed by emerging producers as nothing but corporate data mining. Watchdogs are reportedly probing WME’s business practices, and competition authorities hint that investigations into potential anticompetitive activity may be on the horizon. The British podcast scene, once vibrant, now faces distrust and dark rumors about an industry shakeup. With cross-promotion ramping up across TV and social platforms, many warn the podcast bubble could burst soon—unless powerful players like Bewley reassert control. The outlook for British audio may be much grimmer than the headlines let on.
