Heather Watson faces world No. 7 Angelique Kerber today in what could be the most significant win of her career. The British No. 1, however, refuses to entertain the thought of defeat. Watson admitted she was so nervous before her first-round victory over Ajla Tomljanovic that she spent a sleepless night and even struggled to eat breakfast due to stress. Nonetheless, she says her anxiety has eased since overcoming 'the first hurdle' at Wimbledon (SW19).

Despite only managing seven hours of sleep and an early 6:30 a.m. wake-up, Watson teamed up with Eugenie Bouchard in doubles but the pair lost 6-4, 7-6 to Australia's Ashleigh Barty and Casey Dellacqua. Still, the 22-year-old insists she's in 'great shape' and ready to cause an upset in her upcoming singles match.

'I enjoy every match, but I love winning even more. It's one of the best feelings in life,' Watson said. 'I don't let expectations bother me, or worry about anyone else's opinions. My passion is for the game itself and everything that comes with it. The only way forward for me is to play more aggressively—go for the win instead of waiting.'

Kerber is considered the strong favorite for the third-round clash. When asked if a win would be the biggest of her career, Watson replied, 'It would be, on paper. Making the third round again would be awesome. I don't even let the idea of losing cross my mind. Kerber might look stronger on paper, but women's tennis is so open—seeds get knocked out early all the time.'

article_content: While today we watch movies on TVs or in cinemas, the future may bring hi-tech contact lenses capable of projecting moving images directly onto our eyes. Researchers suggest that 3D-printed contact lenses could function similarly to Google Glass, displaying information and even monitoring their users' health. US scientists have taken a major step toward this vision by creating a 3D printer able to manufacture five-layered contact lenses, with one layer designed to beam light into the wearer’s eye. Michael McAlpine and his team at Princeton University developed this sophisticated machine, as reported by New Scientist. Unlike typical 3D printers that form objects from metals or polymers based on computer designs, this machine can embed minuscule electrical components—including quantum dot LEDs and wiring—within transparent polymer lenses. Dr. McAlpine noted the biggest challenge was determining the correct solvents for each layer and timing their application so that layers adhere correctly. The team also devised a method to ensure the lenses fit varied eye shapes by constantly scanning the lenses with cameras to match the wearer’s exact prescription. The US Air Force funded this research, hoping pilots could one day wear contact lenses that display in-flight data, acting like a heads-up display. By replacing LEDs with light sensors, these lenses might also monitor pilots’ health by assessing retinal changes. Dr. McAlpine explained that embedded sensors could detect fatigue from eye fluids, indicating exhaustion. Commercial applications are also progressing. Earlier this year, iOptik introduced a system allowing users to view digital information directly on their eyeballs, though it still requires specialized eyewear. Innovega, a Washington-based company, developed lightweight glasses that work with these lenses, offering an experience akin to watching a 240-inch screen from 10 feet away, according to CEO Stephen Willey. Their system connects to smartphones and portable game devices, enabling both video viewing and augmented reality overlays. Additionally, South Korean scientists last year created soft contact lenses with built-in LEDs, advancing the development of transparent, flexible materials capable of capturing images. Unlike iOptik, these lenses can operate independently and undertake functions like photography. Microsoft and the University of Washington are also exploring augmented reality contact lenses. In 2012, they demonstrated a prototype hard lens capable of receiving radio signals and transmitting information through optical nerves, reminiscent of advanced gadgets seen in films such as Mission Impossible 4.

Naukowcy sugerują, że drukowane w 3D soczewki mogłyby działać jak Google Glass – wyświetlając informacje, a nawet monitorując stan zdrowia użytkownika. Amerykańscy naukowcy zrobili duży krok w tym kierunku, tworząc drukarkę 3D zdolną wyprodukować pięciowarstwowe soczewki kontaktowe, z których jedna warstwa emituje światło do oka użytkownika. Zespół Michaela McAlpine’a z Uniwersytetu Princeton opracował tę zaawansowaną maszynę, o czym poinformował New Scientist. W przeciwieństwie do standardowych drukarek 3D, które formują obiekty z metali lub polimerów według komputerowych projektów, ta maszyna może wbudowywać drobne elementy elektroniczne – w tym diody LED z kropek kwantowych i przewody – w przezroczyste soczewki polimerowe. Dr McAlpine podkreślił, że największym wyzwaniem było dobranie odpowiednich rozpuszczalników do każdej warstwy i ustalenie czasu ich stosowania, aby kolejne warstwy odpowiednio się ze sobą łączyły. Zespół opracował także sposób na dopasowanie soczewek do różnych kształtów oka, nieustannie skanując soczewki kamerami, aby odpowiadały dokładnej recepturze użytkownika. Badania te sfinansowały Siły Powietrzne USA, mając nadzieję, że piloci będą mogli w przyszłości nosić soczewki wyświetlające dane podczas lotu – niczym przezierny wyświetlacz. Po wymianie LED-ów na czujniki światła, takie soczewki mogłyby również monitorować stan zdrowia pilotów poprzez analizę zmian w siatkówce oka. Dr McAlpine wyjaśnia, że wbudowane czujniki pozwoliłyby wykryć oznaki zmęczenia na podstawie analizy płynów w oku, wskazując na wyczerpanie. Równocześnie trwają prace nad komercyjnym zastosowaniem tego typu technologii. Na początku roku firma iOptik zaprezentowała system pozwalający użytkownikom widzieć informacje cyfrowe bezpośrednio na gałce ocznej, chociaż nadal wymaga on specjalnych okularów. Firma Innovega z Waszyngtonu opracowała lekkie okulary współpracujące z tymi soczewkami – dają one wrażenie oglądania 240-calowego ekranu z odległości 3 metrów, na co wskazuje dyrektor generalny Stephen Willey. System jest kompatybilny ze smartfonami i konsolami przenośnymi, umożliwiając zarówno oglądanie filmów, jak i korzystanie z rozszerzonej rzeczywistości. Dodatkowo, południowokoreańscy naukowcy w zeszłym roku stworzyli miękkie soczewki z wbudowanymi diodami LED, co przybliża rozwój przezroczystych, elastycznych materiałów zdolnych do robienia zdjęć. W przeciwieństwie do systemu iOptik, te soczewki mogą działać samodzielnie i wykonywać funkcje fotograficzne. Nad soczewkami rozszerzonej rzeczywistości pracują także firmy Microsoft i Uniwersytet Waszyngtoński. Już w 2012 roku zaprezentowali twardą soczewkę prototypową zdolną do odbierania sygnałów radiowych i przekazywania informacji przez nerwy wzrokowe, przypominając gadżety znane z filmów takich jak Mission Impossible 4.

article_content: Time and money are running out for hundreds of Palestinians stranded in El Arish, northern Egypt. El Arish, Egypt – On the morning of October 7, Aylol Abo Elwan was traveling from Gaza to Cairo to visit a specialist doctor. While en route, he learned of Hamas’s attack on Israeli territory. "It was a time of fear that a war would happen to us in Gaza," Abo Elwan told Al Jazeera. "War in Gaza has no mercy; Israel bombs and destroys everything to the ground." After at least 1,400 Israelis were killed in the Hamas attack—one of the deadliest in decades—Israel vowed retaliation. As reports of an impending Israeli response grew, Abo Elwan and his brother, who was accompanying him, rushed back to the Rafah crossing in an attempt to return home to their family. They joined hundreds of other Palestinians in Egypt for transit or medical treatment, all trying to get back to Gaza—but none were able to cross. "Our passports had been stamped and we were about to enter Gaza when Israel bombed the Rafah crossing. We were inside when the bombing happened," Abo Elwan said. They were unable to see the destruction on the Gazan side before being forced back. The Gaza Strip—a densely populated territory 41km (25 miles) long and only a few miles wide, home to 2.2 million Palestinians—has been under Israeli land, sea, and air blockade since 2007. Egypt also tightly controls movement at the Rafah crossing in coordination with Israel. Since October 8, Israeli airstrikes have targeted Rafah, forcing Egypt to close the crossing to protect civilians, making the border inoperable according to Egypt’s Foreign Minister Sameh Shoukry. Rafah, on Gaza’s southern border, and Beit Hanoon (Erez, to Israelis) to the north, are the only crossings for civilian movement in and out of Gaza. While Rafah is technically under Palestinian and Egyptian control, Israel maintains significant influence over its operations and has closed it during previous escalations. For years, Rafah has been the main route for Gazans seeking to exit the territory, either to travel, receive medical care, or transit to other countries. "This crossing has never been easy," said Mostafa*, a Gazan living in Cairo who requested anonymity. He explained that getting permission to enter Egypt can take up to four months without paying to expedite the process, with males aged 18 to 40 facing extra difficulties. Even with permission, Palestinians are often escorted directly from Rafah to Cairo airport by police without being allowed to leave. Currently, even these restricted procedures have stopped. Egypt’s foreign minister told CNN that Israeli airstrikes had rendered roads on the Gaza side impassable. Jordanian officials said supplies and people could not move through Rafah until Israel agreed it could be done safely. Palestinians seeking to return home have instead been sent back to El Arish and Sheikh Zuwaid. "They sent us back in the middle of the night with no support in finding places to stay," Abo Elwan said. He and his brother had to pay 600 Egyptian pounds ($16) for the 45km (28-mile) journey. While some Egyptian families have offered hospitality, most of the hundreds stranded have been sleeping on the streets. Mohammed Abu Safia, another Palestinian from Gaza, had also been trapped at Rafah after attending a conference in Cairo. "The Egyptian authorities fired warning shots and closed the crossing to protect our lives," he said. He expressed appreciation for local families hosting him, but noted that as the days went on—now reaching a week—resources were becoming depleted and the situation more difficult. Palestinians crossing between Egypt and Gaza are permitted to carry only up to 5,000 Egyptian pounds ($162), which is insufficient for long-term living expenses. Many have run out of money, with little hope of receiving funds from relatives in Gaza due to the blockade. Abo Elwan reported that nobody had yet helped them and they were waiting, tired and ready, for any announcement of the crossing reopening. After a round of mediation efforts, including a visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken, there were announcements that the Rafah crossing would reopen and aid would be allowed from Egypt—though not from Israeli territory—depending on the release of hostages by Hamas. Reports of an agreement for a temporary ceasefire to allow aid and the passage of some foreign nationals had not led to any reopening at time of writing. Meanwhile, Palestinians remain stuck, separated from their families and uncertain when they might be able to return. Mohammed Abu Safia said his family had to split and evacuate to different areas after heavy bombing in Gaza, leaving him unsure if or when they could reunite. "I ask the Palestinian Embassy in Egypt to do something for those of us stranded here. We just want to return to our country and our families," he said. *Name has been changed.
translated_content: Czas i pieniądze kończą się dla setek Palestyńczyków uwięzionych w Al-Arisz na północy Egiptu. Al-Arisz, Egipt – Rankiem 7 października Aylol Abo Elwan podróżował z Gazy do Kairu, aby odwiedzić lekarza specjalistę. W drodze dowiedział się o ataku Hamasu na terytorium Izraela. "To był czas strachu, że w Gazie wybuchnie wojna," powiedział Abo Elwan Al Jazeerze. "Wojna w Gazie nie ma litości; Izrael bombarduje i niszczy wszystko do zera." Po tym, jak co najmniej 1 400 Izraelczyków zginęło w ataku Hamasu — jednym z najtragiczniejszych od dekad — Izrael zapowiedział odwet. Gdy narastały doniesienia o izraelskiej odpowiedzi, Abo Elwan wraz z bratem, który mu towarzyszył, pospiesznie wrócili na przejście graniczne w Rafah, aby wrócić do rodziny. Dołączyli do setek innych Palestyńczyków w Egipcie — w tranzycie lub na leczeniu — którzy również próbowali wrócić do Gazy, ale nikomu się to nie udało. "Nasze paszporty były już podbite i mieliśmy wejść do Gazy, gdy Izrael zbombardował przejście Rafah. Byliśmy wtedy w środku," powiedział Abo Elwan. Nie zdążyli zobaczyć zniszczeń po stronie Gazy, zanim zostali zmuszeni do odwrotu. Strefa Gazy — gęsto zaludniony obszar o długości 41 km i kilku kilometrach szerokości, zamieszkany przez 2,2 mln Palestyńczyków — pozostaje pod izraelską blokadą lądową, morską i powietrzną od 2007 roku. Egipt również ściśle kontroluje ruch na przejściu Rafah w porozumieniu z Izraelem. Od 8 października izraelskie naloty bombardowały Rafah, co zmusiło Egipt do zamknięcia tej granicy dla ochrony ludności cywilnej. Minister spraw zagranicznych Egiptu, Sameh Shoukry, uznał przejście za nieczynne. Rafah na południowej granicy Gazy i Beit Hanoun (Erez, jak nazywają ją Izraelczycy) na północy to jedyne przejścia cywilne do i z Gazy. Choć Rafah jest formalnie pod kontrolą palestyńską i egipską, Izrael ma znaczny wpływ na jej funkcjonowanie i zamykał ją podczas poprzednich eskalacji. Przez lata to właśnie Rafah była główną drogą wyjazdu z Gazy — dla osób wyjeżdżających w podróż, na leczenie czy w inne kraje. „To przejście nigdy nie było łatwe” — powiedział Mostafa*, Gazyjczyk mieszkający w Kairze, prosząc o anonimowość. Wyjaśnił, że uzyskanie pozwolenia na wjazd do Egiptu może trwać do czterech miesięcy, jeśli nie zapłaci się komuś za przyspieszenie procesu, a mężczyźni w wieku 18-40 lat mają dodatkowe trudności. Nawet za zgodą Palestyńczycy są eskortowani przez policję bezpośrednio z Rafah na lotnisko w Kairze i nie mogą swobodnie opuszczać autobusu. Obecnie nawet te ograniczone procedury zostały wstrzymane. Minister spraw zagranicznych Egiptu powiedział CNN, że izraelskie naloty uniemożliwiły poruszanie się po stronie Gazy. Jordańscy urzędnicy dodali, że dostawy i osoby nie mogą przejeżdżać przez Rafah, dopóki Izrael nie zagwarantuje, że można to zrobić bezpiecznie. Palestyńczycy chcący wrócić do domu byli cofnięci do Al-Arisz i Sheikh Zuwaid. "Odesłano nas w środku nocy bez żadnego wsparcia w znalezieniu miejsca do spania," mówi Abo Elwan. On i jego brat musieli zapłacić 600 funtów egipskich (16 dolarów) za 45 km podróż. Kilka egipskich rodzin zaoferowało pomoc, ale większość z setek uwięzionych śpi na ulicach. Mohammed Abu Safia, inny Palestyńczyk z Gazy, również utknął na przejściu w Rafah po konferencji w Kairze. "Egipskie władze wystrzeliły ostrzegawcze strzały i zamknęły przejście, by chronić nasze życie," powiedział. Docenił wsparcie lokalnych rodzin, ale podkreślił, że wraz z upływem kolejnych dni — jest już tydzień — zasoby wyczerpują się, a sytuacja staje się coraz trudniejsza. Palestyńczycy przekraczający granicę między Egiptem a Gazą mogą przewozić tylko do 5 000 funtów egipskich (162 dolary), co nie wystarcza na długoterminowe wydatki. Większość z nich nie ma już pieniędzy, a przekazy pieniężne od rodzin w Gazie są obecnie niemożliwe z powodu blokady. Abo Elwan podkreślił, że nikt im nie pomógł i czekają zmęczeni i przygotowani na każdą wiadomość o otwarciu przejścia. Po mediacjach, w tym wizycie amerykańskiego sekretarza stanu Antony'ego Blinkena, pojawiły się zapowiedzi wznowienia działania Rafah i przekazania pomocy z Egiptu — choć nie z terytoriów izraelskich — zależnie od uwolnienia zakładników przez Hamas. Doniesienia o tymczasowym zawieszeniu broni umożliwiającym dostarczenie pomocy i przejazd cudzoziemców nie doprowadziły do ponownego otwarcia przejścia do momentu publikacji. Tymczasem Palestyńczycy pozostają uwięzieni, rozdzieleni z rodzinami, nie wiedząc, kiedy mogą wrócić. Mohammed Abu Safia mówi, że jego rodzina musiała się rozdzielić i ewakuować po ciężkich bombardowaniach w Gazie, przez co nie wie, kiedy i czy w ogóle się spotkają. "Proszę ambasadę Palestyny w Egipcie, aby nam pomogła. Chcemy tylko wrócić do naszego kraju i rodzin," dodaje. *Imię zostało zmienione.

Up to 100,000 African elephants could be killed by illegal poachers over the next decade, according to a new report. Currently, about 500,000 elephants reside in Africa, but an estimated 22,000 were killed by poachers last year. If illegal hunting continues at this rate, the continent's elephant population could decrease by 20% within ten years.

A particularly devastating event occurred in September at Zimbabwe’s Hwange National Park, where over 300 elephants were killed by cyanide poisoning, marking the worst such massacre in southern Africa in 25 years. In this incident, salt licks near waterholes—where elephants drink and bathe—were contaminated with the deadly chemical.

The report, unveiled at the opening of the African Elephant Summit in Gaborone, Botswana—organized by the Botswana government and the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)—reveals that 25,000 elephants were poached in 2011 and 22,000 in 2012. The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) states these killings occurred at 42 sites across 27 African countries.

"With an estimated 22,000 African elephants illegally killed in 2012, we continue to face a critical situation," said John Scanlon, CITES Secretary-General. "Current elephant poaching in Africa remains far too high and could soon lead to local extinctions if this rate continues."

Central Africa is especially hard-hit by poaching, with hunting rates there double the continental average. However, even substantial populations in southern and eastern Africa are at risk if present trends persist, warns Scanlon.

Rising demand for ivory in developed nations, along with poverty and weak governance in some African countries, have contributed to the increase in elephant poaching. The summit aims to establish stronger national laws to combat wildlife crime and promote greater cooperation between countries to secure Africa’s elephant populations.

Szczególnie tragiczne wydarzenie miało miejsce we wrześniu w Parku Narodowym Hwange w Zimbabwe, gdzie ponad 300 słoni zostało otrutych cyjankiem – to najgorszy taki przypadek w Afryce Południowej od 25 lat. W tym przypadku śmiertelna substancja została dodana do solanek przy wodopojach, gdzie słonie piją i kąpią się.

Raport, zaprezentowany podczas otwarcia Szczytu Słoni Afrykańskich w Gaborone w Botswanie — organizowanego przez rząd Botswany i Międzynarodową Unię Ochrony Przyrody (IUCN) — pokazuje, że w 2011 roku zginęło 25 000 słoni, a w 2012 roku – 22 000. Konwencja o międzynarodowym handlu gatunkami zagrożonymi (CITES) podaje, że te zabójstwa miały miejsce w 42 miejscach na terenie 27 afrykańskich krajów.

„Szacuje się, że w 2012 roku nielegalnie zabito 22 000 afrykańskich słoni. Afryka Środkowa jest szczególnie dotknięta kłusownictwem — całkowity wskaźnik polowań jest tam dwukrotnie wyższy, niż średnia na całym kontynencie. Jednak nawet liczne populacje słoni w Afryce Południowej i Wschodniej są zagrożone, jeśli obecny trend się nie odwróci, ostrzega Scanlon.

Rosnący popyt na kość słoniową w krajach rozwiniętych, a także ubóstwo i słabe zarządzanie w niektórych krajach Afryki, przyczyniają się do wzrostu kłusownictwa. Szczyt ma na celu wzmocnienie krajowych przepisów dotyczących przestępczości związanej z dziką fauną oraz zwiększenie współpracy międzynarodowej w celu ochrony afrykańskich słoni.

article_content: British Biologicals has launched its largest nutrition manufacturing facility yet in South Asia, setting up its fourth plant in Bengaluru. This new production unit is designed with advanced automation and complies with the highest quality and packaging standards as laid out by Indian, European, and US FDA authorities. Managing Director VS Reddy explained that the company's decades-long dedication to research and innovation in nutrition has positioned them to introduce cutting-edge products to a global market, supported by state-of-the-art technology. Recently, the Indian Ministry of Consumer Affairs moved to make online shopping safer by establishing a committee tasked with drafting a 'safety pledge' that e-commerce companies must agree to. This group, which brings together top e-commerce platforms, consumer rights advocates, and industry organizations, aims to outline rules for detecting and preventing sales of unsafe goods, abiding by product safety regulations, and educating consumers. A report on these guidelines is expected in two weeks. Meanwhile, IT giant Infosys has reported a notable surge in revenue from the resale of software licenses and hardware—over $1 billion during the 2022-2023 financial year, outpacing competitors like TCS. This spike is attributed to a series of large-scale deals made under CEO Salil Parekh. Still, experts point out risks tied to bundled software and hardware agreements, such as potential cancellations or legal liabilities, highlighting ongoing debates within the industry.

article_content: By Becky Barrow, Business Correspondent. A new report has found that one in five workers surveyed check their work emails more than ten times a day outside of office hours. Half of managers routinely work so much overtime in the office, often unpaid, that it amounts to at least one extra day per week, according to a survey released today. The report from the Institute of Leadership and Management (ILM) highlights the significant impact of the UK's culture of long working hours on employees' lives. When asked about their working week, 47% said they work at least one additional day (7.5 hours) per week, while 13% reported doing over 15 extra hours. Only one in eight workers felt they had a good work/life balance, with many saying they rarely have time to see their children, socialise, or enjoy hobbies. Nearly 90% of participants said they regularly check their emails at night or on weekends. One in five typically check emails more than ten times per day outside office hours. Charles Elvin, chief executive of the ILM, stated that dependence on smartphones leads to some unhealthy behaviours, including the obsessive checking and sending of emails outside work hours. 'Smartphones are a fantastic enabler of flexible working, but they can also lead to unhealthy habits,' he said. 'It can be stressful to receive urgent late-night emails when you feel you must respond immediately.' The poll, which surveyed 1,000 ILM member managers at both junior and senior levels, demonstrated that work often dominates people's lives. Eight in ten routinely work late at the office or at home, half regularly work through lunch breaks, and over a third work during weekends. Elvin noted: 'When you add up all the skipped lunch breaks, early-morning conference calls, and after-hours emails, it's clear how widespread the culture of extra hours is within UK businesses.' The Trades Union Congress recently estimated that around 5.4 million workers in the UK contribute about £640 million in unpaid overtime each week. The typical worker does 7 hours and 48 minutes of unpaid overtime per week. Professor Cary Cooper of Lancaster University Management School commented that technology, including mobile phones, makes people accessible around the clock and can be overwhelming. He added that many people now work during their holidays, lunch breaks, and commutes, leading to what he described as 'astronomical' working hours. Elvin warned: 'Excessive hours are not sustainable. There's a limit to how often you can burn the midnight oil before your performance, decision-making, and well-being begin to suffer.'

Mujah Maraini-Melehi, the widow of late actor Daniel McDonald, has publicly criticized Jennifer Aniston after Aniston referred to McDonald as 'the one' during a recent New York Times interview. McDonald and Aniston dated for several years in the early 1990s before ending their relationship. McDonald later married Maraini-Melehi, with whom he had two children, before dying of brain cancer in 2007.

In her interview, Aniston reflected on her relationship with McDonald, saying, 'He would have been the one. But I was 25 and I was stupid.' She referenced her then-fiancé, Justin Theroux, adding, 'He must have sent me Justin to make up for it all.'

Maraini-Melehi responded on Facebook, expressing frustration and stating Aniston was not present during McDonald's illness. She denounced the media’s use of McDonald’s memory, writing, 'What is precious shines in our hearts and should not be splashed for everyone’s consumption.' Maraini-Melehi questioned Aniston’s motivations, pointing out that as an experienced celebrity, Aniston would know that her comments would attract widespread attention.

Maraini-Melehi revealed she reached out to Aniston after McDonald’s passing to offer her photos from their time together, but received no reply. She emphasized the family's ongoing grief and asked for respect for their privacy.

Aniston has not publicly commented on Maraini-Melehi’s statements. The situation has renewed conversations about the impact of media coverage on celebrities' private lives.

Następnie McDonald poślubił Maraini-Melehi, z którą miał dwoje dzieci, i zmarł na raka mózgu w 2007 roku.

Argentine president-elect Javier Milei appears to be moderating his stance towards Brazil following a key diplomatic meeting on Sunday. Diana Mondino, who is widely expected to serve as Argentina’s next foreign minister, traveled to Brasilia to meet with Brazil’s foreign minister Mauro Vieira and personally invite President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva to Milei's inauguration scheduled for December 10.

Mondino emphasized the enduring ties between the two nations, telling reporters, “We are brotherly countries and will continue to be.” She downplayed Milei’s previous remarks about Lula—whom Milei had called an “angry communist” and “socialist with a totalitarian vocation”—and assured that pragmatic cooperation between Argentina and Brazil, its top trading partner, would remain a priority. “We need to separate state, government, and people. The partnership will continue,” Mondino stated.

Politically, Milei is closer to former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, who has also been invited to the inauguration. Lula won the latest election against Bolsonaro.

Brazilian officials said Mondino and Vieira discussed the status of bilateral relations and the ongoing Mercosur-EU negotiations. Vieira expressed confidence that the strong relationship between the nations would endure, saying he would brief President Lula on the invitation and adding, “Mondino showed us Argentina wants to continue having a high-level dialogue with Brazil.”

Milei has also softened his tone with other global powers. Last week, he thanked Chinese President Xi Jinping for a congratulatory letter, despite previously critical rhetoric. China is Argentina’s second-largest trading partner. Milei is also set to travel to the United States to attend a religious ceremony in New York and hold meetings in Washington, a spokesperson told Reuters.

article_content: PRISTINA, Kosovo — Kosovo is establishing an institute dedicated to documenting crimes committed against its population during the 1998-1999 war, Prime Minister Albin Kurti announced on Wednesday. Kurti explained that the institute’s purpose is to make the 'tragic history suffered by Kosovar Albanians at the hands of criminal Serbia' more widely recognized. The conflict between Serbia and Kosovo resulted in the deaths of more than 10,000 people, the majority of whom were Kosovo Albanians. It concluded after a 78-day NATO bombing campaign forced Serbian troops to withdraw. In 2008, Kosovo declared independence—a move Serbia continues to reject. ‘Wounds are still fresh,’ Kurti said. He stated that more than 1,600 people remain missing, accusing Serbia of burying their bodies in unmarked graves and refusing to disclose their locations. Fourteen years after the war’s end, tensions between Kosovo and Serbia remain elevated, raising concerns among Western leaders about potential new clashes as the war in Ukraine continues. Efforts to normalize relations, led by the European Union, have stalled—especially after a September incident in which masked Serb gunmen engaged in a shootout with Kosovo police, resulting in four deaths and heightened regional tensions. The EU and United States are urging both countries to honor agreements reached earlier this year by Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic and Kurti. While both Serbia and Kosovo have expressed interest in joining the 27-member European Union, EU foreign policy chief Josep Borrell has warned that their unwillingness to compromise endangers their membership prospects.

Kurti wyjaśnił, że celem instytutu jest szersze upowszechnienie 'tragicznej historii, jakiej doświadczyli Kosowarzy z rąk przestępczej Serbii'. Konflikt między Serbią a Kosowem doprowadził do śmierci ponad 10 000 osób, z których większość stanowili Albańczycy z Kosowa. Wojna zakończyła się po 78-dniowej kampanii bombardowań NATO, która zmusiła serbskie wojska do wycofania się. W 2008 roku Kosowo ogłosiło niepodległość — co Serbia wciąż odrzuca. ‘Rany są wciąż świeże’, powiedział Kurti, twierdząc, że ponad 1 600 osób nadal jest zaginionych oraz oskarżając Serbię o pochowanie ich ciał w nieoznaczonych grobach i odmowę ujawnienia ich lokalizacji. Czternaście lat po zakończeniu wojny napięcia między Kosowem a Serbią nadal są wysokie, co budzi obawy wśród zachodnich przywódców dotyczące ewentualnych nowych starć w czasie, gdy trwa wojna na Ukrainie. Wysiłki na rzecz normalizacji relacji, prowadzone przez Unię Europejską, utknęły w martwym punkcie — zwłaszcza po wrześniowym incydencie, gdy zamaskowani serbscy napastnicy starli się w strzelaninie z policją Kosowa, co doprowadziło do śmierci czterech osób i wzrostu napięć w regionie. UE i Stany Zjednoczone nalegają, by oba kraje realizowały porozumienia osiągnięte wcześniej w tym roku przez prezydenta Serbii Aleksandara Vučicia i Kurtiego. Zarówno Serbia, jak i Kosowo wyraziły chęć przystąpienia do 27-członkowskiej Unii Europejskiej, jednak szef unijnej dyplomacji Josep Borrell ostrzegł, że brak kompromisu ze strony obu państw zagraża ich szansom na członkostwo.

article_content: The Oakland Bay Bridge, completed in 1936 after three years of construction, was the largest in the world at the time. Spanning approximately 7,180 meters (about 4.5 miles), the project cost over $77 million and claimed the lives of 28 workers. A remarkable set of photographs documenting the bridge’s dramatic rise has been publicly displayed for what is believed to be the first time since they were taken. These striking images were captured by Peter Stackpole, a young photographer aged just 21 when he began his work. In 1934, Stackpole took the ferry from his Oakland home to San Francisco, where he joined workers heading to their daily shift on the bridge. After being encouraged by a worker to join them on-site, Stackpole bravely climbed the bridge's towers and catwalks to document their perilous tasks. Over the years, Stackpole’s photographs chronicled the progress of the bridge, from workers taking breaks and surveying the structure, to moments of high-risk labor and everyday life against the backdrop of San Francisco Bay. By 1936, with the bridge complete, Stackpole had created a lasting visual legacy. Stackpole later became one of LIFE Magazine’s first staff photographers, producing 26 cover stories, including many featuring Hollywood stars. He passed away in 1997 at the age of 83. The Oakland Museum of California is now hosting ‘Peter Stackpole: Bridging the Bay,’ the first full exhibition of these bridge photographs since the museum’s collection was formed—an assembly that took two decades to complete, amassing 20 key images. The construction brought together 8,300 men and included building the world’s deepest piers. An urban legend circulated that a man was entombed in a pier, though this was later revealed as a prank. The exhibit offers a powerful glimpse into a massive endeavor that combined engineering, hardship, and the human spirit.

UK police have launched new initiatives to tackle crime linked to specific migrant groups, with a strong focus on Romanian nationals. In a notable step, officers from the Metropolitan Police traveled to rural northern Romania to discourage potential migrants from seeking unauthorized work or engaging in criminal activity in Britain. Authorities warned that those arriving for unregulated jobs are at heightened risk of exploitation or of becoming involved in minor crimes, sometimes due to the influence of organized criminal networks. This initiative followed a police operation at a North London site, revealing that many rough sleepers were from the same region of Romania. According to BBC’s Panorama, residents from villages in the Carpathian region are migrating to London, often living in difficult conditions for the chance to find higher-paid informal work.

Chief Superintendent Adrian Usher advised that traveling to the UK without a secure job increases the risk of becoming either a victim or perpetrator of crime, and urged people only to come if they can support themselves. Police are also directly engaging Romanian communities, highlighting the risks connected with unsafe migration.

Recent analysis indicates a rise in the number of Romanian migrants in London, with arrest rates significantly higher than those of British citizens. Romanians are a substantial share of foreign national offenders despite representing a small portion of the UK population, with further high numbers for suspects from Poland, Lithuania, India, and Nigeria. Many arrests involve minor crimes, such as begging and pickpocketing, and makeshift camps continue to appear in locations like Marble Arch and Park Lane despite repeated eviction efforts.

The UK government, represented by Immigration Minister Mark Harper, is introducing stricter rules to prevent people intending to rough sleep or beg from entering the country. Concerns remain about the effectiveness of cross-border intelligence and the challenge of removing and keeping out repeat offenders. Romanian Ambassador Ion Jinga stressed that Romania does not tolerate crime and maintains one of Europe’s lowest crime rates. Local leaders, including Susan Hall from Harrow Council, are concerned about the unknown scale of migration and the challenge of meeting increased demand for local services, noting that related issues are now affecting suburban as well as inner-city communities.

Amber Deanna Stanley, a 17-year-old honors student from Kettering, Maryland, was tragically shot and killed in her own bed during a home invasion late Wednesday night. According to Prince George's County police, a male suspect forcibly entered the Stanley home around 10:30 p.m. and shot Amber multiple times. Her 37-year-old sister, the sister's young daughter, and a 17-year-old foster sister were also at home during the attack but were unharmed.

Police are actively canvassing the neighborhood and have offered a $25,000 reward for information leading to an arrest. The motive remains unknown, and the investigation is ongoing.

Amber was a high-achieving student at Charles H. Flowers High School, where she aspired to study medicine at Harvard University. School principal Gorman Brown described her as an outstanding and well-liked student who was active in the school community.

Neighbors expressed shock and sadness over the incident, noting recent unusual activity and increased traffic in the normally quiet area. Prior to the shooting, police responded to the Stanley home on August 17 regarding an assault report; no arrests were made, and it is unclear if the cases are connected.

The Prince George's County Public Schools community is mourning Amber's death, condemning the senseless violence and offering condolences to her family. Police are urging anyone with information to come forward.

article_content: Researchers from Britain and Japan have succeeded in reverting human stem cells to a very early, embryonic-like stage. This significant milestone may help develop new therapies for currently incurable conditions, including heart and eye diseases, Parkinson's disease, and stroke recovery. The team reset the stem cells to mimic those in embryos roughly 7 to 10 days post-fertilization, which is before the embryo implants in the womb. This completely 'blank slate' status is crucial for scientists studying the earliest stages of human development—periods that are otherwise inaccessible for direct observation and may hold answers to miscarriages and developmental disorders. Austin Smith, director of the Cambridge Stem Cell Institute, described these cells as representing the true beginning of tissue formation in humans. He noted this approach could eventually reveal key insights into early development biology. Although human pluripotent stem cells can already be made from embryos or by reprogramming adult cells, producing cells in the most pristine, early state has proven challenging. Unlike mouse cells, which can be preserved in an early stage using a protein called LIF, human stem cells require different genetic manipulation to achieve this state. To resolve this, the researchers induced two genes—NANOG and KLF2—that together triggered the cells to return to an earlier and more flexible condition. The work, led by Austin Smith with Yasuhiro Takashima from the Japan Science and Technology Agency, was published in the journal Cell. Takashima emphasized the need for follow-up research to determine how these reset cells compare to existing stem cells for use in therapies and whether starting entirely from scratch might be beneficial. Chris Mason, a regenerative medicine expert from University College London who was not involved in the study, praised the breakthrough. He highlighted the importance of having access to such pristine stem cells for generating clinically relevant cell types, predicting this advancement could make cell therapies safer and more affordable for both patients and healthcare providers.
translated_content: Naukowcy z Wielkiej Brytanii i Japonii skutecznie przywrócili ludzkie komórki macierzyste do bardzo wczesnego, zarodkowego stanu. To przełomowe osiągnięcie może przyczynić się do opracowania nowych terapii obecnie nieuleczalnych chorób, takich jak schorzenia serca i oczu, choroba Parkinsona lub udar. Zespół naukowców odtworzył komórki macierzyste tak, by przypominały te występujące w zarodkach około 7–10 dni po zapłodnieniu, czyli jeszcze przed zagnieżdżeniem się w macicy. Takie „czyste” komórki mają kluczowe znaczenie dla badań nad najwcześniejszymi etapami rozwoju człowieka—czasu niedostępnego do bezpośredniej obserwacji, który może skrywać przyczyny poronień czy zaburzeń rozwojowych. Austin Smith, dyrektor Cambridge Stem Cell Institute, opisał te komórki jako prawdziwy początek formowania tkanek u ludzi, dodając, że to podejście może kiedyś odsłonić nowe fakty o biologii wczesnego rozwoju. Chociaż teraz możliwe jest pozyskanie pluripotencjalnych komórek macierzystych z zarodków lub reprogramowanych komórek dorosłych, uzyskanie komórek w najczystszym, początkowym stanie było dotąd dużym wyzwaniem. W odróżnieniu od komórek myszy, które można utrzymać na wczesnym etapie dzięki białku LIF, ludzkie komórki wymagają innego podejścia genetycznego. Aby to osiągnąć, naukowcy wprowadzili geny NANOG oraz KLF2, które wspólnie spowodowały powrót komórek do wcześniejszego, elastycznego stadium. Prace prowadzone przez Austina Smitha i Yasuhiro Takashima z Japan Science and Technology Agency opisano na łamach czasopisma Cell. Takashima podkreślił, że potrzebne są kolejne badania porównujące odtworzone komórki z istniejącymi typami i oceniające, czy takie „czyste” komórki sprawdzą się lepiej w przyszłych terapiach. Chris Mason, ekspert medycyny regeneracyjnej z University College London, który nie był zaangażowany w badania, pochwalił wyniki. article_content: New Jersey Governor Chris Christie has undergone significant weight loss since his Lap-Band surgery in February 2013. Though he hasn’t publicly mentioned the exact number, experts say photos suggest he’s dropped at least 100 pounds. Dr. Jaime Ponce, a bariatric surgery expert, praised Christie’s progress and described the change as very impressive. Christie, who has dealt with weight challenges for many years, chose the surgery with his long-term health and family in mind. His transformation has led to speculation about his potential candidacy in the 2016 presidential race, but Christie hasn’t confirmed any plans. Lap-Band surgery is a minimally invasive procedure that places an adjustable band around the upper stomach, creating a smaller pouch to slow down eating. The procedure is relatively brief with a short recovery, but possible risks include blockages, slippage, swallowing problems, infection, and nutrition deficits. Christie has spoken openly about his weight struggles and the emotional toll they have taken, highlighting misunderstandings some people have about obesity. After his surgery, his doctor confirmed he adopted a healthier lifestyle, including a better diet and consistent exercise involving both cardio and strength training.

article_content: You can enjoy the holidays without overspending. A new Forbes Advisor survey found that 36% of Americans expect to spend more this holiday season than last year. According to a National Retail Federation survey, consumers plan to spend an average of $875 on gifts, decorations, food, and other seasonal items this year.  Here are six holiday tips, learned as a financial coach, to help you spread joy without breaking the bank:  1) Prioritize Your Top 5 Holiday Wishes When deciding your holiday budget, write down everything you want to do between now and the new year. Then pick your five most important priorities and rank them. This way, if you need to adjust your budget, you know what to fund first. For example, if visiting family is your priority, you might trim your gift budget and use those funds for a New Year’s Eve trip with loved ones. The key is to plan ahead for what and who matters most.  2) Get Feedback on Last Year’s Holiday Spending Ask loved ones if they enjoyed their gifts last year, or if there were any 'one and done' gifts—items that aren’t needed again. If someone says they don’t want anything, believe them. Some people prefer not to receive extra items or gifts that pressure them to reciprocate. Also, check with your family about traveling. About 48% of Americans intend to travel over the holidays, according to a 2023 Deloitte survey. It’s okay for your family to skip travel if last year was exhausting. Before planning, consider last year’s spending and if you want to celebrate the same way again.  3) Buy Gifts Using the $1 Rule The $1 rule is simple to start now: Only buy gifts that cost $1 or less per expected use. For example, if you’re buying a $20 toy or item, will the recipient use it at least 20 times? If not, choose items that will be truly appreciated and used. This rule helps prevent impulse buys and encourages mindful gifting.  4) Challenge Yourself to a Zero-Based Decorating Budget It’s easy to overspend trying to make your home look perfect. Instead, find festive decorating ideas that cost nothing and use items you already have. You can still create a cheerful atmosphere without buying new décor.  5) Plan Meals by Bites, Not Dishes Holiday leftovers are common, but often we prepare more than needed. From catering experience, 15 bites of food per guest is plenty for a complete meal—a few bites each of protein, sides, and dessert. This saves money and prevents overeating. For 10 guests, plan around 150 bites total, across several dishes. Consider smaller portions of desserts to reduce waste, and think carefully about how much food you’ll really need—including for leftovers.  6) Find a Holiday Budget Partner Now Whether you’re with loved ones for Thanksgiving or later, find a trusted partner to help keep each other on budget this holiday season. Set spending goals together and check in on your progress. Choose someone supportive who will give honest feedback and help you stay financially mindful. Having a partner makes holiday budgeting less stressful and more encouraging.

Ta zasada chroni przed impulsywnymi zakupami i pomaga przemyśleć wybór prezentów.  4) Zdecyduj się na zerowy budżet na dekoracje Łatwo przesadzić, próbując ozdobić dom jak z magazynu. Postaw na pomysłowe dekoracje z rzeczy, które już masz i które nic nie kosztują. W ten sposób uzyskasz świąteczny nastrój bez wydawania pieniędzy na nowe ozdoby.  5) Planuj świąteczne posiłki, licząc porcje zamiast dań Po świętach często zostaje mnóstwo jedzenia. Z doświadczenia w cateringu wiem, że 15 kęsów na osobę to wystarczająca ilość na pełny posiłek – po kilka kęsów białka, dodatków oraz deseru. To pozwala oszczędzić pieniądze i uniknąć przejedzenia. Dla 10 osób zaplanuj około 150 kęsów, rozdzielonych na różne dania. Mniejsze porcje deserów zmniejszą marnowanie jedzenia, więc przemyśl, ile naprawdę potrzebujesz – także na ewentualne resztki.  6) Znajdź świątecznego partnera budżetowego Jeśli spotykasz się z rodziną lub przyjaciółmi podczas Święta Dziękczynienia albo później, wybierz zaufaną osobę, z którą możecie się wspólnie pilnować budżetu. Ustalcie wspólny cel wydatków i regularnie sprawdzajcie postępy. Wybierz kogoś, kto udziela wsparcia i szczerze doradzi, a nie oceni. Partner budżetowy sprawia, że planowanie i oszczędzanie w święta jest łatwiejsze i mniej stresujące.

article_content: KABUL: Amid ongoing concerns about illegal immigration, approximately 450,000 Afghan migrants have voluntarily returned to Afghanistan from Iran, according to Khaama Press, which cited local Iranian media reports. Javad Khani, the official responsible for managing illegal migrants at the National Organisation for Migration in Iran, told Tasnim News Agency that there may be around four million illegal migrants currently living in the country. Khani stated that eight major cities in Iran—Tehran, Sistan and Balochistan, Khorasan Razavi, Qom, Kerman, Yazd, Fars, and Alborz—are home to 92 percent of the country's illegal Afghan migrants. Tasnim News Agency is a semi-official news outlet in Iran associated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. According to Khaama Press, citing Iranian media, at least one million illegal Afghan migrants in Iran have now received identity cards. Khani added that the majority of migrants in Iran are from Afghanistan, and new initiatives are underway to register those lacking documentation. Recently, Afghan refugees in Iran have expressed concerns about increased deportations, arrests, and police harassment, reports TOLO News. The Taliban has urged neighboring countries not to deport Afghan refugees. While deportations of Afghan refugees from Pakistan have escalated, Iran has also begun to enforce forced deportations. Afghan refugee representatives in Iran have criticized both the Iranian government and the international community for insufficient support, calling for greater assistance to address the challenges faced by Afghan refugees. "Afghan refugees are being deported from Iran. The Iranian people and government are very oppressive towards refugees. Iran pushes out refugees ahead of winter, which is not right," said Spogmai Jabbarkhil, an Afghan refugee representative in Iran, as quoted by TOLO News.

article_content: Sabeer Nelliparamban is the Founder and CEO of Zil Money Corporation, Online Check Writer, and Tyler Petroleum Inc. The financial sector is undergoing rapid transformation thanks to fintech, with significant implications for financial inclusion. By leveraging technology, fintech companies are making it easier for underbanked and unbanked populations to access essential financial services—something traditional banks have struggled to achieve on their own. This democratization of access is closing longstanding gaps and revitalizing the financial landscape, particularly for underserved communities. Fintech’s Role in Expanding Financial Inclusion Understanding fintech from a business perspective reveals how these innovations increase access to banking while maintaining profitability. Fintech companies are tasked with developing new solutions that help consumers and sustain viable business models. According to the Federal Reserve, in 2021, 13% of Americans lacked essential banking services, and 5% had no banking services at all. Fintech promises to change this reality by making financial services more affordable and accessible, as highlighted in a 2023 United Nations report that notes how digital solutions like direct deposits can reduce costs such as check-cashing fees. Bridging the Financial Divide Fintech is not replacing traditional banks but enhancing them. Statista reports a rise in collaborations between banks and fintech firms from 2020 to 2021, signaling a mutually beneficial relationship. Traditional banks offer trust and stability, while fintech brings innovation and efficiency. Together, they can lower barriers to entry, making financial services available to more consumers. For example, some U.S. households spend over $150 a year on check-cashing, with total costs for the unbanked and underbanked reaching as high as $3,000 annually. Fintech-driven digital solutions, such as direct transfers, present new options for these groups. Far from replacing banks, fintech is poised to complement established banking institutions. This partnership leverages banks’ reputations for stability and fintech’s ability to introduce agile, streamlined offerings, thereby improving overall access. Fintech’s data-driven methods can serve people with little or no credit history, making risk assessment more precise and tailored financial products more widely available. This empowers individuals and startups to participate more actively in the economy. Empowering Inclusion Through Fintech Leadership Fintech leaders play a key role in advancing inclusion by focusing on accessible design, digital education, and supportive policies. Collaboration between fintech firms and banks can help close persistent access gaps, bringing creative, equitable solutions to marginalized communities. Organizations such as the Centre for Strategic and International Studies stress the importance of digital literacy, infrastructure, and governance to ensure technology delivers on its inclusive promise. Fintech’s Future: Toward a Fairer Financial System Fintech promises not only more convenient and accessible transactions, but also fosters financial literacy by simplifying complex concepts and offering user-friendly platforms. Sabeer Nelliparamban’s own entrepreneurial journey demonstrates this: initially developing financial management software for personal use, then scaling it into a public product addressing diverse needs and making financial management more inclusive. While non-finance entrepreneurs entering fintech face obstacles—such as regulatory compliance, competition, and funding—they also drive innovation and fresh perspectives. With the right support, they can help make the sector even more user-centric and open to all. Conclusion: Fintech as an Engine of Equality Fintech is more than a trend—it is a catalyst for inclusion, efficiency, and resilience in the financial world. Through further innovation and close cooperation with established banks, fintech can help make the financial system more accessible and equitable for everyone. Zgodnie z danymi Rezerwy Federalnej z 2021 r., 13% Amerykanów nie miało podstawowych usług bankowych, a 5% nie korzystało z żadnych usług bankowych. Fintech ma zmienić tę rzeczywistość, czyniąc usługi finansowe tańszymi i łatwiej dostępnymi, co podkreśla raport ONZ z 2023 r., wskazując, że cyfrowe rozwiązania, takie jak bezpośrednie przelewy, obniżają takie koszty jak opłaty za realizację czeków. Zasypywanie przepaści finansowej Fintech nie zastępuje tradycyjnych banków, lecz je wzmacnia. Według Statista, od 2020 do 2021 roku wzrosła liczba współprac między bankami i firmami fintech, co pokazuje, że obie strony korzystają na tej relacji. Tradycyjne banki zapewniają zaufanie i stabilność, a fintech wnosi innowacyjność i efektywność. Razem mogą zmniejszyć bariery wejścia, udostępniając usługi finansowe większej liczbie osób. Przykładowo, niektóre amerykańskie gospodarstwa domowe wydają ponad 150 dolarów rocznie na realizację czeków, a całkowite koszty dla osób wykluczonych lub niedostatecznie obsługiwanych mogą sięgnąć nawet 3 000 dolarów rocznie. Cyfrowe rozwiązania oparte na fintechu, takie jak bezpośrednie przelewy, dają nowe możliwości tym grupom. Fintech nie zastąpi banków, lecz je uzupełni, korzystając z ich renomy oraz wprowadzając zwinne, usprawnione usługi i zwiększając tym samym ogólny dostęp. Dzięki analizie danych fintech może obsługiwać osoby z niską historią kredytową lub bez niej, co pozwala na lepszą ocenę ryzyka i oferowanie dopasowanych produktów finansowych. To wzmacnia pozycję osób indywidualnych i start-upów, umożliwiając im aktywniejszy udział w gospodarce. Włączanie przez liderów fintech Liderzy branży fintech odgrywają kluczową rolę w rozwoju włączenia poprzez projektowanie dostępnych rozwiązań, edukację cyfrową oraz wspieranie sprzyjających polityk. Współpraca firm fintech i banków pomaga zasypywać luki w dostępie, tworząc innowacyjne i sprawiedliwe rozwiązania dla społeczności marginalizowanych. Takie organizacje jak Centrum Studiów Strategicznych i Międzynarodowych podkreślają znaczenie kompetencji cyfrowych, infrastruktury i ładu, by technologia faktycznie wspierała równość finansową. Przyszłość fintechu – ku sprawiedliwszemu systemowi finansowemu Fintech to nie tylko wygodniejsze i bardziej dostępne transakcje, ale też promowanie wiedzy finansowej — upraszczanie trudnych pojęć i oferowanie przyjaznych platform. Przykładem jest droga przedsiębiorcza Sabeera Nelliparambana, który stworzył oprogramowanie do zarządzania finansami najpierw na własny użytek, a potem udostępnił je szerzej, wspierając osoby z różnych środowisk. Choć przedsiębiorcy spoza sektora finansowego wchodząc w fintech napotykają wyzwania — jak regulacje, konkurencja czy finansowanie — to wnoszą świeże spojrzenie i innowacje. Dzięki odpowiedniemu wsparciu mogą uczynić branżę jeszcze bardziej zorientowaną na użytkownika i otwartą na wszystkich. Podsumowanie: Fintech motorem równości Fintech to więcej niż trend – to siła napędowa włączenia, efektywności i odporności sektora finansowego. Dzięki innowacjom i ścisłej współpracy z uznanymi bankami fintech może sprawić, że system finansowy stanie się dostępniejszy i bardziej sprawiedliwy dla wszystkich. article_content: A recent survey by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) reveals that over half of individuals and 45% of businesses in India received income tax refunds within a month. This development has played a significant role in boosting trust in the tax department, with more than 80% of respondents citing faster refund processing as a key factor. The government’s emphasis on automating processes has contributed to this improvement; previously, refunds could take up to a year. According to the survey, which covered more than 3,500 individuals and businesses, about 88% said refunds are now processed quicker than five years ago, and 65-70% reported that wait times have decreased since last year. Additionally, 62% found the refund process 'very convenient.' However, some challenges remain. While three-fourths of individual respondents experienced no excess deduction under the Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) system, only 22% of businesses reported the same. In fact, 26% of business entities said they paid 10-20% more than their actual liability. In related news, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has directed Jakraya Sugar Ltd and its directors to refund funds collected from investors, citing non-compliance with regulatory norms. The company and its directors are also barred from participating in the securities market for three years. Separately, the Haryana Government will refund development fees totaling Rs 5.19 crore to 1,588 property owners who were charged in error. Property owners have been notified and can apply for reimbursement through the NDC portal.

To osiągnięcie znacząco zwiększyło zaufanie do urzędu skarbowego — ponad 80% respondentów wskazało, że szybsza obsługa zwrotów jest kluczowa. Skoncentrowanie się rządu na automatyzacji procesów przyczyniło się do tej poprawy; wcześniej zwroty mogły trwać nawet rok. Według badania obejmującego ponad 3500 osób fizycznych i firm, około 88% wskazuje, że zwroty są obecnie przetwarzane szybciej niż pięć lat temu, a 65-70% zauważyło skrócenie czasu oczekiwania względem ubiegłego roku. Dodatkowo, 62% uznało proces zwrotu za 'bardzo wygodny'. Jednak pozostają pewne wyzwania. O ile trzy czwarte osób fizycznych nie miało nadmiernych potrąceń w systemie Tax Deducted at Source (TDS), to tylko 22% firm zgłosiło taki brak. Aż 26% przedsiębiorstw przyznało, że zapłaciło o 10-20% więcej niż wynosił ich faktyczny obowiązek podatkowy. W innych wiadomościach, indyjski organ nadzoru finansowego SEBI nakazał firmie Jakraya Sugar Ltd oraz jej dyrektorom zwrot środków pozyskanych od inwestorów ze względu na nieprzestrzeganie regulacji. Spółka i jej zarząd zostali wykluczeni z rynku papierów wartościowych na trzy lata. Ponadto rząd stanu Haryana zwróci opłaty rozwojowe o łącznej wartości 5,19 crore rupii dla 1 588 właścicieli nieruchomości, którym błędnie je naliczono. Właściciele zostali powiadomieni i mogą ubiegać się o zwrot przez portal NDC.

article_content: Many people have experienced a fall after drinking too much, but some recent incidents at UK railway stations have been especially dangerous. Network Rail has released CCTV footage showing some of the riskiest behavior caught on camera, including a man in Leeds falling repeatedly down an escalator, and another man in Edinburgh tumbling onto the tracks after trying to kick a pigeon. One particularly frightening clip shows a passenger at Manchester Piccadilly Station leaning against a moving train before falling under a carriage onto the rails. Fortunately, he narrowly missed the wheels and survived. Network Rail released these videos as part of a safety campaign, warning passengers about the dangers of traveling after heavy drinking. In the last year, over 1,600 injuries—ranging from slips and trips to serious falls—were reported across the 17 stations managed by Network Rail, with many incidents related to alcohol. Leeds, Paddington, and Liverpool Street stations have had the highest number of passenger falls. Accidents in the past year included one fatality, 51 broken bones, 19 dislocations, five concussions, and dozens of bruises or cuts as people fell on steps, escalators, over luggage, and even off platforms. Robin Gisby, managing director of Network Rail operations, stated that while teams work hard to keep stations safe, alcohol often impairs judgment, leading to these incidents. British Transport Police Deputy Chief Constable Paul Crowther added that passengers should be more aware of their surroundings if they've been drinking, to help reduce avoidable accidents. To raise awareness, the campaign includes posters and a safety video shown at stations and on YouTube.

Aby zwiększyć świadomość zagrożeń, w ramach kampanii pojawiły się plakaty oraz film informacyjny wyświetlany na dworcach i w serwisie YouTube.

article_content: Sri Lanka’s Court of Appeal has suspended the sports minister’s decision to dismiss the country’s embattled cricket board, restoring the ousted officials pending a full hearing. The court accepted a petition from board president Shammi Silva, who challenged sports minister Roshan Ranasinghe’s move to dissolve Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) and install an interim committee. According to a court official, the restoration is temporary for two weeks, until the case is heard again. This latest development follows a months-long dispute between Ranasinghe and the SLC, Sri Lanka’s wealthiest sports organization. Ranasinghe accused the board of widespread corruption and had removed its members days after the national men’s cricket team suffered a heavy defeat against India at the World Cup. When Tuesday’s court decision was announced, members of the interim committee led by former Sri Lankan captain Arjuna Ranatunga were seen leaving SLC’s offices. Ranatunga, the skipper of the 1996 World Cup-winning team, had vowed to clean up the board and revitalize cricket in the country. On Monday, he stated, “Sri Lanka Cricket had become known as the most corrupt institution in the country. I want to change that image.” Meanwhile, the government has established a cabinet committee chaired by Foreign Minister Ali Sabry to address ongoing issues within the cricket board. The International Cricket Council (ICC), which prohibits political interference in national boards and has previously suspended Sri Lanka, has not commented on the crisis so far. Last month, Ranasinghe withdrew a three-member panel investigating the board after the ICC viewed it as interference. Recently, Ranasinghe wrote to ICC members seeking understanding, stating that Sri Lanka Cricket faces ongoing complaints of player disciplinary problems, management corruption, financial misconduct, and match-fixing allegations. He emphasized that any interim measures would be taken only to establish good governance. Sri Lanka has not won the World Cup since 1996. Ranasinghe blamed the board for the decline in standards. In 2019, then-sports minister Harin Fernando introduced strict anti-corruption laws after the ICC identified Sri Lanka as one of the most corrupt cricketing countries.

Sąd przyjął petycję prezesa zarządu, Shammi Silvy, który zakwestionował posunięcie ministra sportu, Roshana Ranasinghe, mające na celu rozwiązanie Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) i powołanie komitetu tymczasowego. To najnowsza odsłona wielomiesięcznego sporu między Ranasinghe a SLC, najbogatszą organizacją sportową w kraju. Ranasinghe oskarżył zarząd o powszechną korupcję i usunął jego członków kilka dni po tym, jak męska reprezentacja Sri Lanki przegrała wysoko z Indiami na mistrzostwach świata. Międzynarodowa Rada Krykieta (ICC), która zabrania ingerencji politycznej w krajowe zarządy i wcześniej zawieszała Sri Lankę, na razie nie skomentowała kryzysu. W zeszłym miesiącu Ranasinghe wycofał trzyosobową komisję badającą zarząd po tym, jak ICC uznało to za ingerencję. Niedawno Ranasinghe napisał do członków ICC z prośbą o zrozumienie - stwierdził, że Sri Lanka Cricket boryka się z licznymi skargami dotyczącymi problemów dyscyplinarnych zawodników, korupcji kierownictwa, nadużyć finansowych i podejrzeń o ustawianie meczów. Podkreślił, że ewentualne środki tymczasowe zostaną wprowadzone wyłącznie w celu zapewnienia zasad dobrej administracji. Sri Lanka nie wygrała Mistrzostw Świata od 1996 roku. Ranasinghe obwinia zarząd za spadek poziomu. W 2019 roku ówczesny minister sportu, Harin Fernando, wprowadził surowe przepisy antykorupcyjne po tym, jak ICC określiło Sri Lankę jako jeden z najbardziej skorumpowanych krajów krykietowych.

article_content: Over the past three years, even leading tech companies such as Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Tesla have not consistently outperformed the S&P 500. While these stocks have delivered impressive long-term returns, beating the broader market year after year is a rare achievement. Experienced investors and portfolio managers widely acknowledge the difficulty of consistently surpassing the S&P 500, particularly given the unusual market conditions of the last three years—including the global pandemic, unprecedented stimulus and near-zero interest rates, ongoing geopolitical conflicts, soaring inflation, and a period of aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes. In this challenging context, the Trefis high-quality (HQ) portfolio, launched in September 2020 during the height of the pandemic, reports outperforming the S&P 500 by more than 1,000 basis points over the past three years. HQ has reportedly beaten the S&P 500 each year since its inception, including its partial first year in 2020 and each subsequent year through 2023. The team expresses a willingness to learn from others who have achieved similar consistency. The HQ portfolio's success is attributed to sticking to core investment principles—focusing on stocks with strong revenue growth, profitability, disciplined balance sheets, and reasonable valuations. The Trefis team acknowledges the persistent challenge of following these fundamentals, especially given temptations to pursue popular growth stocks or ignore financial discipline. Their methodology is systematic, data-driven, and pragmatic. Empirical, a Boston-based firm, provides opportunities for interested investors to learn more about HQ and additional Trefis strategies. A key insight from Trefis is the value gained from blending human expertise with AI-driven analysis. Since 2019, they have developed the thinkHub platform, which employs advanced analytics while prioritizing transparency and auditability. Their philosophy, termed 'Understandable-AI,' centers on integrating lessons learned from machine analytics back into the system for continuous improvement, rather than merely depending on opaque, black-box algorithms. The investment approach makes use of quantitative peer comparisons and careful consideration of macroeconomic factors—such as the continuing economic impacts of COVID-19 and rising inflation. This forms what they call a 'multi-lens system,' enabling analysis from multiple perspectives. Building on this foundation, Trefis has expanded to include other strategies, such as the Bayesian and Reinforced Value portfolios. The latter is designed as a hedged strategy against market-specific risks. Still, they recognize that even robust strategies with a high probability of annual outperformance face real challenges maintaining consistency over multiple years. Looking forward, Trefis plans to broaden their data sources and improve thinkHub's transparency and user-friendliness, particularly for non-technical users. Their overarching aim is to maintain a culture that fosters collaborative learning between humans and machines to build resilient investment strategies. For those interested in further details or considering investments in Trefis strategies, direct inquiries are encouraged.

W tych trudnych warunkach portfel Trefis high-quality (HQ), uruchomiony we wrześniu 2020 r. w szczycie pandemii, deklaruje przewagę nad S&P 500 o ponad 1000 punktów bazowych w ciągu trzech lat. Zgodnie z informacjami Trefis, HQ pokonał S&P 500 w każdym roku swojej działalności, począwszy od częściowego roku 2020 i w kolejnych latach aż do 2023. Zespół Trefis podkreśla, jak trudno konsekwentnie przestrzegać tych zasad, zwłaszcza gdy kuszą modne spółki wzrostowe, a dyscyplina finansowa jest czasem ignorowana. Ich metodologia jest systematyczna, oparta na danych i pragmatyczna. Firma Empirical z Bostonu oferuje zainteresowanym możliwość zgłębienia szczegółów portfela HQ oraz innych strategii Trefis. Ich filozofia, nazwana 'Understandable-AI', opiera się na ciągłym doskonaleniu systemu dzięki wnioskom płynącym z analityki maszynowej, zamiast polegania wyłącznie na tzw. 'czarnej skrzynce'. Podejście inwestycyjne obejmuje porównania z konkurentami poprzez analizę ilościową oraz wnikliwe uwzględnianie czynników makroekonomicznych – takich jak utrzymujące się skutki gospodarcze COVID-19 czy rosnąca inflacja. Tworzy to tzw. 'system wielosoczewkowy', który pozwala analizować inwestycje z wielu perspektyw. W oparciu o to podejście Trefis wdraża kolejne strategie, takie jak portfele Bayesian i Reinforced Value – ten ostatni zaprojektowany jest jako strategia zabezpieczająca przed specyficznymi ryzykami rynkowymi. Zespół zdaje sobie jednak sprawę, że nawet bardzo dobre strategie o wysokim prawdopodobieństwie rocznego sukcesu mają trudności w utrzymaniu konsekwencji przez wiele lat. Patrząc w przyszłość, Trefis zamierza poszerzać źródła danych i poprawiać przejrzystość oraz łatwość obsługi platformy thinkHub, zwłaszcza dla osób nietechnicznych. article_content: Emily Cunningham, a stay-at-home mother in Charlotte, NC, manages the complex needs of her children’s severe food allergies every day. Her four-year-old daughter, Elena, is allergic to eggs, tree nuts, dairy, and peanuts, while her eight-month-old son, Wyatt, has a serious dairy allergy. Even brief contact with these allergens can trigger life-threatening reactions. To protect their children, the Cunninghams keep their home completely free of allergens, only purchasing foods they know are safe. This vigilance comes with a steep price—the family spends about $1,000 monthly on allergy-related medications and supplies, like epinephrine injectors, and an additional $80 each month on rice milk. The issue isn’t unique to them. Food allergies now impact an estimated 4% to 6% of children in the U.S., and the number appears to be rising. Some experts suggest that increased hygiene and delayed introduction of certain foods may be contributing factors. According to a recent JAMA Pediatrics report, caring for children with food allergies costs the nation about $25 billion each year. Around $4,184 is spent annually per child, covering both direct medical expenses and indirect costs such as specialized foods, lost income, and childcare. These figures are much higher than past estimates, which often overlooked many personal and out-of-pocket expenses. Many families, including the Cunninghams, experience career changes as a result. Emily left her job as a speech therapist to focus on her children’s safety, and her husband shifted careers to develop technology that supports families managing allergies. Policy efforts could help. Some lawmakers have proposed bills to encourage schools to stock and administer epinephrine, aiming to make public spaces safer and reduce emergency costs. Future advances in treatments might significantly ease the burden on families. Oral immunotherapy—gradually introducing allergens—could help protect children from severe reactions, and new, more accessible epinephrine injectors are also reducing costs. Emily reports that as demand increases, families are seeing more products become available and more competition, which is helping with pricing and choices.

article_content: Wales have made a remarkable turnaround and now stand on the verge of an unexpected place in the Rugby World Cup semi-finals, but must first overcome a formidable Argentina side searching for form in France. The two teams will face off in Marseille, kicking off an intriguing weekend of World Cup knockout action, with both sides holding credible ambitions of advancing to the next stage. Earlier this year, Wales struggled in the Six Nations and dealt with significant off-field issues regarding players' contracts. Since then, they have reversed their fortunes, finishing top of their World Cup group. Notable victories include a convincing 40-6 win over Australia and a dramatic opening win against Fiji in Pool C. Whether Wales' campaign would have changed if Fiji had not dropped the ball in the closing moments of their match is still a matter for debate. However, coach Warren Gatland is satisfied with his unbeaten squad’s momentum heading into the quarter-finals. "We haven't had the perfect performance yet, but we’ve shown we're tough to beat," Gatland said on Thursday. "This squad has plenty more to give, both collectively and individually, and we’re eager for Saturday’s clash in Marseille." Argentina, too, believe they can raise their level, having narrowly qualified for the last eight. The two-time semi-finalists did not get past the group stage four years ago and appeared at risk of repeating that after losing to England in their Pool D opener. They bounced back last weekend with a see-saw victory over Japan in a win-or-go-home contest. Pumas coach Michael Cheika reflected on the team’s progress over the past two years: "Everything we’ve worked on will help us feel ready for this game," he said Thursday. Cheika has made bold selections, including calling up the injury-prone scrumhalf Tomas Cubelli and reworking the forward trio following Pablo Matera’s injury, which ended his tournament. Wales have made their own adjustments after Taulupe Faletau suffered a broken arm last week. Encouragingly, flyhalf Dan Biggar, a previous match-winner, returns from a pectoral injury, providing a big boost for Wales. Wales have won both previous Rugby World Cup encounters with Argentina and were also 20-13 victors when the two sides met in Cardiff last November.

article_content: Climate change is making the underwater world increasingly noisy, according to new research published in the journal PeerJ. The study, led by NIOZ oceanographer Luca Possenti, finds that in some locations, sounds from ships could be five times louder by the end of this century. The research combined mathematical simulations with partners at Utrecht University and TNO, using both moderate and extreme climate scenarios developed by the UN’s climate panel (IPCC). In the ocean, both water temperature and acidity affect how sound travels. As greenhouse gas emissions continue, oceans are becoming warmer and more acidic, causing underwater sounds to carry farther in most regions. Specifically, the study highlights the northern Atlantic Ocean, where declining inflows of warmer surface water are expected to change underwater temperature layers. This shift could create a unique 'sound channel' near the surface, acting like a tunnel that allows noise to travel greater distances. Possenti explains that, under a moderate climate scenario, this could raise underwater sound levels in the North Atlantic by 7 decibels by century’s end—almost five times the noise energy. Increased noise levels will come not just from more ships, but also from sources such as air guns used in seismic surveys. Researchers warn that even under moderate climate change scenarios, the rise in underwater noise could be severe. Possenti emphasizes the impact on marine life: since underwater visibility is low, many fish and marine mammals rely on sound to communicate and sense predators. Increased noise could disrupt communication and threaten entire ecosystems. To bolster the study’s predictions, Possenti and teams from TNO and MARIN are also conducting real-world measurements. Using breaking glass spheres, they produce sounds at the volumes used by deep-diving marine mammals, recording how far the noise travels—sometimes tens to hundreds of kilometers. Understanding exactly how underwater conditions affect sound speed and travel is ongoing work. However, given the potentially major impacts on marine ecosystems, gaining this knowledge is seen as essential for predicting climate change effects on ocean life.

Zespół badawczy pod kierownictwem oceanografa NIOZ, Luci Possentiego, ustalił, że w niektórych miejscach dźwięki pochodzące od statków mogą być nawet pięć razy głośniejsze do końca tego wieku. Badania opierały się na modelowaniu matematycznym we współpracy z Uniwersytetem w Utrechcie i TNO, wykorzystując umiarkowane i ekstremalne scenariusze klimatyczne opracowane przez panel ONZ ds. klimatu (IPCC). W oceanach temperatura wody i jej kwasowość wpływają na to, jak rozchodzą się dźwięki. Wraz z rosnącą emisją gazów cieplarnianych ocean staje się cieplejszy i bardziej kwaśny, co powoduje, że dźwięk rozchodzi się na większe odległości w większości regionów. Badacze szczególnie zwracają uwagę na północny Atlantyk, gdzie spodziewany spadek napływu cieplejszej wody powierzchniowej zmienia podwodne warstwy temperaturowe. Może to doprowadzić do powstania unikalnego 'kanału dźwiękowego' bliżej powierzchni oceanu, działającego jak tunel, przez który hałas będzie niósł się dalej. Possenti wyjaśnia, że w scenariuszu umiarkowanego ocieplenia do końca wieku poziom dźwięków pod wodą w północnym Atlantyku może wzrosnąć o 7 decybeli, czyli niemal pięciokrotnie podnieść energię akustyczną. Wyższy poziom hałasu będzie wynikał nie tylko ze wzrostu ruchu statków, lecz także z innych źródeł, takich jak pistolety powietrzne wykorzystywane w badaniach sejsmicznych. Naukowcy ostrzegają, że nawet przy umiarkowanych zmianach klimatu wzrost hałasu pod wodą może być poważny. Possenti podkreśla wpływ na życie morskie: ze względu na ograniczoną widoczność pod wodą, wiele gatunków ryb i ssaków morskich polega na dźwięku, aby się komunikować oraz wykrywać drapieżniki. Większy hałas może ten kontakt utrudnić i zagrozić całym ekosystemom. Aby potwierdzić prognozy modelowe, Possenti wraz z zespołami z TNO i MARIN prowadzi także pomiary w rzeczywistych warunkach. Dzięki tłuczonym szklanym kulom generują dźwięki o poziomach stosowanych przez głęboko nurkujące ssaki morskie, a następnie sprawdzają, jak daleko się one niosą — czasem nawet na setki kilometrów. Badania nad tym, jak dokładnie warunki pod wodą wpływają na prędkość i zasięg dźwięku, wciąż trwają. Jednak ze względu na potencjalnie duży wpływ na ekosystemy morskie, zdobycie tej wiedzy jest kluczowe, by przewidzieć skutki zmian klimatu dla życia w oceanach.

article_content: The 2023 Trace Awards were held in Kigali, Rwanda on Saturday, October 21, celebrating achievements in African and global music. Nigerian superstars Davido and Rema emerged as some of the night’s biggest winners. Rema took home two awards: ‘Song of the Year’ for his hit ‘Calm Down’ and ‘Best Global African Artiste,’ an honor he shares with South African singer Nomcebo Zikode. Davido also won two key categories, ‘Best Male’ and ‘Best Collaboration’ for his track ‘Unavailable’ with Musa Keys of South Africa. Burna Boy clinched the prestigious ‘Album of the Year’ award for his project ‘Love Damini.’ Other notable winners across diverse categories included Viviane Chidid (Best Female), Asake (Best Artist Africa – Anglophone), Didi B (Best Artist Africa – Francophone), Lisandro Cuxi (Best Artist Africa – Lusophone), Fally Ipupa (Best Live), Yemi Alade (Best Music Video for ‘Baddie’), Robot Boii (Best Dancer), Michael Brun (Best DJ), Tam Sir (Best Producer), and KS Bloom (Best Gospel Artist). The event highlighted the dynamic range of talent from across Africa and beyond, underscoring the continued global impact of African music.
