article_content: ASEAN is urging India to become part of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), seeing India’s involvement as a way to increase economic integration and market opportunities for all members. ASEAN Secretary-General Dr. Kao Kim Hourn highlighted the inclusiveness and potential benefits of this rule-based trade agreement. RCEP, which launched in November 2020, includes ten Southeast Asian nations as well as China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, and New Zealand. Together, these countries account for around 30% of global GDP and population. Although India was involved in the negotiations, it chose to withdraw due to fears of negative economic impacts. Dr. Kao pointed out that ASEAN and India already collaborate across sectors like space, investment, tourism, defense, and counter-terrorism, and suggested expanding their partnership into new fields such as biotech, public health, renewable energy, digital economies, and better connectivity. At the recent ASEAN summit in Jakarta, Prime Minister Narendra Modi reaffirmed India’s commitment to ASEAN’s central role in regional affairs, introducing a 12-point proposal to enhance cooperation in areas like connectivity, trade, and digital transformation. ASEAN has called for a more liberal aviation pact to allow more direct flights between India and Southeast Asia, aiming to strengthen tourism and interpersonal ties. Regarding international issues, Dr. Kao restated ASEAN’s dedication to resolving conflicts through dialogue and diplomacy, and stressed the importance of the United Nations, citing ongoing conflicts such as Israel-Palestine. The relationship between India and ASEAN has steadily deepened since 1992, evolving from sectoral dialogues to a comprehensive strategic partnership established last year. In domestic news, Indian authorities have stepped up tax enforcement against social media-based retailers for large-scale evasion, accompanied by broader compliance investigations under GST regulations. Separately, industrialist Gautam Singhania faces accusations of assault from his estranged wife, Nawaz Modi.
translated_content: ASEAN namawia Indie do przystąpienia do Regionalnego Wszechstronnego Partnerstwa Gospodarczego (RCEP), postrzegając to jako szansę na większą integrację gospodarczą i nowe możliwości rynkowe dla wszystkich członków. Sekretarz generalny ASEAN, dr Kao Kim Hourn, podkreśla inkluzywność i potencjalne korzyści płynące z tej opartej na zasadach umowy handlowej. RCEP, podpisane w listopadzie 2020 roku, skupia dziesięć krajów Azji Południowo-Wschodniej wraz z Chinami, Japonią, Koreą Południową, Australią i Nową Zelandią. Razem stanowią około 30% światowego PKB i ludności. Indie brały udział w negocjacjach, lecz ostatecznie wycofały się z obaw o skutki gospodarcze. Dr Kao zaznaczył, że ASEAN i Indie współpracują już w obszarach takich jak kosmos, inwestycje, turystyka, obrona i zwalczanie terroryzmu, sugerując rozszerzenie partnerstwa o biotechnologię, zdrowie publiczne, energię odnawialną, gospodarkę cyfrową i lepszą łączność. Podczas ostatniego szczytu ASEAN w Dżakarcie premier Indii, Narendra Modi, potwierdził wsparcie Indii dla kluczowej roli ASEAN w regionie, przedstawiając 12-punktową propozycję rozszerzenia współpracy w zakresie łączności, handlu i transformacji cyfrowej. ASEAN zaproponował także liberalizację porozumień lotniczych, co umożliwiłoby więcej bezpośrednich lotów między Indiami a krajami Azji Południowo-Wschodniej, wspierając turystykę i kontakty międzyludzkie. W kwestiach międzynarodowych dr Kao ponownie podkreślił zaangażowanie ASEAN na rzecz rozwiązywania konfliktów przez dialog i dyplomację oraz rolę ONZ, wskazując na aktualne konflikty, takie jak izraelsko-palestyński. Partnerstwo Indii i ASEAN pogłębia się od 1992 roku, przechodząc od dialogu sektorowego do ustanowienia strategicznego partnerstwa kompleksowego w zeszłym roku. W wiadomościach krajowych indyjskie władze zintensyfikowały kontrole podatkowe wobec sprzedawców korzystających z mediów społecznościowych, ujawniając masowe unikanie zobowiązań podatkowych oraz prowadząc szeroko zakrojone postępowania w ramach przepisów GST. Osobno, przemysłowiec Gautam Singhania został oskarżony przez swoją byłą żonę, Nawaz Modi, o przemoc fizyczną.

Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has called on Nigerian youth to lead the campaign against climate change and champion the transition to a green economy. Speaking at the Presidential Youth Retreat themed 'Contributing To Green Economy' at the Youth Development Centre in Abeokuta, Ogun State, Obasanjo encouraged young people to reject the idea that they are only leaders of tomorrow, emphasizing that they are, in fact, leaders of today. He urged them to actively confront and overcome any obstacles preventing them from showcasing their leadership skills.

Obasanjo highlighted the negative impacts of climate change, resulting from carbon dioxide emissions, citing abnormal weather patterns, extreme temperatures, flooding, and droughts among the concerning outcomes. He stressed that these challenges require united action to halt their progression. Obasanjo stated, 'Climate change is real, even though some people may still deny its existence. We have witnessed its effects through floods, droughts, and extreme weather conditions.'

He noted that scientific findings have shown human activities have disrupted the balance of nature—including forests, hills, valleys, and wildlife—which has led to significant environmental imbalances. Obasanjo warned that the same people responsible for this disruption would also suffer its consequences, such as rising sea levels, food insecurity, and further extreme weather events. He concluded by affirming that the best way to address climate change is to adopt a green economy—committed to reducing carbon emissions and increasing green spaces through sustainable practices.

Podczas Prezydenckiego Retreatu Młodzieżowego pod hasłem „Wkład w Zieloną Gospodarkę” w Centrum Rozwoju Młodzieży w Abeokucie (stan Ogun), Obasanjo zachęcił młodych ludzi, by odrzucili przekonanie, iż są przywódcami dopiero jutra – podkreślił, że są nimi już dziś. Wezwał ich, by aktywnie przełamywali wszelkie bariery uniemożliwiające im pokazanie swojego przywództwa.

Obasanjo wskazał na negatywne skutki zmian klimatu spowodowanych emisją CO2: nietypowe zjawiska pogodowe, ekstremalne temperatury, powodzie czy susze. Podkreślił, że te wyzwania wymagają wspólnego działania, by ich dalszy rozwój powstrzymać. – Zmiana klimatu to rzeczywistość, choć niektórzy temu zaprzeczają. Widzieliśmy jej skutki w powodzi, suszy, ekstremalnych warunkach pogodowych – mówił.

article_content: Bobi, a purebred Rafeiro do Alentejo dog from Portugal, posed with his Guinness World Record certificates at his home in Conqueiros, central Portugal, on May 20. The world bids farewell to a remarkable canine. Bobi, the 31-year-old Portuguese dog recognized as the oldest dog ever, died on Friday. Guinness World Records announced Bobi's passing on its website, expressing sadness at the news. Bobi was a livestock guardian dog, a breed with a typical life expectancy of 12 to 14 years. Earlier this year, he was named not only the oldest living dog but also the oldest dog ever recorded. Bobi lived to an extraordinary age of 31 years and 165 days. However, Bobi's life was almost cut short as a puppy. According to his owner, Leonel Costa, Bobi was one of four puppies born in 1992. Costa's parents decided not to keep the puppies, as the family already had enough animals. At that time, older generations sometimes buried unwanted puppies, Costa told Guinness. By chance, the parents missed Bobi, who was hidden in a wood pile. Costa and his brothers kept Bobi a secret from their parents until the dog was old enough not to be put down. Costa attributes Bobi's longevity to a calm environment in Conqueiros, free roam of the countryside, companionship with cats, and a diet of human food soaked in water to remove seasoning. In February, Guinness announced Bobi as the oldest living dog, just two weeks after naming Spike, a 23-year-old Chihuahua mix from Ohio. NPR requested information from Guinness about the current oldest living dog after Bobi's death but did not immediately receive a response. With his age, Bobi surpassed Bluey, an Australian cattle dog who lived 29 years and five months and died in 1939, becoming the oldest dog in recorded history.
translated_content: Bobi, rodowodowy pies rasy Rafeiro do Alentejo z Portugalii, pozował ze swoimi certyfikatami Rekordów Guinnessa w domu w Conqueiros, w środkowej Portugalii, 20 maja. Świat żegna niezwykłego psa. Bobi, portugalski pies w wieku 31 lat, uznany za najstarszego psa w historii, zmarł w piątek. Rekordy Guinnessa ogłosiły jego odejście na swojej stronie, wyrażając żal z powodu jego śmierci. Bobi był psem stróżującym, którego rasa zwykle żyje 12–14 lat. Wcześniej w tym roku został uznany nie tylko za najstarszego żyjącego psa, ale także za najstarszego psa wszech czasów. Bobi dożył imponującego wieku 31 lat i 165 dni. Jednak życie Bobiego było o mało nie przerwane już jako szczeniaka. Według jego właściciela, Leonela Costy, Bobi był jednym z czterech szczeniąt urodzonych w 1992 roku. Rodzice Costy nie chcieli ich zostawić, bo rodzina miała już sporo zwierząt. W tamtych czasach starsi ludzie czasem zakopywali niechciane szczenięta, powiedział Costa dla Guinnessa. Przypadkiem rodzice przeoczyli Bobiego, który ukrył się w stosie drewna. Costa i jego bracia ukrywali Bobiego przed rodzicami, aż pies był już za stary, by go uśpić. Costa tłumaczy długowieczność Bobiego spokojnym otoczeniem w Conqueiros, możliwością swobodnego poruszania się po wsi, towarzystwem kotów oraz dietą z ludzkiego jedzenia moczonego w wodzie dla usunięcia przypraw. W lutym Guinness ogłosił Bobiego najstarszym żyjącym psem, zaledwie dwa tygodnie po tym jak nadał ten tytuł Spike’owi, 23-letniemu mieszańcowi chihuahua z Ohio. NPR zwróciło się do Guinnessa z pytaniem, kto po śmierci Bobiego został najstarszym żyjącym psem, lecz nie otrzymało natychmiastowej odpowiedzi. Dzięki swojemu wiekowi Bobi prześcignął Bluey’a, australijskiego psa zaganiającego, który żył 29 lat i 5 miesięcy i zmarł w 1939 roku, zostając najstarszym psem w historii.

article_content: On October 6, Euronews published an opinion piece by Dr. Gladden Pappin, president of the Hungarian Institute of International Affairs, discussing reasons why Sweden may not join NATO. While some of Dr. Pappin’s points warrant consideration, several statements require correction and additional context. For instance, Dr. Pappin downplays the threat posed by Russia, arguing that the ongoing war in Ukraine means Russia is unlikely to threaten NATO territory soon and dismisses claims about Russia’s imperial ambitions. This view is surprising given Russia’s aggressive actions in Ukraine, which border Hungary and have resulted in the deaths of ethnic Hungarian soldiers serving in the Ukrainian armed forces. Dr. Pappin's assessment contradicts the latest NATO position. The final communique from the Vilnius Summit on July 11 reads, ‘the Russian Federation is the most significant and direct threat to Allies’ security and to peace and stability in the Euro-Atlantic area.’ All NATO members, including Hungary, agreed to this declaration. Dr. Pappin also claims that Sweden’s military contribution to NATO would be limited. Contrary to this, Hungarian officials have acknowledged Sweden’s preparedness and strong defense posture. In an interview after the op-ed, Hungary’s Chief of General Staff, Lt. Gen. Gábor Böröndi, stated that Sweden’s armed forces are adequately prepared for NATO membership and emphasized that the issue is primarily political. According to The Military Balance 2023, Sweden’s defense budget in 2022 exceeded $8 billion (€7.5bn), nearly 2.5 times higher than Hungary’s $2.99bn (€2.8bn). Sweden's military is small but highly trained and well equipped, including nearly 100 JAS-39 Gripen fighter jets. Notably, Hungary operates Gripen jets as its sole fighter aircraft—leasing about a dozen from Sweden and currently negotiating contract extensions beyond 2026. Dr. Pappin further argues that trust issues between Budapest and Stockholm justify delaying Sweden’s NATO membership. However, Hungary’s continued reliance on Swedish military technology, especially the Gripen jets, contradicts this claim. Strategically, Sweden’s NATO accession would greatly strengthen the alliance’s presence in the Baltic Sea region, improving the collective defense of Finland, Poland, and the Baltic states, including strategic planning and logistics. Dr. Pappin’s article appears aligned with a broader Hungarian communication strategy aimed at creating ambiguity about Hungary's position on Sweden’s NATO bid, possibly as a delay tactic. The Hungarian Institute of International Affairs is subordinated to the Prime Minister’s Office, making it unlikely such an op-ed would be published without official coordination. While the Hungarian government claims to support Sweden’s NATO membership and attributes delays to parliament, Dr. Pappin’s article casts doubt on this explanation. Genuine support would likely preclude the publication of official criticism of Sweden’s readiness. Since 2010, Hungary’s parliament is dominated by Prime Minister Viktor Orbán’s Fidesz party, which usually passes government-backed policies without significant debate. It is implausible that parliament is independently delaying Sweden's ratification on such a critical matter. On the same day as Dr. Pappin’s article, Zsolt Németh, Chairman of the Foreign Affairs Committee and a veteran Fidesz figure, stated Hungary would support Sweden’s NATO membership and that the alliance would be stronger as a result. These contrasting official messages point to a coordinated, ambiguous communication approach. Dr. Pappin avoids addressing who truly benefits from Hungary’s stance. In an interview, Németh admitted Hungary coordinates closely with Turkey regarding the timing of Sweden’s ratification. Turkey, having set conditions for Sweden and the US, benefits by not being alone in delaying accession. Conversely, Hungary has issued no demands and only offers critical commentary. This approach does not serve clear Hungarian interests and risks harming its credibility as a NATO ally. Meanwhile, Russia, which opposes NATO expansion, benefits from the delay; Sweden joining would secure the Baltic Sea region for NATO and challenge Russia’s military position. Russia is reorganizing its forces in the area, a process lengthened by Sweden’s delayed NATO membership. Hungary’s stance thus indirectly supports Turkish and Russian interests in the region. Dr. András Rácz is a Senior Fellow at the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP). For feedback or submissions, contact view@euronews.com.

Jednak dalsza zależność Węgier od szwedzkiej technologii militarnej, zwłaszcza myśliwców Gripen, podważa tę tezę. Nieprawdopodobne, by parlament samodzielnie opóźniał ratyfikację w tej kluczowej sprawie. Tego samego dnia, gdy ukazał się artykuł dr. Te odmienne wypowiedzi urzędników sugerują skoordynowaną, ale niejednoznaczną linię komunikacyjną. Dr. Pappin nie odpowiada, kto faktycznie korzysta na obecnej polityce Węgier. To podejście nie przynosi jasnych korzyści Węgrom i może szkodzić ich wiarygodności jako sojusznika NATO. Rosja, przeciwnik rozszerzenia NATO, także korzysta z opóźnienia – wejście Szwecji do Sojuszu wzmocniłoby pozycję NATO nad Bałtykiem i ograniczyło wpływy Rosji. Obecnie Moskwa reorganizuje siły wojskowe w regionie, a proces ten wydłużany jest przez opóźnienie akcesji Szwecji. Obecna strategia Węgier pośrednio wspiera Turcję oraz Rosję w regionie. article_content: A customer is seen replacing the pump dispenser at a Chevron gas station in Columbus, Mississippi, on October 23. Over the last year, the average price of regular gasoline has dropped by more than 40 cents. According to the U.S. Labor Department, inflation cooled in October, largely due to declining gas prices, which helped offset rising rental costs. Consumer prices in October were up 3.2% from a year earlier, a softer increase compared to the 3.7% rise in the previous month. From September to October, overall prices remained unchanged. Gasoline prices fell by 5% during October, which contributed to keeping inflation in check. AAA reports the national average price for regular gas is now $3.35 per gallon—over 40 cents less than a year ago. In almost a dozen states, the average price is now below $3 per gallon. Meanwhile, the cost of rent, auto insurance, and medical care increased in October, while prices for airline tickets, hotel rooms, and used cars declined. Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices and is viewed as a better indicator of long-term trends, was 4.0% in October, slightly down from 4.1% the previous month. Core prices rose 0.2% between September and October, compared to a 0.3% increase the previous month. The cooler-than-expected inflation report is likely to reassure investors that the Federal Reserve may be less likely to raise interest rates again at its next meeting in December.

W październiku wzrosły koszty wynajmu, ubezpieczenia samochodu i opieki medycznej, podczas gdy ceny biletów lotniczych, noclegów hotelowych i samochodów używanych spadły. Inflacja bazowa, czyli wskaźnik nieuwzględniający zmiennych cen żywności i energii, oraz uznawany za lepszą miarę długoterminowych trendów, wyniosła w październiku 4,0%—odrobinę mniej niż 4,1% miesiąc wcześniej. Sam Allardyce has strongly addressed Mauro Zarate's criticism after the West Ham United striker accused his manager of showing him disrespect. Zarate, age 27, has been allowed to go on loan to Queens Park Rangers for the remainder of the season, even though top scorer Diafra Sakho will be absent due to participating in the Africa Cup of Nations with Senegal. Zarate claimed that Allardyce had sidelined him, saying, 'He has made things difficult for me ever since I arrived.'

Allardyce stated Zarate is currently undergoing a medical at QPR ahead of his loan move. Zarate was the first of nine signings West Ham made last summer, but he has struggled to secure a regular place in the side. Co-owner David Sullivan signed Zarate to a three-year contract during the off-season.

Allardyce explained that Zarate's limited playing time was due to tough competition from other forwards like Sakho, Ecuadorian international Enner Valencia, and England's Andy Carroll. 'Clearly, he is very frustrated at not being picked, but what he is saying is simply not true,' Allardyce said. 'He wasn't playing because he wasn't good enough—not in an absolute sense, as he is talented and has contributed well. But compared to the others, he could not play as regularly as he wanted. It's as simple as that.'

Zarate suggested he fell out of favor because he was brought in by co-chairman David Sullivan, not at Allardyce's request. He has also faced stiff competition from other successful new signings like Enner Valencia. ‘When you look at Valencia, Sakho, and Andy Carroll and what they've achieved compared to what Mauro has contributed when he’s played, and considering we have this level of talent available, someone is bound to be unhappy,' Allardyce said. 'Carlton Cole, one of my favorites, has spent more time on the bench and had fewer opportunities than Zarate. Carlton is a fantastic professional and a great person, so this has nothing to do with personal bias.'

Allardyce was also surprised to be singled out by Chelsea boss Jose Mourinho, who suggested that rival managers were involved in a 'campaign' to label Chelsea players as divers. Mourinho made these remarks after Chelsea's 1-1 draw with Southampton, following a yellow card issued to Cesc Fabregas for simulation. Allardyce had earlier criticized Branislav Ivanovic, who avoided a booking for what appeared to be a dive in Chelsea's 2-0 win over West Ham. Responding to Mourinho's accusations, Allardyce said: 'What's he talking about?' Allardyce firmly denied Mourinho's claims of a 'campaign' targeting Chelsea.

article_content: Slayer, known for intense albums such as 'Reign In Blood,' 'Hell Awaits,' and 'World Painted Blood,' recently showed a compassionate side. Guitarist Kerry King, 50, and members of the band's crew found a freezing, abandoned kitten on the streets of Indianapolis after dining at St. Elmo's Steak House. The kitten, offered by a homeless man for a dollar, was taken in by assistant tour manager Jess Cortese, who cared for it overnight on the tour bus. The next day, thanks to a staff member at the concert venue, the kitten—later named Gypsy—was adopted into a new, loving home where she is thriving. The Old National Centre, where Slayer performed with Suicidal Tendencies and Exodus, shared a photo confirming Gypsy’s adoption. The kitten’s new owner posted on Facebook: 'Here she is! I named her Gypsy! I gave her a bath last night and she slept for five hours on a heating pad. She's at the vet this morning being treated for fleas and worms. Thank you, Slayer, for your act of kindness.' Slayer, formed in Huntington Park, California, gained fame with their 1986 album 'Reign in Blood' and sold over 3.5 million albums in the U.S. between 1991 and 2004. Although often surrounded by controversy for graphic lyrics and imagery, the band demonstrated kindness with this animal rescue.

Kociak, oferowany przez bezdomnego za dolara, został przygarnięty przez zastępczynię menedżera trasy, Jess Cortese, która opiekowała się nim przez noc w autobusie zespołu. Następnego dnia, dzięki pracownikowi sali koncertowej, kotek – później nazwany Gypsy – znalazł nowy, kochający dom i teraz ma się świetnie. Old National Centre, miejsce, gdzie Slayer grał wspólnie z Suicidal Tendencies i Exodus, opublikowało zdjęcie potwierdzające adopcję Gypsy. Nowa właścicielka zamieściła na Facebooku: „Oto ona! Nazwałam ją Gypsy! Wykąpałam ją wczoraj wieczorem, potem spała pięć godzin na poduszce grzewczej. Dziś rano była u weterynarza, leczona na pchły i robaki. Dziękuję Slayerowi za ten akt dobroci.” Slayer, założony w Huntington Park w Kalifornii, zdobył rozgłos po albumie „Reign in Blood” z 1986 roku i sprzedał ponad 3,5 miliona płyt w USA w latach 1991–2004. Choć zespół bywa krytykowany za kontrowersyjne teksty i okładki, tym razem pokazał swoje wielkie serce, ratując zwierzę.

article_content: The Federal Government’s oil revenue for May 2023 dropped to N223 billion, a 72% reduction from the monthly target of N804 billion, according to the Central Bank of Nigeria’s Monthly Economic Report. This figure represents a 36% decrease from April’s oil earnings. The report attributes the shortfall primarily to lower receipts from Petroleum Profit Tax and Royalties. Overall, gross federation earnings also declined, driven by decreases in both oil and non-oil revenues. Federation revenue totaled N837 billion in May, which is 16% lower than in April and falls 53% below the budgeted amount. Non-oil revenue sources dominated, accounting for 73.4% of the federation’s revenue in the review period, totaling N614 billion—a 5.4% drop from April and 36% below target. This reduction is largely attributed to weaker collections of Company Income Tax, Value Added Tax, and Customs & Excise Duties due to seasonal business tax filing patterns. The CBN report coincides with similar findings from Reuters, noting that U.S. imports of crude oil from OPEC and non-OPEC partners have steadily declined over the past year, tightening supply in the U.S. but supporting other markets such as Europe. In October, U.S. crude waterborne imports averaged 2.47 million barrels per day, down from 2.92 million in September, with notable declines from OPEC+ countries including Nigeria, Algeria, and Saudi Arabia. CBN further stated that earnings from Nigeria’s crude oil exports weakened due to declining crude oil prices, exacerbated by the United States’ debt challenges. Provisional data indicated that crude oil and gas export receipts fell by 3.8% to $4.06 billion in May (from $4.22 billion in April). Crude oil export receipts specifically dropped 4.2% to $3.58 billion, while gas export receipts decreased by 2.1% to $0.49 billion. Spot prices for Nigeria’s Bonny Light crude fell by 11.16% to $76.91 per barrel from $86.57 in April. Similar declines were recorded for UK Brent ($76.95/bbl), Forcados ($77.24/bbl), WTI ($72.34/bbl), and the OPEC Reference Basket ($75.70/bbl). On the production side, Nigeria’s domestic crude oil production grew to 1.18 million barrels per day in May, following the resolution of industrial action and the lifting of force majeure by Exxon Mobil. Of this, 0.45 million barrels per day were allocated for domestic use, and 0.73 million barrels per day were exported. Despite the increase, production remains below the OPEC quota of 1.742 million barrels per day by 0.562 million. According to Elliot Ibie, President of the Nigerian Association of Petroleum Explorationists, the sector continues to face post-pandemic challenges such as security issues, pipeline vandalism, oil theft, and slow implementation of reforms like the Petroleum Industry Act. Addressing these problems is essential for boosting investment, increasing oil exploration, and improving export levels and federal revenues.

Oznacza to również 36% spadek w porównaniu z dochodami z kwietnia. Według raportu, główną przyczyną niedoboru były niższe wpływy z podatku dochodowego od ropy (Petroleum Profit Tax) oraz opłat licencyjnych (Royalties). Dominowały źródła poza-naftowe (73,4% całkowitych dochodów federacji), które wyniosły 614 miliardów nair – to 5,4% mniej niż w kwietniu i aż o 36% poniżej celu. Spadek ten wynika głównie z gorszych wpływów z podatku CIT, VAT oraz ceł i akcyz, co odzwierciedla sezonowość rozliczeń podatkowych firm. Raport CBN pokrywa się z informacjami Reutersa – amerykański import ropy naftowej drogą morską od krajów OPEC i spoza OPEC systematycznie maleje od roku, co ogranicza podaż w USA, ale wspiera inne rynki, np. w Europie. W październiku średni import ropy naftowej do USA wyniósł 2,47 mln baryłek dziennie, wobec 2,92 mln we wrześniu – największy spadek dotyczył państw OPEC+, w tym Nigerii, Algierii i Arabii Saudyjskiej. CBN dodał, że dochody Nigerii z eksportu ropy osłabiły się w wyniku spadków cen surowca, potęgowanych przez sytuację długu publicznego Stanów Zjednoczonych. Dane wstępne pokazują, że przychody z eksportu ropy i gazu zmniejszyły się w maju o 3,8% do 4,06 miliarda dolarów (w kwietniu: 4,22 mld). Sam eksport ropy zanotował spadek o 4,2% do 3,58 mld dolarów, a gazu o 2,1% do 0,49 mld dolarów. Średnia cena spot ropy Bonny Light w Nigerii spadła o 11,16%, do 76,91 dolarów za baryłkę (kwiecień: 86,57 USD). Podobny spadek dotyczył cen Brent z UK (76,95 USD/baryłkę), Forcados (77,24 USD), WTI (72,34 USD) oraz koszyka referencyjnego OPEC (75,70 USD). Z drugiej strony, produkcja krajowa ropy wzrosła do 1,18 mln baryłek dziennie w maju, po zakończeniu strajków i wznowieniu produkcji przez Exxon Mobil. Z tej ilości 0,45 mln baryłek przeznaczono na rynek krajowy, a 0,73 mln na eksport. Mimo wzrostu, produkcja wciąż pozostaje poniżej limitu OPEC, wynoszącego 1,742 mln baryłek dziennie (o 0,562 mln mniej). Jak podkreśla Elliot Ibie, prezes Nigerijskiego Stowarzyszenia Eksploratorów Ropy Naftowej, branża wciąż musi mierzyć się z wyzwaniami po pandemii COVID-19: problemami z bezpieczeństwem, wandalizmem rurociągów, kradzieżą ropy oraz opóźnieniami wdrożenia reform, takich jak Ustawa o Przemyśle Naftowym. Rozwiązanie tych problemów jest kluczowe dla większych inwestycji, intensywniejszych poszukiwań ropy oraz wzrostu eksportu i dochodów federacji.

article_content: BJP spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla has condemned comments made by Congress state chief Kamal Nath, who reportedly cautioned government officials in Niwari district that no one would be exempt from consequences if Congress regained power in Madhya Pradesh. Poonawalla questioned whether Congress represents friendliness or intimidation, and accused the party of a recurring pattern of threatening public officials. He suggested this behavior reveals a deep-seated arrogance within Congress and called upon the Election Commission to intervene. During a public rally, Kamal Nath advised local administrators, reminding them that their actions should take into account the possibility of Congress returning to office, as it could affect their careers over the next several years. In response, Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma publicly criticized Congress for what he described as arrogance and an obsession with power, claiming they act as though they have already won the election. Meanwhile, Kamal Nath dismissed the BJP's election manifesto, accusing the party of lacking original ideas and simply copying Congress’s agenda. The Madhya Pradesh assembly elections will take place in a single phase on November 17, with 230 seats up for grabs. The results will be announced on December 3.

Poonawalla zastanawiał się, czy Kongres to partia przyjaźni, czy groźby, i zarzucił jej powracające grożenie urzędnikom państwowym. Według niego takie zachowanie świadczy o głęboko zakorzenionej arogancji w tej partii, dlatego wezwał Komisję Wyborczą do interwencji. Podczas publicznego wiecu Kamal Nath zaapelował do lokalnych administratorów, aby w swoich działaniach brali pod uwagę, że powrót Kongresu do władzy może wpływać na ich kariery przez następne lata. Premier Assamu, Himanta Biswa Sarma, publicznie zarzucił Kongresowi arogancję i obsesję na punkcie władzy oraz stwierdził, że zachowują się, jakby wybory już wygrali. Tymczasem Kamal Nath skrytykował program wyborczy BJP, twierdząc, że partii brak oryginalnych pomysłów i jedynie kopiuje działania Kongresu. Wybory do zgromadzenia stanowego w Madhya Pradesh odbędą się w jednej turze 17 listopada, a wyniki zostaną ogłoszone 3 grudnia. Do obsadzenia jest 230 mandatów.

article_content: Lorraine Kelly, a popular ITV daytime TV presenter, is stepping into the role of style ambassador for JD Williams, a retailer catering to women over 50. At 54, Lorraine has been photographed modeling the brand's new Autumn/Winter 2014 range and has announced she will also design a collection for Spring/Summer 2015. JD Williams surveyed their customers about whose style they admire, and Lorraine was the unanimous favorite, with both men and women saying they trust her fashion sense. Speaking at the range’s launch at the Shangri-La hotel in The Shard, London, Lorraine shared, 'I’m thrilled JD Williams asked me to be an ambassador. I’m 54 and I absolutely love fashion.' Lorraine noted that older women are often overlooked by the fashion industry, despite representing a significant portion of the market, and hopes her work with JD Williams will help change that. She worked closely with designers, suggesting details like adding sleeves and creating cuts that flatter women over 50. Research shows that the UK’s over-50 female fashion market is worth £2.5 billion per season and is the fastest-growing sector, making it surprising that it is underserved. Lorraine will edit a range for JD Williams and is already designing her SS15 collection for the brand. She believes comfort is key in fashion: 'Feeling comfortable in what you wear is most important.' Lorraine explained that many women her age find it difficult to get stylish, flattering clothes and that all her chosen items make her feel great. Toni Jones, editor of 30ishStylist.com, praised Lorraine for being a style role model for women in their fifties, saying she experiments with color and trends while maintaining classic, flattering shapes. 'She has selected wearable pieces with a touch of fashion edge, showing you don’t have to try too hard to look stylish – this should inspire more women to embrace their style.' The launch event featured Lorraine alongside style expert Hilary Alexander as they presented the range to the press. Lorraine is excited about her upcoming SS15 designs, expressing pride in her age and joy at helping women feel confident. She emphasizes that mature women have significant buying power and are a 'force to be reckoned with.' The JD Williams Lorraine Kelly collection is available in sizes 10 to 32, with prices ranging from £20 for a jewelled jersey top to £150 for an embellished party dress.

article_content: Life lessons are essential to growing our knowledge and shaping our lives. Each experience—whether a challenge, success, or moment of clarity—adds depth to who we are. As Steve Jobs noted in his 2005 Stanford commencement speech, "You can't connect the dots looking forward; you can only connect them looking backward." Reflecting on our past experiences helps us gain wisdom. Examining what led to our greatest successes and learning from mistakes empowers us to make better choices in the future. These pivotal moments become the foundation on which we build meaningful lives and careers. Self-Discovery: The Mirror of Understanding Understanding ourselves is key to finding purpose in our work. As noted by Elizabeth Perry in a recent Better Up article, life moves quickly and taking the time for self-discovery often gets neglected. However, uncovering our life lessons can lead to greater self-confidence, reduced self-criticism, and clearer focus. Major life lessons reveal our true passions, strengths, and values, guiding us in our choices and actions. Aligning our careers with these core aspects transforms work from a routine into a source of fulfillment. Resilience: The Unsung Hero Resilience, developed through challenges, is crucial at work. It involves learning from setbacks and moving forward with determination. In professional life, this means embracing change and seeing both failures and successes as steps toward growth. It's valuable to reflect not only on failures but also on successes to understand which traits and strengths contributed. Recognize the role others play in achievements and express gratitude. Empathy: Building Connections Empathy, gained through relationships, is foundational to meaningful work. It strengthens professional networks, helps manage teams compassionately, and better understand clients' needs. Emotional intelligence transforms work into a shared human journey. Consider how giving and receiving empathy enriches social connections and personal well-being. Perspective: Prioritizing What Matters Life teaches us to focus on what is truly important. In our careers, setting the right priorities turns overwhelm into purposeful direction. Remember times when lack of focus diluted your efforts, and reflect on how better prioritization could have improved outcomes. Goal Setting: Adapting Over Time Past experiences shape how we approach goals. Knowing what has worked—or not—helps with effective career planning. It’s important to adapt goals as circumstances change and recognize when flexibility is needed. Developing this wisdom leads to better results, especially in uncertain times. Ethical Decision-Making: Guided by Values Life lessons often involve ethical dilemmas that form our moral framework. In a professional setting, making decisions that align with our ethics is vital. Reflect on your own experiences with ethical challenges and the lessons learned from them. Creative Problem-Solving: Fueling Innovation Creativity, developed by facing life’s obstacles, benefits any career. It encourages inventive thinking and the ability to solve problems in unique ways. Remembering the challenges you've overcome can reignite passion, especially during stagnant periods. Life lessons are not just stories from the past; they are guiding lights for a rewarding career. By weaving these lessons into our work, we find purpose and fulfillment, enriching not only our lives but also the world around us.
translated_content: Lekcje życiowe są kluczowe dla poszerzania naszej wiedzy i kształtowania życia. Każde doświadczenie – czy to wyzwanie, sukces, czy moment jasności – pogłębia nasze ja. Jak zauważył Steve Jobs w swoim przemówieniu na Stanford w 2005 roku: "Nie da się połączyć punktów patrząc w przyszłość; można to zrobić tylko patrząc wstecz." Refleksja nad przeszłymi przeżyciami pomaga nam zdobyć mądrość. Analiza powodów naszych największych sukcesów oraz nauka z błędów pozwala podejmować lepsze decyzje w przyszłości. Takie przełomowe chwile stanowią fundament, na którym budujemy sensowne życie i karierę. Samoświadomość: Lustro zrozumienia Poznanie siebie jest kluczowe, by znaleźć sens w pracy. Jak napisała Elizabeth Perry w artykule dla Better Up, życie biegnie szybko i często brakuje nam czasu na samopoznanie. Jednak odkrywanie swoich lekcji życiowych może prowadzić do większej pewności siebie, mniejszej samokrytyki i lepszej koncentracji. Ważne życiowe lekcje ujawniają nasze prawdziwe pasje, mocne strony i wartości, które kierują naszymi decyzjami i działaniami. Dopasowując karierę do tych aspektów, zamieniamy rutynę w źródło spełnienia. Odporność: Niedoceniany bohater Odporność, kształtowana przez życiowe trudności, jest niezbędna w pracy. Polega na wyciąganiu wniosków z niepowodzeń i ruszaniu naprzód z determinacją. W życiu zawodowym oznacza to akceptowanie zmian i traktowanie zarówno porażek, jak i sukcesów jako kroków w rozwoju. Warto analizować nie tylko porażki, ale też sukcesy, by zrozumieć, jakie cechy i umiejętności do nich doprowadziły. Doceniaj rolę innych w swoich osiągnięciach i okazuj wdzięczność. Empatia: Budowanie relacji Empatia, nabyta dzięki relacjom, jest fundamentem sensownej pracy. Wzmacnia sieci zawodowe, pomaga zarządzać zespołami z troską i lepiej rozumieć potrzeby klientów. Inteligencja emocjonalna przemienia pracę we wspólną podróż. Pomyśl, jak okazywanie i przyjmowanie empatii wzbogaca relacje społeczne i dobrostan. Perspektywa: Ustalanie priorytetów Życie uczy nas skupiać się na tym, co naprawdę ważne. W pracy właściwe priorytety zamieniają chaos w celowe działanie. Przypomnij sobie momenty, w których brak skupienia rozpraszał wysiłki, i zastanów się, jak lepsze priorytety mogłyby poprawić efekty. Cele: Elastyczność w czasie Doświadczenia z przeszłości wpływają na to, jak podchodzimy do wyznaczania celów. Świadomość tego, co działało, a co nie, ułatwia planowanie kariery. Ważne jest, by dopasowywać cele do zmiennych okoliczności i rozpoznawać momenty, w których trzeba być elastycznym. Taka mądrość prowadzi do lepszych rezultatów – szczególnie w niepewnych czasach. Etyka: Prowadzeni wartościami Lekcje życiowe często obejmują dylematy moralne, które kształtują nasze wartości. W pracy podejmowanie decyzji zgodnych z własną etyką jest niezwykle istotne. Zastanów się nad swoimi doświadczeniami z dylematami moralnymi i wyciągniętymi z nich wnioskami. Kreatywność: Siła innowacji Kreatywność rozwijana poprzez przezwyciężanie trudności pomaga w każdej branży. Wspiera nieszablonowe myślenie i rozwiązywanie problemów w wyjątkowy sposób. Przypominanie sobie pokonanych przeszkód może na nowo rozbudzić zawodową pasję – zwłaszcza w okresie stagnacji. Lekcje życiowe to nie tylko opowieści z przeszłości – są drogowskazami do satysfakcjonującej kariery. Wplatając je w pracę, zyskujemy sens i spełnienie, wzbogacając nie tylko siebie, ale też świat wokół nas.

article_content: In August 2005, as Hurricane Katrina approached New Orleans, LaShawn Traylor faced a life-threatening medical emergency while seven months pregnant. She was rushed to Methodist Hospital, where doctors performed an emergency C-section due to an enlarged heart. Her son, Lorenzo, arrived prematurely, weighing only 2 pounds, 11 ounces. LaShawn was soon placed in a medically induced coma on a ventilator as the hurricane drew closer. Meanwhile, her husband Lionel evacuated their four other children to Jackson, Mississippi, leaving a picture of their newborn with LaShawn before leaving. When LaShawn regained consciousness three days later, she found herself separated from her family. With the city under mandatory evacuation and Lorenzo moved to another hospital, LaShawn’s ordeal was just beginning. She initially underestimated the storm’s severity, as it seemed calm when she awoke. After Katrina struck, the levees failed and New Orleans flooded. With Methodist Hospital’s lower floors underwater and power lost, staff struggled to keep patients alive manually. Supplies quickly dwindled, heightening Traylor’s fear—especially since she hadn’t yet held her baby. Though told Lorenzo was relocated to Children’s Hospital, uncertainty about his fate weighed heavily on her. Traylor feared the worst for her fragile newborn. Eventually, helicopters began evacuations from the hospital rooftop. LaShawn was airlifted and spent 18 hours on a bridge, waiting for rescue after her delivery. Dehydrated, she was eventually taken by bus to the airport, then flown to Texas. At the airport, LaShawn was among mothers leaving Methodist Hospital. Unlike the others, she only had pictures of her son. During a brief interview that aired on television, she appealed for help, which eventually reached her husband Lionel, who had heard nothing from his wife or child in days. When they reunited at a shelter in Fort Worth, LaShawn still didn’t know their son’s whereabouts. Aid organizations worked tirelessly to find Lorenzo, who had been transferred between three hospitals during the evacuation. He was eventually found safe at Baton Rouge General Hospital. Their reunion brought immense relief. Four months later, the family returned to find their New Orleans home destroyed by flooding. They spent a short time in a FEMA trailer but finally relocated to Jackson, Mississippi. There, the family rebuilt—LaShawn completed her education, and Lionel became a full-time pastor, while Lorenzo thrived. LaShawn went on to create Rise Above Katrina, a foundation supporting other Katrina survivors with housing and financial planning. Looking back, she says, 'Life is better now. Katrina was a wake-up call. Now I live my life with purpose.'
translated_content: W sierpniu 2005 roku, gdy huragan Katrina zbliżał się do Nowego Orleanu, LaShawn Traylor doświadczyła poważnych problemów zdrowotnych będąc w siódmym miesiącu ciąży. Trafiła do szpitala Methodist, gdzie lekarze zdecydowali się na cesarskie cięcie z powodu powiększonego serca. Jej syn, Lorenzo, przyszedł na świat przedwcześnie, ważąc zaledwie 1,22 kg. Wkrótce po porodzie LaShawn została wprowadzona w śpiączkę farmakologiczną i podłączona do respiratora, a huragan był coraz bliżej miasta. Jej mąż, Lionel, ewakuował czwórkę ich dzieci do Jackson w stanie Missisipi, zostawiając przy LaShawn zdjęcie noworodka na pożegnanie. Trzy dni później LaShawn odzyskała przytomność, ale była sama, oddzielona od bliskich. Miasto objęto obowiązkową ewakuacją, a Lorenzo trafił do innego szpitala – to był początek trudnych przeżyć dla LaShawn. Na początku nie sądziła, że sytuacja jest aż tak poważna, bo gdy się przebudziła, za oknem było spokojnie. Po przejściu Katriny pękły wały, a Nowy Orlean został zalany. Dolne piętra szpitala Methodist znalazły się pod wodą i odcięto prąd – personel medyczny ręcznie ratował życie pacjentów. Kończyły się też zapasy jedzenia i wody, a LaShawn ogarniał strach, zwłaszcza że nie mogła przytulić syna. Powiedziano jej, że Lorenzo został przeniesiony do szpitala dziecięcego, ale nieustanna niepewność o jego los była przytłaczająca. Bała się, że jej wcześniak nie przeżyje tych dramatycznych wydarzeń. W końcu helikoptery zaczęły ewakuować pacjentów ze szpitalnego dachu. LaShawn została przetransportowana i przez 18 godzin czekała na pomoc, siedząc pod mostem, wyczerpana po porodzie. Odwodniona, trafiła w końcu autobusem na lotnisko, a stamtąd została przewieziona samolotem do Teksasu. Na lotnisku znalazła się wśród matek z oddziału położniczego, lecz jako jedyna nie miała dziecka przy sobie – tylko zdjęcia Lorenzo. W krótkim wywiadzie telewizyjnym błagała o pomoc – jej apel usłyszał Lionel, który od dni nie miał wiadomości o żonie i synu. Gdy spotkali się w schronisku Czerwonego Krzyża w Fort Worth, LaShawn wciąż nie wiedziała, gdzie jest ich dziecko. Wolontariusze i organizacje pomocowe prowadzili intensywne poszukiwania – Lorenzo trafił w trakcie ewakuacji do trzech szpitali. Finalnie odnalazł się w Baton Rouge General Hospital. Spotkanie rodziny po tylu trudach przyniosło im ogromną ulgę. Po czterech miesiącach wrócili do Nowego Orleanu – ich dom był zniszczony przez powódź. Krótko mieszkali w przyczepie FEMA, po czym osiedlili się w Jackson w stanie Missisipi. Tam odbudowali życie – LaShawn ukończyła studia, Lionel został pastorem, a Lorenzo rozwijał się zdrowo. article_content: New scientific findings suggest that human activities, particularly city-building and industrial development, may be shaping the evolution of animal brains. According to research from Associate Professor Emilie Snell-Rood at the University of Minnesota, some city-dwelling animals have larger brains on average compared to those living in rural areas. Snell-Rood and undergraduate Naomi Wick analyzed museum specimens of small mammals collected over the past century. They focused on ten species—including shrews, voles, bats, squirrels, mice, and gophers—from both urban and rural environments in and around the Twin Cities. Their study found that white-footed mice and meadow voles from city environments had, on average, brains about six percent larger than those from the countryside. This supports the idea that adapting to urban life may require increased cognitive ability, reflected in larger cranial capacity. However, the results were not consistent across all species. For example, some urban mammal populations saw no change in brain size over time, while in two species, urban brain sizes even declined. Conversely, certain rural populations, such as bats and shrews, showed increases in cranial capacity. The researchers believe these patterns are more likely due to evolutionary changes rather than differences in diet or nutrition, as overall body size remained unchanged. Snell-Rood notes that building and maintaining larger brains is metabolically expensive for animals, implying there are trade-offs between brain growth and other biological investments like reproduction. She emphasizes that animal populations are responding to the ways humans transform both cities and rural areas, though adaptation varies widely between species and over time. The study highlights the complexity of how human environmental changes are influencing the course of animal evolution.

article_content: Ronnie Smith, a 33-year-old teacher from Austin, Texas, was shot and killed while jogging near his home in Benghazi, Libya. No group has claimed responsibility for the killing. Libyan authorities have promised to investigate, as the incident marks the latest in a series of targeted killings in cities like Benghazi and Derna, with many victims being security personnel, activists, and members of the judiciary. Smith moved to Libya about a year and a half before his death. He worked at the International School Benghazi, where English was taught. Following news of the tragedy, many praised him on the school's Facebook page, describing him as respectful, optimistic, and dedicated to his students. Many also expressed condolences to Smith's wife, Anita, and their young son. Smith had tweeted recently about missing his family, who had returned to the United States. His colleagues at Austin Stone Community Church in Texas confirmed that Smith stayed in Libya to help his students with their midterm exams. After Smith's death, the church removed from its website a video of Smith discussing his faith and his desire to share his spiritual beliefs in places where churches were not accessible. The church shared edited clips with news outlets, in which Smith expresses trust in God and peace about his work. On his church profile, Smith wrote about his lifelong faith and desire to model his life after theologian Jonathan Edwards. Dave Barrett, executive pastor of Austin Stone Community Church, said Smith wished for peace and prosperity for Libya and for its people to experience spiritual joy. There has been concern that Smith’s openness about his religious beliefs could have put him at risk, as proselytizing is illegal in Libya. After the 2011 revolution, fears of missionary work have increased, and there have been previous incidents involving accusations of proselytism and violence toward Christians. Paul Lee, a spokesman for Smith's church, stated that Smith was not working as a missionary in Libya, though the church does operate missionary programs elsewhere. Libya remains dangerous for foreigners following incidents like the 2012 attack on the US diplomatic mission in Benghazi. Analysis by experts suggests Smith may have been targeted because of his nationality, with possible links to al Qaeda or allied groups. An al Qaeda spokesman had recently called on supporters to avenge the capture of a Libyan militant. Smith had also tweeted about threats of kidnappings by Islamist groups in Libya. Many tributes posted online praised Smith's commitment and mourned his loss. Some drew parallels to other attacks targeting Americans in Libya and expressed both grief and frustration about the ongoing instability.

article_content: CMS Info Systems is confident of achieving its FY25 revenue target, aiming to double its revenue from an FY21 base of approximately INR 1,300 crore to INR 2,500–2,700 crore, said Anush Raghavan, President – Cash Management Solutions, in an interview with ETMarkets. In Q2 FY24, the company recorded a 15% year-on-year increase in operating revenue, with adjusted PAT rising 25% YoY to Rs 92 crore. Consolidated quarterly revenue stands at Rs 544 crore, driven in part by Managed Services & Technology Solutions, which now contribute 38% to overall revenues. Raghavan attributed this strong performance to focused execution and market leadership. The Cash Logistics business expanded its network by 12% YoY, reaching 129,000 business points, reflecting growth in banking and post-pandemic organized retail sectors. The Managed Services and Technology Solutions segment reported new business wins of Rs 500 crore in Q2 FY24, growing the overall order book to Rs 3,800 crore, with 75% of it already executed. CMS’s reach currently covers 97% of Indian districts and 16,000+ pin codes, providing significant operating leverage as the business scales. The company has maintained consistent growth of over 20% for six consecutive quarters, sustained by growing opportunities in banking, retail, and e-commerce. Much of CMS’s revenue is annuity-driven, promoting predictable and stable operations. Operational efficiency has improved by more than 20% over the past four years, aided by investments in automation technology. Plans for the next 12 months focus on executing new business wins, delivering value-added solutions to customers, and strengthening market share across all segments. Raghavan highlighted that the continued growth of India’s retail sector and ongoing bank network expansion support a positive long-term outlook. For the first half of FY24, Managed Services and Technology Solutions secured Rs 650 crore in new deals, particularly in Banking Automation and ATM-as-a-Service. These wins reflect banks’ focus on expanding their physical infrastructure. In the September quarter, Foreign Institutional Investors and Mutual Funds increased stakes in the company, while the promoters’ share declined from 46% to 26%. CMS has partnered with investors like Blackstone (2009–2015) and SION Investment Holdings (Barings Asia) from 2015 onwards. The company credits its growth to professional governance and a consistent, management-driven approach. article_content: After eight months off-air, ABC’s "Lost" returns tonight to address, among other mysteries, the dazzling white light that ended the 2009 season so explosively. Was it a nuclear blast, a quantum time shift, or a reboot to the story's origins? These questions loom as "Lost"—broadcast TV’s most complex drama—begins its final stretch: sixteen episodes that will conclude its signature time-bending, empathy-shifting narrative. However, the most important question, six years after "Lost" premiered in 2004, remains: Who still cares? That’s a fair question, considering how much television and its audiences have changed. When "Lost" debuted, its shocking island plane crash made for riveting, must-watch TV. But with the advent of DVRs and DVD box sets, the landscape is different. Fans of serialized shows like "Lost" or Fox’s "24" often record and time-shift their viewing, skipping water-cooler chats until they’re caught up. Some even avoid weekly broadcasts, preferring to binge-watch entire seasons later, uninterrupted by commercials. This is a big change from the days when TV finales were national events. In 1967, the last episode of ABC’s "The Fugitive" attracted enough viewers to break records, outdrawing even The Beatles’ appearance on "The Ed Sullivan Show." In 1983, the series finale of CBS’s "M*A*S*H" drew 121.6 million viewers—77% of all TV households—setting a record that still stands. With TV audiences now scattered across so many options, those numbers will likely never be matched. At its peak in season two, "Lost" averaged nearly 19 million viewers. By last season, that was down to under 12 million, and the season finale—with its unsettling fade to white—pulled in about 10 million viewers. Other networks tried to copy the "Lost" formula with shows like CBS’s "Threshold" and ABC’s "Invasion," but these series struggled to find audiences and ended without closure. "Lost," at least, is heading toward a definite ending, making this final season an event to savor. Opportunities for such moments are rare on broadcast TV now. While cable offers more serialized dramas, few network shows build this kind of anticipation for a finale. Many former fans may return to see how "Lost" ends, hoping for something meaningful—and they may get it. The show’s creators have long planned the series’ conclusion (the writer’s guess is it will end as it began, with a closeup of Jack’s eye) and are crafting these final episodes to reflect both the beginning and ending of the story. Despite all the changes in technology and viewing habits, "Lost" is a show that rewards viewers who watch live. ABC didn’t provide critics with advance copies of the premiere, and while that’s disappointing, it adds to the anticipation. This is a show I want to watch as it airs and talk about with friends afterward—a rare TV experience today, and one not to be taken for granted. The opinions in this commentary are solely those of David Bianculli.

Jednak najważniejsze pytanie, sześć lat po premierze w 2004 roku, brzmi: Kogo to jeszcze obchodzi? To całkiem uzasadnione pytanie, biorąc pod uwagę, jak bardzo zmieniła się telewizja i jej widzowie. Gdy „Lost” debiutował, szokująca katastrofa samolotu na wyspie sprawiła, że był to serial, którego nie można było przegapić. Jednak wraz z pojawieniem się nagrywarek DVR i zestawów DVD sytuacja się zmieniła. Fani seriali takich jak „Lost” czy „24” często nagrywają odcinki i oglądają je później, unikając rozmów w pracy, dopóki nie nadrobią zaległości. Niektórzy celowo omijają cotygodniowe emisje, woląc obejrzeć cały sezon później, bez przerw na reklamy. To ogromna zmiana wobec dawnych czasów, gdy finały seriali były wydarzeniami ogólnonarodowymi. W 1967 roku ostatni odcinek „The Fugitive” pobił rekord oglądalności, wyprzedzając nawet występ Beatlesów w programie „The Ed Sullivan Show”. W 1983 roku finał „M*A*S*H” zgromadził 121,6 miliona widzów—77% wszystkich gospodarstw domowych z telewizorem—ustalając rekord, który wciąż nie został pobity. Obecnie, gdy widzowie mają do wyboru tyle możliwości, takie liczby raczej się już nie pojawią. W drugim sezonie „Lost” oglądało średnio prawie 19 milionów widzów. W ostatnim sezonie liczba ta spadła poniżej 12 milionów, a finał, zakończony zaskakującym przejściem do bieli, przyciągnął około 10 milionów widzów. Inne stacje próbowały powtórzyć sukces „Lost” serialami takimi jak „Threshold” czy „Invasion”, ale nie zdobyły one dużej publiczności i zakończyły się bez zamknięcia wątku. „Lost” przynajmniej zmierza do rzeczywistego zakończenia, co czyni ten sezon wydarzeniem, które warto celebrować. Teraz takie chwile są rzadkością w telewizji ogólnodostępnej. Owszem, na kablówkach pojawia się więcej seriali z rozbudowaną fabułą, ale niewiele z nich wzbudza tak wielkie emocje przed finałem. Wielu dawnych fanów może powrócić, by zobaczyć, jak „Lost” się skończy, licząc na coś wyjątkowego—i możliwe, że to dostaną. Twórcy serialu od dawna planowali zakończenie (autor przypuszcza, że serial skończy się tak, jak się zaczął—zbliżeniem na oko Jacka) i przygotowują finałowe odcinki, które będą odnosić się zarówno do początków, jak i końca historii. Mimo zmian w technologii i sposobie oglądania, „Lost” to serial, który najbardziej nagradza widzów oglądających na żywo. ABC nie udostępniło krytykom przedpremierowych kopii pierwszego odcinka ostatniego sezonu, a choć to trochę rozczarowuje, tylko zwiększa oczekiwanie. To serial, który chcę obejrzeć na bieżąco i potem rozmawiać o nim ze znajomymi—rzadkie dziś doświadczenie, którego nie warto lekceważyć. Opinie wyrażone w tym komentarzu są wyłącznie zdaniem Davida Bianculliego.

article_content: Jimmy Anderson is poised to make history as he enters the final Test against India at The Oval on Friday, needing just eight more wickets to become England’s all-time leading Test wicket-taker, surpassing Sir Ian Botham. Anderson, 32, from Burnley, is already England’s leading wicket-taker across all formats with 649 international wickets—376 of them in Test cricket. Anderson’s journey has seen him transform from a raw, inconsistent fast bowler into one of the most reliable and skillful swing bowlers in the modern game. His competitive nature has occasionally led to controversies, such as the recent verbal altercation with Indian batsman Ravi Jadeja. However, those who know him best describe him as highly determined, yet reserved off the field. Anderson’s father, Michael, recalls a childhood marked by a strong competitive spirit—a trait common in their family. Rapid growth in his teenage years added to his bowling pace, and his performances soon drew the attention of Lancashire selectors. Former England all-rounder and coach Mike Watkinson remembers Anderson as a quiet yet determined player with a distinctive action and consistent ability to swing the ball. After joining the England one-day side in 2002 and excelling at the 2003 World Cup, Anderson made his Test debut. With strong competition for places and a serious back injury in 2006, his career was at risk, but he used the setback to enhance both his fitness and technique. Longtime teammate Luke Sutton praises Anderson’s unique style and mental resilience, noting that overcoming challenges has made him stronger. Now, having bowled more overs than any other English bowler, Anderson’s commitment to the game and country is unwavering. With guidance from sports psychologist Mark Bawden, Anderson has developed distinct on-field ('Jimmy') and off-field ('James') personas. He may appear combative on the field, but those who know him describe his reserved and humorous nature away from cricket. As he faces the upcoming Oval Test, Anderson’s family will be there to support him. His father Michael proudly reflects on his son’s career, finding it sometimes hard to believe that their 'little boy' plays for England. After more than a decade at the top, Anderson's influence on English cricket is clear, and he continues to chase new milestones.

Droga Andersona to przemiana z nieoszlifowanego i czasem niestabilnego szybkiego miotacza w jednego z najbardziej niezawodnych i technicznych swingujących bowlerów obecnych czasów. Jego waleczna natura czasem prowadzi do kontrowersji — jak ostatnia sprzeczka słowna z indyjskim batsmanem Ravi Jadeją. Jednak ludzie, którzy go znają, opisują go jako bardzo zdeterminowanego, choć poza boiskiem jest raczej spokojny. article_content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has stated that Israel does not intend to occupy or govern Gaza after its conflict with Hamas, but insists that the enclave must be demilitarized, deradicalized, and rebuilt. In a Fox News interview aired Thursday, Netanyahu said Israel seeks a civilian government for Gaza after Hamas, which has controlled the enclave since 2006, but did not specify who would establish such a government. "We don’t seek to govern Gaza, we don’t seek to occupy it. But we seek to give it and us a better future—and that requires defeating Hamas," he said, noting that there is no set timetable for these objectives. Gaza is widely seen by the international community as an occupied territory, since Israel maintains control over its borders, airspace, and territorial waters, even though it withdrew forces and settlers in 2005. In 2007, Israel imposed a blockade on Gaza, which was captured along with other Palestinian territories—East Jerusalem and the West Bank—in the 1967 war. While Israel argues the 2005 withdrawal ended its occupation, international law experts, such as former UN special rapporteur Michael Lynk, assert that the occupation persists due to Israel's effective control over Gaza. During the interview, Netanyahu mentioned a 'credible force' would be required to enter Gaza as needed to counter threats and prevent the resurgence of a Hamas-like entity. His comments come after stating that Israel would be responsible for Gaza’s security for an 'indefinite period' after the war, which drew criticism from the United States. White House national security spokesperson John Kirby said President Joe Biden does not support reoccupying Gaza, and Secretary of State Antony Blinken stated that a lasting peace requires no post-conflict reoccupation. Israeli officials have since clarified that managing Gaza’s security does not mean Israel intends to administratively govern the enclave, but statements from other officials, including Defence Minister Yoav Gallant, have caused confusion about Israel’s long-term plans. US officials have suggested the Palestinian Authority could govern Gaza after the conflict, though Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas has said this would only be possible with a political solution that returns territory captured in the 1967 Arab-Israeli War. On Thursday, Netanyahu reiterated his opposition to a ceasefire with Hamas, while the Biden administration announced Israel had agreed to daily four-hour pauses in fighting to allow civilians to flee conflict zones. 'A ceasefire with Hamas means surrender to terror,' Netanyahu said, praising Israeli military performance and vowing the campaign would continue 'however long it takes.' Israel has pledged to eliminate Hamas in response to the group’s October 7 attacks, which Israeli officials say killed 1,405 people, mostly civilians. According to Gaza’s Health Ministry, Israeli strikes have killed at least 10,569 Palestinians, including 4,324 children.
translated_content: Premier Izraela, Benjamin Netanjahu, oświadczył, że Izrael nie zamierza okupować ani sprawować rządów w Strefie Gazy po konflikcie z Hamasem, ale podkreśla, że enklawa musi zostać zdemilitaryzowana, zderadykalizowana i odbudowana. W wywiadzie dla Fox News, wyemitowanym w czwartek, Netanjahu powiedział, że Izrael dąży do ustanowienia cywilnego rządu w Gazie po Hamasie, który sprawuje władzę w enklawie od 2006 roku, ale nie wskazał, kto miałby taki rząd utworzyć. "Nie chcemy rządzić Gazą, nie chcemy jej okupować. Chcemy dać jej i sobie lepszą przyszłość – a do tego konieczne jest pokonanie Hamasu" – stwierdził, dodając, że nie ma ustalonego harmonogramu tych działań. Wspólnota międzynarodowa powszechnie postrzega Gazę jako terytorium okupowane, ponieważ Izrael kontroluje jej granice, przestrzeń powietrzną i wody terytorialne, mimo wycofania wojska i osadników w 2005 roku. W 2007 roku Izrael nałożył blokadę na Gazę, którą zdobył wraz z innymi terytoriami palestyńskimi – Wschodnią Jerozolimą i Zachodnim Brzegiem – podczas wojny w 1967 roku. Izrael twierdzi, że wycofanie w 2005 roku zakończyło okupację, ale eksperci prawa międzynarodowego, m.in. były specjalny sprawozdawca ONZ Michael Lynk, utrzymują, że okupacja trwa z powodu efektywnej kontroli Izraela nad Gazą. W wywiadzie Netanjahu wspomniał o potrzebie utrzymania 'wiarygodnej siły', która mogłaby wkraczać do Gazy w razie potrzeby, by przeciwdziałać zagrożeniom i uniemożliwić odrodzenie się struktur podobnych do Hamasu. Jego wypowiedzi pojawiły się po wcześniejszym oświadczeniu, iż Izrael przejmie odpowiedzialność za bezpieczeństwo Strefy Gazy przez 'nieokreślony czas' po wojnie, co spotkało się z krytyką ze strony Stanów Zjednoczonych. Rzecznik Białego Domu ds. bezpieczeństwa narodowego, John Kirby, poinformował, że prezydent Joe Biden nie popiera ponownej okupacji Gazy, a sekretarz stanu Antony Blinken stwierdził, że trwały pokój wymaga braku ponownej okupacji po konflikcie. Izraelscy urzędnicy wyjaśniali później, że zarządzanie bezpieczeństwem Gazy nie oznacza zamiaru administracyjnego rządzenia tą enklawą, jednak wypowiedzi innych polityków, m.in. ministra obrony Yoava Gallanta, wywołały niejasności co do długoterminowych planów Izraela. Przedstawiciele USA zasugerowali, że po zakończeniu konfliktu rządy w Gazie mogłaby przejąć Autonomia Palestyńska, choć prezydent Mahmoud Abbas stwierdził, że jest to możliwe wyłącznie w ramach politycznego rozwiązania przywracającego tereny zajęte przez Izrael w wyniku wojny w 1967 roku. W czwartek Netanjahu ponownie odrzucił możliwość zawieszenia broni z Hamasem, podczas gdy administracja Bidena ogłosiła, że Izrael zgodził się na codzienne czterogodzinne przerwy w walkach, aby cywile mogli opuścić strefy konfliktu. 'Zawieszenie broni z Hamasem to kapitulacja przed terroryzmem' – powiedział Netanjahu, chwaląc postawę izraelskiego wojska i zapowiadając kontynuację operacji 'tak długo, jak będzie to potrzebne'. Izrael zapowiedział eliminację Hamasu w odpowiedzi na atak z 7 października, w którym – według izraelskich władz – zginęło 1405 osób, głównie cywilów. Według Ministerstwa Zdrowia w Gazie izraelskie ataki zabiły co najmniej 10 569 Palestyńczyków, w tym 4 324 dzieci.

article_content:
Australian cyclist Michael Rogers claimed his first Tour de France stage victory by winning the demanding 237.5km 16th stage from Carcassonne to Bagneres-de-Luchon, the longest leg of this year's event. Rogers, representing Tinkoff-Saxo, led a decisive breakaway and finished strongly on the descent into the Pyrenees, earning his team their second victory of the Tour. 

This win was particularly meaningful for Rogers after a previous doping controversy. Earlier in the year, the International Cycling Union (UCI) determined that food contamination likely explained his positive test after a race in China, choosing not to extend punishment beyond his disqualification from the Japan Cup—a conclusion that alleviated stress for Rogers and his family.

Meanwhile, Italian rider Vincenzo Nibali retained the yellow jersey, finishing stage 16 alongside Spain’s Alejandro Valverde about nine minutes after Rogers. Thibaut Pinot of France moved up to third in the general classification, overtaking Romain Bardet, thanks to his performance on the steep ascent to Port de Bales.

Notable finishers in the stage included Jose Serpa (Lampre), Thomas Voeckler and Cyril Gautier (both Europcar), and Vasil Kiriyenka (Sky). The peloton also saw the withdrawal of world champion Rui Costa (Lampre), who left the race due to pneumonia, according to his team following a medical evaluation.

The riders now face Stage 17, the shortest of this year's Tour at 124.5km, featuring three major Category 1 climbs before ending at the Saint-Lary Pla d’Adet ski resort.

Rogers, reprezentujący barwy Tinkoff-Saxo, rozpoczął decydującą ucieczkę i pewnie finiszował na zjeździe w Pirenejach, zapewniając swojej drużynie drugą wygraną w Tourze w tym roku.

Tymczasem Włoch Vincenzo Nibali zachował żółtą koszulkę lidera, kończąc etap razem z Hiszpanem Alejandro Valverde około dziewięć minut po Rogersie. Francuz Thibaut Pinot awansował na trzecie miejsce w klasyfikacji generalnej, wyprzedzając Romaina Bardeta po znakomitym podjeździe na Port de Bales.

article_content: Frank Swain began to lose his hearing at age 20, but instead of simply adapting, he decided to transform his experience by listening to Wi-Fi networks. Working with sound designer Daniel Jones in London, Swain developed a system that translates data from nearby Wi-Fi routers—like their names, data speeds, and security settings—into soundscapes he can perceive with his hearing aids. Each network generates a unique combination of clicks, tones, or musical loops based on its strength and proximity. Swain mapped and recorded the Wi-Fi sounds while walking by BBC Broadcasting House in central London. He shared how the presence or absence of Wi-Fi networks creates a distinct soundtrack that changes as he moves through public spaces or travels underground. What initially felt extraordinary soon felt familiar as part of his daily life. Swain's project, called Phantom Terrains, lets people 'hear' the usually hidden world of wireless signals. For him, it's a way to turn hearing loss into an advantage. In a similar spirit, artist Nickolay Lamm, assisted by ex-NASA astrobiologist M. Browning Vogel, visualized Wi-Fi signals using colors to represent different channels and pulse patterns. Their visualizations, based on real data from areas like the U.S. Congress and National Mall, aim to show how Wi-Fi surrounds us even though we can't see it. Both Swain and Lamm hope their work inspires people to recognize and appreciate the invisible systems that shape our digitally connected world.

article_content: Ali Carter has staged an impressive return to professional snooker following cancer treatment, and is now set to play Shaun Murphy in the General Cup final in Hong Kong. In his first tournament since last season’s World Championship, Carter defeated defending champion Mark Davis 6-2 in the semi-finals, making a notable break of 139. The General Cup features several leading snooker players. Murphy earned his final spot by narrowly beating Joe Perry 6-5, boasting a break of 144 and 80 in the concluding frame. Aged 35, Carter is a two-time World Championship runner-up who has previously faced testicular cancer and continues to manage Crohn’s disease. Carter withdrew from a Players Tour Championship in Sofia due to his final rounds of chemotherapy for lung cancer. Thrilled with his progress, Carter took to Twitter to share his joy at reaching the final, noting how far he has come since his recent health struggles. He and his manager have both posted updates and photos throughout the tournament, marking a significant chapter in Carter’s inspiring comeback.

article_content: Terry Trafford, a 20-year-old hockey player for the Saginaw Spirit of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL), was found dead in his truck in a Michigan parking lot eight days after being reported missing. Michigan State Police notified team officials of the discovery on Tuesday afternoon, according to a statement posted on the Saginaw Spirit website. Trafford, originally from Toronto, was last seen around 9:30 a.m. on March 3 at the Dow Event Center, the club's home arena. The team expressed its condolences, saying 'Our deepest condolences are with Terry's family and his friends both in Ontario and Michigan. Terry played on our team and was a member of the Spirit family for the last four years and he will be missed.' State police Lieutenant Brian Cole told The Saginaw News and WJRT-TV that an officer found a man's body in an SUV matching the description of the vehicle Trafford was last seen driving. The vehicle was parked outside a Walmart in Saginaw Township. 'One of our troopers was patrolling the parking lot, observed a vehicle which appeared to match the description of the vehicle that the missing player was last seen driving,' Cole said. 'He observed a deceased male inside the vehicle.' Police did not immediately indicate a cause of death. The state police crime lab was called to the scene. Trafford was considered a 'voluntary missing person,' according to Cole. Trafford's girlfriend, Skye Cieszlak, said he was devastated and possibly suicidal after being sent home for breaking team rules. She said Trafford texted her that 'his life was over and that he didn't want to do it anymore.' Cieszlak and Trafford had been dating since 2010, and she indicated he had battled depression. Team President and General Manager Craig Goslin stated Trafford was sent home for violating team rules. According to reports, Trafford was caught smoking marijuana on February 22 during a road trip. He was not permanently removed from the team but was expected to change his behavior. During his four seasons with Saginaw, Trafford recorded 29 goals and 49 assists, with eight goals and 24 assists in the current season. Teammate Gregg Sutch remembered Trafford fondly, tweeting, 'Always known for being a prankster in the room, sometimes he drove you up the wall, but no matter what, you loved Traff.' The Saginaw Spirit postponed Wednesday’s scheduled game following Trafford’s passing.

Dziewczyna Trafforda, Skye Cieszlak, powiedziała, że był zrozpaczony i prawdopodobnie miał myśli samobójcze po odesłaniu do domu za złamanie zasad drużyny. Saginaw Spirit odwołał środowy mecz po śmierci Trafforda.

A group of Wisconsin legislators from both major parties has put forward legislation to establish a pilot program studying psilocybin as a potential treatment for veterans with PTSD. The bill, known as LRB-4215, was introduced by Republicans Senator Jesse James and Representative Nate Gustafson, along with Democratic Senator Dianne Hesselbein and Representative Clinton Anderson. If passed, the measure would direct the University of Wisconsin Board of Regents to oversee research evaluating how psilocybin—the psychoactive compound in magic mushrooms—might help veterans aged 21 and older who suffer from post-traumatic stress disorder. The researchers would be expected to report progress and results to both the state’s governor and legislature.

Supporters emphasize the urgent need to offer new options to veterans with treatment-resistant PTSD. Representative Gustafson stated that providing these opportunities is a matter of moral responsibility and commended bipartisan cooperation on the issue. Senator Hesselbein highlighted that supporting veterans’ health should bring lawmakers together above party divides, saying that veterans deserve the best care available and that trying new methods for PTSD relief is an important step.

Scientific interest in psilocybin is growing internationally, as studies from Johns Hopkins University and other institutions have demonstrated its promise in addressing PTSD, depression, anxiety, and substance abuse. A 2020 JAMA Psychiatry publication reported quick and lasting positive outcomes for those with major depressive disorder treated with psilocybin-assisted therapy; earlier research found similar improvements in cancer patients coping with anxiety and depression.

Senator James, commenting on the topic to Wisconsin Public Radio, noted that slow federal action leaves it up to states to advance such research. The program would operate at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, which already houses the Transdisciplinary Center for Research in Psychoactive Substances. The bill proposes an initial allocation of $100,000 for the pilot, with the option to accept private donations to expand research capabilities.

Representative Anderson underscored that the bipartisan nature of the bill signals genuine intent to improve care for veterans: “We should all support expanded treatment options for veterans with PTSD. This effort is about real solutions—not political posturing.”

Senator Hesselbein wskazała, że troska o zdrowie weteranów powinna łączyć polityków ponad partyjnymi podziałami, podkreślając, że zasługują oni na jak najlepszą opiekę i warto testować nowe podejścia w leczeniu PTSD.

W 2020 roku na łamach czasopisma JAMA Psychiatry opublikowano badania, które dowodzą, że terapia z udziałem psylocybiny może przynieść szybką i trwałą poprawę u osób z ciężką depresją. Program pilotażowy prowadzony byłby na Uniwersytecie Wisconsin-Madison, gdzie funkcjonuje już Transdyscyplinarne Centrum Badań nad Substancjami Psychoaktywnymi. Ustawa zakłada przekazanie 100 000 dolarów na rozruch programu oraz możliwość pozyskiwania darowizn na dalsze badania.

Poseł Anderson podsumował, że ponadpartyjna ustawa odzwierciedla rzeczywistą troskę o wsparcie weteranów: „Rozszerzenie możliwości leczenia PTSD u weteranów powinno nas wszystkich łączyć. To realne rozwiązania, nie polityczna gra.”

A Singapore court has denied bail to Lin Baoying, 44, and Zhang Ruijin, 45, a couple facing charges as part of a massive S$2.8 billion (US$2 billion) money laundering probe. The two, both Chinese nationals, are among ten people accused in what is described as Singapore’s largest money laundering investigation.

Authorities have frozen or seized most of their combined S$325 million assets. Lin is charged with forging documents to sell property in Macau and making false claims about her involvement. Zhang faces charges for similar property-related forgeries and creating a fake loan agreement with a Hong Kong company. The couple was arrested in August 2023 after coordinated raids at Sentosa Cove.

According to court filings, Lin controls over S$215 million in assets across cash, bank deposits, cryptocurrency, luxury goods, real estate, and vehicles, and also holds properties abroad in the UK and Philippines. Zhang’s frozen assets total at least S$110 million and include bank accounts, real estate, vehicles, and valuables connected to his family office, Golden Eagle Assets.

Prosecutors opposed bail, citing their considerable overseas wealth and multiple passports held by Lin—from China, Turkey, Dominica, and Cambodia—indicating a significant flight risk. Zhang’s international family ties and travel also factored into the decision. 

The defence argued the two had not tried to flee or tamper with seized assets and stressed their right to liberty. The judge, however, agreed with the prosecution and denied bail, stating both had the means and motivation to leave Singapore if released.
