article_content: Sweden’s largest egg producer, CA Cedergren, which previously had about 1.2 million chickens—accounting for roughly 20% of all laying hens in the country—has been ordered to euthanize its entire flock due to recurring salmonella outbreaks. According to ATL, Sweden’s leading farming news outlet, the Swedish Board of Agriculture has ended further attempts to sanitize the facility, citing repeated salmonella incidents at CA Cedergren over the past year. Katharina Gielen, head of infection control at the Board, told ATL that previous efforts to clean infected hen houses at the southern Sweden company did not succeed. With ongoing re-infection, more drastic measures are now required. The precise number of chickens to be culled has not yet been confirmed. CA Cedergren has not provided an official statement. Earlier, Sweden experienced a brief egg shortage in July following a salmonella outbreak in December 2022 affecting CA Cedergren. In April, authorities halted all deliveries from the company after salmonella bacteria were found in its packing room. In August, another outbreak resulted in the culling of 340,000 chickens at the facility. Marie Lönneskog Hogstadius, spokesperson for the Swedish Eggs industry organization, told Swedish news agency TT that regular consumers are unlikely to be affected by the culling. Eggs from CA Cedergren were instead supplied to the food industry, where they were heat-treated to eliminate salmonella before being used in prepared meals and powdered eggs. Symptoms of salmonella infection include fever, diarrhea, vomiting, and dehydration. Most healthy people recover within a week without treatment.

Według ATL, czołowego portalu rolniczego w Szwecji, Szwedzka Rada ds. Rolnictwa zakończyła dalsze próby dezynfekcji zakładu, powołując się na powtarzające się przypadki salmonelli w CA Cedergren w ciągu ostatniego roku. Firma CA Cedergren nie wydała oficjalnego stanowiska. Wcześniej, w lipcu, w Szwecji wystąpił krótki niedobór jaj na skutek ogniska salmonelli w grudniu 2022 roku, które dotknęło CA Cedergren. Marie Lönneskog Hogstadius, rzeczniczka organizacji branżowej Swedish Eggs, powiedziała szwedzkiej agencji prasowej TT, że zwykli konsumenci raczej nie odczują skutków tej decyzji. article_content: By Lucy Osborne for the Daily Mail. Civil servants are spending several hours each week editing Wikipedia pages on both trivial and sensitive topics—including pages about Sir Elton John and Jurassic Park. Other subjects edited from Whitehall government computers include comedian Roy 'Chubby' Brown, Scottish football clubs, and even Nazi paratroopers. Since January, more than 600 Wikipedia edits—an average of over two every working day—have been traced back to UK government computers. For example, a Wikipedia entry for Roy 'Chubby' Brown was altered from a government computer to add details about his recent conviction for driving without due care and attention. Previously, government computers have been linked to controversial edits of sensitive pages, such as the Hillsborough disaster and the 'spare room subsidy' (referred to by critics as the ‘bedroom tax’). In June, a 24-year-old civil servant was dismissed after changing the phrase ‘You’ll never walk alone’—the Liverpool FC anthem—to ‘You’ll never walk again’ in the Hillsborough disaster article back in 2012. A Daily Mail investigation has now found that government computers have made thousands of changes to less serious subjects on Wikipedia in recent years, raising questions about civil servants’ use of work time on these activities. Anyone can edit Wikipedia, which is the sixth most visited website in the world, drawing nearly 500 million unique visitors each month. Every edit is recorded, showing the user or IP address, allowing edits to be traced—such as those made from Whitehall networks. In just the past two days, edits from government computers included adding band member names to Hatful Of Rain, correcting a song title on Elton John’s page, and updating a list of episodes for Horrible Histories. Other topics changed included Roy 'Chubby' Brown, Jurassic Park, Shirley Valentine, curry, the SAS, and presenter Des Lynam. At least 15 edits last month were made to pages about Scottish football clubs. Jonathan Isaby from the TaxPayers’ Alliance commented: 'Taxpayers aren’t paying Whitehall mandarins to edit interesting websites—they’re paying them to help run the country. The clue is in the name; civil servants are there to serve civil society, not to take it easy in the office. Taxpayers won’t be impressed.' Although Wikipedia is open for editing by anyone, it has a network of volunteer administrators who can remove false or inappropriate content. Content flagged by users is reviewed by administrators, and a central committee appoints moderators and senior editors. A government spokesperson stated: 'Civil servants are required to follow the Civil Service Code when working online.'

Z komputerów rządowych w Whitehallu edytowano także hasła o komiku Royu 'Chubby' Brownie, szkockich klubach piłkarskich, a nawet niemieckich spadochroniarzach z czasów nazistowskich. article_content: My Friend Cayla has been introduced as the world’s first interactive, internet-connected doll. Dressed stylishly with long, fair hair, Cayla can converse about hobbies and assist children with their homework. By connecting with a smartphone or tablet, she interprets and responds to children’s speech, engaging in straightforward dialogues. When a child poses a question, Cayla uses Google-powered voice recognition software to transcribe the query, searches online for answers, and then communicates her findings. According to the manufacturer, Vivid, this allows children to enjoy meaningful exchanges with their new companion. Cayla’s internet browsing is managed through Google’s SafeSearch filters, which block inappropriate content. Additionally, parents can use the dedicated app to restrict certain words or topics. If Cayla hears swearing or sensitive references such as race or body parts, her online search is automatically halted. In these cases, she will either redirect the conversation or stay silent. At 18 inches tall and priced at £59.99, Cayla is also designed to foster role-play and dress-up alongside her interactive features. Though some have drawn parallels to the idea of high-tech, lifelike robots in works like ‘The Stepford Wives,’ Vivid maintains that Cayla offers only positive and educational experiences. Children can listen to stories, play games, and get homework tips while sharing discussions about everything from math and general knowledge to the weather. Even without internet access, Cayla can tell stories and play pre-programmed games. Cayla made her debut at the annual Toy Fair in London’s Olympia, joining other innovative hi-tech dolls. These include the VTech Little Love—a baby doll that grows with the child, speaks over 100 words and 80 phrases, and costs £24.99—as well as Nenuco Won’t Eat, a doll designed to encourage proper eating by refusing food until persistent efforts succeed. This new generation of interactive toys reflects a broader trend toward virtual companionship and educational support through advanced technology.

article_content: Rebecca Leighton, a 27-year-old nurse, has been charged in connection with the deaths of five patients at Stepping Hill Hospital in Stockport, which is currently under police investigation for possible medical supply tampering. Leighton faces six counts of criminal damage with intent to endanger life under the Criminal Damage Act, as well as one count of theft of medicine from the hospital. She is scheduled to appear before magistrates at Manchester Magistrates' Court. If found guilty, she could face a life sentence. Greater Manchester Police began their investigation after five unexplained deaths at the hospital. They confirmed Leighton’s charges and stated she is suspected of causing damage with intent or recklessness in endangering life. Police identified Vera Pearson, 84, as the fifth victim. Derek Weaver, 83, who died recently, is also linked to the investigation. Pearson was not among the 14 patients initially thought to have received saline contaminated with insulin. Her family requested privacy. Police are continuing their investigation, including questioning Leighton regarding the deaths of George Keep, 84, Arnold Lancaster, 71, and Tracey Arden, 44. Leighton, born at Stepping Hill Hospital, was described by colleagues as a dedicated nurse. She was arrested at 6am on Wednesday at her apartment, which she shares with her fiancé, Tim Papworth, 28. Chris Burke, chief executive of Stockport NHS Foundation Trust, stated that the staff is shocked and appalled by the events and that support is being provided to those affected. Nazir Afzal, Chief Crown Prosecutor for CPS North West, explained that the charges are serious, alleging that Leighton tampered with saline ampoules and bags, endangering patients' lives. Afzal emphasized that the investigation is ongoing and said that additional charges could follow if more evidence becomes available. Rebecca Leighton has been a registered nurse since 2008. Derek Weaver was a retired businessman who reportedly deteriorated suddenly after a severe low blood sugar episode on July 11. His sister, Lynda Bleasdale, praised the hospital staff and described Weaver as a charming and lovely gentleman. Police continue to question visitors to Stepping Hill Hospital.

article_content: 'jOBS', a film about the early years of Apple co-founder Steve Jobs, premiered Friday night at the Sundance Film Festival to mixed reviews. Some critics say the movie presents a one-sided, praise-filled portrayal of Jobs. Ashton Kutcher stars as Steve Jobs, covering his time at Reed College, the 1984 launch of the Macintosh, and the 2001 unveiling of the iPod. Josh Gad plays Steve Wozniak, Jobs' business partner. The film highlights Jobs' significant impact on the personal computer industry. Casey Newton of CNET criticized the film for repeatedly having minor characters doubt Jobs, only for Kutcher’s Jobs to dismiss their concerns. Newton notes the script does not allow co-workers to present strong arguments, assigning all failures to conservative executives and making supporting roles seem flat. Matthew Panzarino from The Next Web offered a more favorable review. He notes there are inaccuracies and that the film omits much of the technical development of the Macintosh and Lisa computers but feels it succeeds as a depiction of a certain period in Jobs’ life. While there was skepticism about Kutcher’s ability to portray Jobs, reviewers found his performance convincing. Both noted his effective imitation of Jobs’ voice, gestures, and characteristic walk. Controversy arose after a scene from the movie went online, which Steve Wozniak labeled inaccurate, explaining to Gizmodo that the interaction between himself and Jobs never happened as shown. The filmmakers responded that 'jOBS' is a feature film dramatization, not intended as a precise, factual account of all conversations and events. Steve Jobs died in October 2011 after a long illness. The film is scheduled for theatrical release on April 19. Another movie about Jobs, written by Aaron Sorkin and based on Walter Isaacson’s biography, is in production with Steve Wozniak acting as consultant.

article_content: On Wednesday, China sharply denounced the new update from the U.S. Commerce Department that tightens controls on the export of advanced computer chips and related manufacturing equipment to China. The updated rules, announced on Tuesday, are designed to block high-tech chip exports that might aid Chinese military initiatives, specifically in fields like hypersonic weapons and artificial intelligence. China’s Commerce Ministry condemned the U.S. controls as ‘improper’ and urged their immediate removal. The Ministry’s statement emphasized that because the semiconductor sector is heavily globalized, U.S. restrictions are undermining routine commerce, breaking international trade standards, and posing serious risks to the stability of industrial supply chains. Chinese officials claim these export limits have resulted in major losses for U.S. and international chipmakers, and warned that China would take whatever steps are necessary to defend its interests. Speaking to journalists, U.S. Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo explained that the restrictions are carefully focused on technologies presenting national security or human rights risks. She clarified that most chips remain unaffected, but stressed that when security or human rights concerns are identified, the U.S. will act decisively, often in coordination with allies. Raimondo noted these rules followed industry consultation and expert assessment. The revised controls impose further limits—not just on U.S. exports to China, but also to companies in places like Macau or under U.S. arms embargoes—to plug potential loopholes. The list of controlled manufacturing technology has expanded, too. U.S. authorities have signaled increased scrutiny for products in a ‘gray zone’ that could still support military uses. The new restrictions also complicate China’s efforts to manufacture advanced chips overseas. China considers mastery of advanced semiconductors central to its economic and global ambitions. Raimondo reiterated U.S. assurances that the intention isn’t to suppress Chinese economic growth. An August meeting between Raimondo and Chinese officials resulted in an agreement to keep sharing information about export controls, though a U.S. official stated there was no discussion of the new rule specifics. Chinese officials are preparing to take part in November’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in San Francisco, where a possible, though yet unconfirmed, meeting between President Joe Biden and President Xi Jinping may occur. The two leaders last spoke in person at the Bali Group of 20 summit, shortly after initial chip export controls were introduced.

Nowe przepisy, ogłoszone we wtorek, mają zablokować eksport zaawansowanych technologicznie chipów, które mogą wspierać chińskie projekty wojskowe, zwłaszcza w takich dziedzinach jak broń hipersoniczna i sztuczna inteligencja. Chińskie Ministerstwo Handlu skrytykowało amerykańskie ograniczenia jako „nieodpowiednie” i zaapelowało o ich natychmiastowe zniesienie. Resort podkreślił, że rynek półprzewodników jest mocno zglobalizowany, a działania USA szkodzą prawidłowej wymianie handlowej, naruszają międzynarodowe normy i poważnie zagrażają stabilności łańcuchów dostaw przemysłu. Chińscy urzędnicy twierdzą, iż restrykcje spowodowały poważne straty zarówno dla amerykańskich, jak i międzynarodowych producentów chipów, oraz zapowiedzieli, że Chiny podejmą wszelkie konieczne działania w celu ochrony swoich interesów. Sekretarz handlu USA Gina Raimondo podkreśliła w rozmowie z dziennikarzami, że ograniczenia dotyczą jedynie technologii stanowiących potencjalne zagrożenie dla bezpieczeństwa narodowego lub praw człowieka. Zaznaczyła, że większość chipów nie podlega żadnym restrykcjom, natomiast w sytuacji zagrożenia bezpieczeństwa lub praw człowieka USA będą działać zdecydowanie, często wraz z sojusznikami. Raimondo wskazała, że przepisy powstały po konsultacjach z branżą i analizach ekspertów. Zmienione regulacje obejmują dodatkowe ograniczenia – nie tylko dla eksportu do Chin, ale także do firm z Makau czy państw objętych embargiem na broń USA – celem uszczelnienia systemu. Rozszerzono też listę sprzętu podlegającego kontroli eksportowej. Amerykańskie władze deklarują wzmożony nadzór nad „szarą strefą” produktów, które mogą trafić do zastosowań wojskowych, nawet gdy formalnie nie podlegają restrykcjom. Nowe przepisy mają również utrudnić Chinom produkcję zaawansowanych chipów poza granicami kraju. Władze Chin uznają rozwój sektora półprzewodników za kluczowy dla swoich ambitnych celów gospodarczych i politycznych. Raimondo zapewniła, że działania USA nie są wymierzone w zahamowanie rozwoju gospodarczego Chin. Podczas sierpniowego spotkania Raimondo z chińskimi partnerami uzgodniono wymianę informacji o ograniczeniach eksportowych, choć – według anonimowego urzędnika – szczegóły nowych regulacji nie były wówczas omawiane. Chińska delegacja zamierza wziąć udział w listopadowym szczycie APEC w San Francisco, gdzie być może – choć wciąż nie ma potwierdzenia – dojdzie do rozmów prezydentów Joe Bidena i Xi Jinpinga. Ostatnio przywódcy tych krajów spotkali się na G20 w Bali, krótko po ogłoszeniu pierwszych kontroli eksportu chipów.

article_content: Eric Sinacori, a 20-year-old junior at UMass Amherst on a scholarship, struggled with substance abuse problems. His father and stepmother discovered his body in the bathroom next to a needle and syringe. Sinacori’s parents were unaware of his heroin problem. Previously, UMass police had found a hypodermic needle after catching him dealing club drugs. Rather than arresting Sinacori or informing his family, UMass police made him a confidential informant and then released him from that role without further support. UMass Police Chief John Horvath told the Boston Globe, 'You’re always looking to move up the ladder and get an individual that is more of a threat to our community.' The university has since suspended its confidential informant program and is conducting a thorough review. A memorial scholarship was established in Sinacori's name. Family and friends remember him as a passionate young man who played high school hockey in New Jersey and attended UMass on scholarship. The university became aware of Sinacori’s drug involvement after another confidential informant reported he was dealing Molly (MDMA). With help from a DEA agent, university police arranged two undercover buys of Molly and LSD from Sinacori in late 2012. After the officer identified himself, Sinacori was offered a deal to avoid prosecution by working as an informant. Sinacori then helped arrange a drug purchase from another student, leading to arrests and suspensions for those involved. Sinacori did not face criminal or academic penalties, nor were his parents informed. Text messages revealed Sinacori struggled with the stress of his role and continuing addiction. Police returned $700 in cash taken from his dorm, keeping only a hypodermic needle. In the days before his death, Sinacori texted about heroin withdrawal and arranged a purchase. On the night he died, he received heroin labeled 'Tropicana' and later overdosed. He did not respond to subsequent messages, and his mother later angrily texted the alleged dealer from his phone. UMass is reviewing its informant program amid concerns about undetected heroin use on campus. Former student Maddie Schnier noted the ease of obtaining heroin at the university.
translated_content: Eric Sinacori, 20-letni student trzeciego roku Uniwersytetu Massachusetts Amherst na stypendium, zmagał się z uzależnieniem od substancji. Jego ojciec i macocha znaleźli go martwego w łazience obok igły i strzykawki. Rodzice Sinacoriego nie wiedzieli o jego problemach z heroiną. Wcześniej policja uniwersytecka znalazła u niego igłę, gdy przyłapano go na handlu narkotykami klubowymi. Zamiast aresztować Sinacoriego lub poinformować rodzinę, policja UMass zrobiła z niego tajnego informatora, po czym zwolniła go z tej roli bez wsparcia. Komendant policji UMass, John Horvath, powiedział Boston Globe: „Zawsze staramy się dotrzeć wyżej i złapać osobę, która stanowi większe zagrożenie dla naszej społeczności”. Uniwersytet zawiesił obecnie program informatorów i poddaje go szczegółowej analizie. Ustanowiono stypendium upamiętniające Sinacoriego. Rodzina i znajomi wspominają go jako pełnego pasji młodego człowieka, który grał w hokeja w liceum w New Jersey i studiował w UMass dzięki stypendium. O zaangażowaniu Sinacoriego w narkotyki uczelnia dowiedziała się dzięki innemu tajnemu informatorowi, który powiedział policji, że handlował Molly (MDMA). Z pomocą agenta DEA, uczelniana policja przeprowadziła dwa zakupy kontrolowane Molly i LSD od Sinacoriego pod koniec 2012 roku. Po ujawnieniu tożsamości przez funkcjonariusza, Sinacori dostał propozycję uniknięcia zarzutów w zamian za zostanie informatorem. Następnie pomógł zorganizować zakup narkotyków od innego studenta, co doprowadziło do ich aresztowania i zawieszenia. On sam nie poniósł żadnych konsekwencji prawnych ani akademickich, a jego rodzice nie zostali poinformowani. Wiadomości tekstowe pokazują, że Sinacori zmagał się zarówno ze stresem związanym z byciem informatorem, jak i uzależnieniem. Policja zwróciła mu 700 dolarów skonfiskowanych z jego pokoju, zatrzymując jedynie igłę. Kilka dni przed śmiercią Sinacori pisał o głodzie narkotykowym i organizował zakup heroiny. W noc śmierci otrzymał heroinę o nazwie „Tropicana” i przyjął ją. Nie odpowiedział na późniejsze wiadomości, a jego mama napisała z jego telefonu gniewną wiadomość do domniemanego dilera. UMass prowadzi przegląd programu informatorów w trosce o możliwy nierozpoznany problem heroinowy na kampusie. Była studentka Maddie Schnier zwróciła uwagę na łatwość zdobycia heroiny na uczelni.

article_content: Thailand is intensifying its efforts to establish itself as a regional electric vehicle (EV) powerhouse by offering a variety of incentives and tax exemptions for car manufacturers setting up EV research and development centers, as announced by a government official on Thursday. Holding the title as Southeast Asia's top vehicle producer and exporter, Thailand has long been a key market for major Japanese brands such as Toyota, Isuzu, and Honda. The Thai government aims to make 30% of its annual car production—estimated at 2.5 million vehicles—electric by 2030. New benefits are being introduced to attract investments and encourage existing factories to convert to EV production. According to Narit Therdsteerasukdi, Secretary General of the Board of Investment, strengthening research and development initiatives is central to boosting Thailand's global competitiveness. Tax relief and grants will reward carmakers who invest in EV research in Thailand, with further benefits for those moving their regional headquarters to the country. The full value of the incentive package has not been specified. Chinese car manufacturers are investing heavily, with combined commitments of $1.44 billion for new production plants. BYD stands out with plans to invest nearly $500 million and manufacture 150,000 electric vehicles per year. Great Wall Motor has also expressed interest in opening an R&D center in Thailand, possibly focusing on battery-powered pickup trucks, a staple of the local market. Japanese companies with existing R&D centers—Toyota, Honda, Nissan, Mitsubishi—are being encouraged to ramp up their development of EVs domestically. Narit emphasized government support to help these automakers transition to electric vehicles. A government subsidy—up to 150,000 baht ($4,100) per EV—has already spurred significant sales growth, accounting for nearly half of Southeast Asia's EV sales in the second quarter of this year. An updated 'EV 3.5 package' is forthcoming, lowering the per-EV subsidy to 100,000 baht, with roll-out set for January after final approval later this year. This initiative is expected to cost around 3 billion baht, based on research from BMI. (Current exchange rate: $1 = 36.21 baht).
translated_content: Tajlandia intensyfikuje starania, by stać się regionalnym liderem w dziedzinie pojazdów elektrycznych (EV), oferując producentom samochodów różne zachęty i ulgi podatkowe na zakładanie centrów badań i rozwoju EV — poinformował w czwartek przedstawiciel rządu. Jako największy producent i eksporter samochodów w Azji Południowo-Wschodniej, Tajlandia od lat jest kluczowym rynkiem dla głównych japońskich marek, takich jak Toyota, Isuzu czy Honda. Rząd planuje, aby do 2030 roku 30% z około 2,5 miliona aut produkowanych rocznie stanowiły pojazdy elektryczne. Wprowadzane są nowe zachęty, by przyciągać inwestorów i motywować istniejące fabryki do przejścia na produkcję EV. Narit Therdsteerasukdi, sekretarz generalny Rady Inwestycji, podkreśla, że rozwój badań i innowacji jest kluczowy dla utrzymania konkurencyjności Tajlandii. Firmy inwestujące w badania nad EV otrzymają ulgi podatkowe i dotacje, a dodatkowe korzyści przewidziano dla tych, którzy przeniosą do kraju swoje siedziby regionalne. Szczegóły wartości pakietu nie zostały ujawnione. Chińscy producenci samochodów zobowiązali się do inwestycji o łącznej wartości 1,44 miliarda dolarów w nowe fabryki. BYD planuje przeznaczyć prawie 500 milionów dolarów na produkcję 150 000 aut elektrycznych rocznie. Firma Great Wall Motor rozważa otwarcie ośrodka badań i rozwoju w Tajlandii, być może skoncentrowanego na elektrycznych pickupach, które cieszą się popularnością na lokalnym rynku. Japońskie firmy posiadające już centra R&D — Toyota, Honda, Nissan, Mitsubishi — są zachęcane do rozwoju technologii EV na miejscu. Narit zapewnia, że rząd wspiera dotychczasowych producentów w przejściu na pojazdy elektryczne. Dotacja w wysokości do 150 000 bahtów (4 100 USD) na EV od rządu już znacząco zwiększyła sprzedaż, stanowiąc niemal połowę wszystkich transakcji EV w regionie w drugim kwartale tego roku. Trwa przygotowanie nowego pakietu 'EV 3.5', który obniży subsydium do 100 000 bahtów na pojazd. Jego wdrożenie przewidziano na styczeń po zatwierdzeniu jeszcze w tym roku. Koszt programu szacowany jest na około 3 miliardy bahtów według firmy BMI. (Aktualny kurs wymiany: 1 USD = 36,21 bahta).

article_content: Prime Minister Rishi Sunak is under internal cabinet pressure to restrict visas for foreign NHS and care workers, as Conservative MPs urge prompt, robust action to meet the party’s migration reduction pledges. Immigration Minister Robert Jenrick has put forward a five-point strategy—supported by the New Conservative group of around 20 MPs—to strengthen the UK’s migration policies. The group’s leader, Miriam Cates, argues in The Telegraph that unchecked migration could have longer-lasting consequences than tax policy, warning that mass immigration is fundamentally changing Britain. According to The Times, Jenrick’s plan would stop international students from staying in the UK after their studies and limit how many family members migrants can bring. While these steps faced previous resistance over economic concerns, newly released migration data has prompted the Treasury to seriously consider them. Sunak is expected to announce new measures as early as next month. The Daily Mail reports that former Home Secretary Suella Braverman has launched a Tory revolt in response to new migration statistics, calling them a 'bombshell.' Braverman stated on social media that the pressure on housing, the NHS, and communities from migration has become unsustainable, and called for Sunak to act immediately. The Daily Express raises fears that migration may soon become unmanageable, while the Daily Mirror accuses the Conservatives of 'breaking Britain' due to failures on immigration, economic policy, household costs, and the Covid response. Elsewhere, the Financial Times reports that British tech entrepreneur Lawrence Jones was convicted of raping two women in the 1990s and sexually assaulting another during her employment at his company, UKFast. The Guardian reports that, through an old legal system, King Charles III receives estates in parts of northern England from people who die without will or heirs. These assets revert to the Duchy of Lancaster, the king’s estate, with proceeds reportedly used for property renovations. The Duchy claims that any surplus after costs is donated to charity. Finally, The Telegraph says senior Treasury officials have floated the idea of an early Budget—sparking talk of a possible early election—though official plans still point to a March budget.

Minister ds. imigracji, Robert Jenrick, zaproponował pięciopunktową strategię — wspieraną przez grupę New Conservative liczącą około 20 posłów — mającą na celu zaostrzenie polityki migracyjnej. Liderka tej grupy, Miriam Cates, stwierdziła na łamach The Telegraph, że brak kontroli nad migracją może mieć poważniejsze skutki niż polityka podatkowa, ostrzegając, że masowa migracja trwale zmienia Wielką Brytanię. Według The Times plan Jenricka ma uniemożliwić zagranicznym studentom pozostanie w Wielkiej Brytanii po studiach i ograniczyć liczbę członków rodzin, których migranci mogą sprowadzić. Choć dotąd budziły one sprzeciw ze względu na obawy gospodarcze, nowe dane o migracji sprawiły, że skarb państwa poważnie rozważa te rozwiązania. Oczekuje się, że Sunak ogłosi takie zmiany już w przyszłym miesiącu. Jak donosi Daily Mail, była minister spraw wewnętrznych Suella Braverman rozpoczęła bunt wśród torysów w reakcji na nowe dane o migracji, nazywając je „bombą”. Braverman napisała w mediach społecznościowych, że napór na mieszkania, NHS i spójność społeczną powodowany przez migrację staje się nie do utrzymania, i wezwała Sunaka do natychmiastowego działania. Daily Express wyraża obawę, że migracja może wkrótce osiągnąć punkt bez powrotu, natomiast Daily Mirror oskarża torysów o „niszczenie Wielkiej Brytanii”, wskazując na porażki rządu dotyczące migracji, gospodarki, kosztów życia i reakcji na pandemię. Financial Times informuje, że brytyjski przedsiębiorca technologiczny Lawrence Jones został skazany za gwałty na dwóch kobietach w latach 90. oraz za napaść seksualną na trzecią kobietę, będącą pracownicą jego firmy UKFast. Guardian opisuje, jak zgodnie z dawnym prawem, król Karol III otrzymuje majątki w północnej Anglii po osobach zmarłych bez testamentu i spadkobierców. Te nieruchomości trafiają do księstwa Lancaster — królewskiej posiadłości — a dochody mają być przeznaczane na remonty majątku; księstwo twierdzi, że nadwyżki po rozliczeniu kosztów przekazywane są na cele charytatywne. Na koniec, The Telegraph pisze, że wysocy urzędnicy skarbu rozważają wcześniejsze ogłoszenie budżetu, wywołując spekulacje o możliwych przedterminowych wyborach, choć oficjalnie planowane jest przedstawienie budżetu w marcu.

article_content: David Cameron and Boris Johnson, often seen as potential rivals for the Conservative Party leadership, presented a united front as they campaigned together for the upcoming Newark by-election. On the trail, the Prime Minister laughed, joked, and bought a slice of rocky road cake for the London Mayor, displaying friendly rapport. Their joint appearance outside London drew parallels to the 2005 Labour photo op, when Tony Blair bought Gordon Brown ice cream while under pressure about his leadership plans. Cameron and Johnson toured Newark market stalls, exchanged banter about baking, and posed for photos with babies and locals. The Prime Minister’s gesture of buying cake for Johnson reminded observers of Blair’s attempt to counter rumors of discord. The two spent several hours mingling with the public, taking selfies, and handing out leaflets in support of Conservative candidate Robert Jenrick, following the resignation of former MP Patrick Mercer. UKIP leader Nigel Farage chose not to stand in the by-election, so MEP Roger Helmer represented UKIP instead. At Les Flowerdew’s bakery stall, Cameron bought Johnson a £1 slice of rocky road, joking, 'That’s a gift. Rocky Road... you know you want it.' Johnson teased Cameron’s baking skills, and both agreed the cake was excellent. During their walkabout, Cameron and Johnson answered questions from locals about hospital services, crime, schools, and VAT rates. Cameron emphasized government investment in the NHS and said Newark hospital would remain open, though he could not promise to scrap the 20% VAT if re-elected. Resident Brian Boby confronted the Prime Minister about Newark's hospital and ambulance services, expressing concern about service levels and police presence. Cameron responded by highlighting increases in healthcare staffing and reaffirmed commitment to improving ambulance services. Winning Newark is seen as important for the Conservatives to show they can resist the UKIP challenge before the 2015 general election.
translated_content: David Cameron i Boris Johnson, często postrzegani jako potencjalni rywale o przywództwo w Partii Konserwatywnej, pokazali jedność, wspólnie prowadząc kampanię przed zbliżającymi się wyborami uzupełniającymi w Newark. Premier żartował, śmiał się i kupił Johnsonowi plasterek ciasta rocky road, pokazując przyjacielskie relacje. Ich wspólne wystąpienie poza Londynem przywołało skojarzenia z akcją Labour z 2005 roku, kiedy Tony Blair kupił Gordonowi Brownowi lody pod presją dotyczącą planów przekazania władzy. Cameron i Johnson odwiedzili stoiska na targu w Newark, żartowali o pieczeniu i pozowali do zdjęć z dziećmi i mieszkańcami. Gest premiera, który kupił ciasto Johnsonowi, dla wielu przypomniał próbę Blaira przeciwdziałania pogłoskom o niezgodzie. Obaj politycy spędzili kilka godzin wśród ludzi, robiąc selfie i rozdając ulotki popierające kandydata konserwatystów Roberta Jenricka, po rezygnacji z funkcji przez byłego posła Patricka Mercera. Lider UKIP Nigel Farage nie kandydował, dlatego partię reprezentował eurodeputowany Roger Helmer. Na stoisku piekarni Lesa Flowerdewa Cameron kupił Johnsonowi plasterek rocky road za 1 funta, żartując: 'To prezent. Rocky Road... wiesz, że masz na to ochotę.' Johnson żartował z umiejętności pieczenia Camerona, a obaj uznali ciasto za znakomite. Podczas rozmów z mieszkańcami Cameron i Johnson odpowiadali na pytania dotyczące szpitala, przestępczości, szkół oraz stawki VAT. Premier podkreślił rządowe inwestycje w NHS i zapewnił, że szpital w Newark pozostanie otwarty, choć nie mógł obiecać zniesienia 20% VAT w razie reelekcji. Mieszkaniec Brian Boby zwrócił uwagę premierowi na problemy szpitala i pogotowia w Newark, wyrażając też obawy o poziom usług i obecność policji. Cameron odpowiedział, że liczba personelu medycznego wzrosła i zapewnił, że poprawa działania pogotowia jest priorytetem. Zwycięstwo w Newark uznawane jest za kluczowe dla konserwatystów, by udowodnić, że mogą przeciwstawić się UKIP przed wyborami w 2015 roku.

article_content: Moscow, Russia — The mortality rate in Moscow has 'doubled recently' due to a prolonged period of heat and smog, according to Andrei Seltsovsky, the head of the city's health department, who spoke to Russian news agencies on Monday. Seltsovsky reported that the average daily mortality rate in Moscow typically ranges from 360 to 380, but currently stands at about 700. Of the 1,500 available spaces in city morgues, 1,300 were occupied. The Russian Health and Social Development Ministry stated on its website Monday that the number of deaths directly attributed to the country's ongoing wildfires remains at 52. Additionally, 62 people across Russia are hospitalized with wildfire-related illnesses, and a total of 741 have sought medical assistance as a result of the fires. The ministry added that 22 out of Russia's 83 regions, mostly in central parts of the country, have been affected by wildfires. Temperatures are forecast to remain high in central and northwestern Russia through August 20, with no immediate relief in sight. According to the Russian meteorological service Roshydromet, air pollution levels in and around Moscow are expected to remain high in the coming days. The agency reported that the air contains byproducts of burning forests and peat, as well as toxic emissions from vehicles and industries. Roshydromet called on Moscow's industrial businesses to reduce emissions by 20 to 40 percent from Monday afternoon through Wednesday afternoon to help ease air pollution. Alexander Frolov, head of Roshydromet, appeared on Russian state television Monday, noting that high pollutant levels in Moscow's air pose a significant health risk. He said the highest concentration of particulate dust, recorded on August 7 and 8, exceeded permitted levels by 3.4 times. This accumulation is particularly hazardous, as it remains in the human body. Frolov also noted that carbon monoxide and ozone levels surpassed allowed norms. 'We have likely experienced the worst period so far, with dangerous levels of pollutants resulting first from vehicle and industrial emissions, and second from extensive forest fires,' he said. Most of the Moscow region and the broader European part of Russia remain at high risk for wildfires, with many areas rated at the fifth, or emergency, hazard level according to Roshydromet's fire risk index. Forests in the southwest, south, and southeast of the Moscow region are especially prone to fires, largely due to the presence of peat bogs. Russia's emergency ministry told state media RIA Novosti on Sunday that 276 wildfires have been extinguished, but 554 are still burning, covering more than 190,000 hectares (over 730 square miles). Frolov said these dire conditions are having a severe impact on Russia's agriculture as well. Precipitation is not expected in August, making it difficult to plan for winter crops in many regions. Roshydromet forecasts up to a 30 percent reduction in Russia's harvests due to drought. Prime Minister Vladimir Putin announced a ban on grain exports last week, effective August 15 through at least December 31. The ban is in response to uncertainty over this year's agricultural output. The government will review the ban's duration once the harvest results are clear. Some regions will not be planting winter grain at all this year, so the export ban is expected to remain in place for an extended period. 'This is a temporary measure, but we are in an extraordinary situation and must consider the needs of our citizens and farmers,' Putin said at a government meeting broadcast Monday on state television. He noted Russia needs about 78 million metric tons of grain to supply its population this year; current estimates suggest only 60 to 65 million metric tons may be harvested, making it necessary to draw from the state intervention fund. Frolov remarked on Monday that the current heat is unprecedented, stating, 'Neither we nor our ancestors have observed anything like it within a thousand-year period since the founding of our country. This kind of phenomenon is absolutely unique.' CNN's Maxim Tkachenko contributed to this report.
translated_content: Moskwa, Rosja — Współczynnik śmiertelności w Moskwie "podwoił się ostatnio" z powodu długotrwałej fali upałów i smogu, poinformował Andriej Selcowski, szef miejskiego departamentu zdrowia, cytowany przez rosyjskie agencje informacyjne w poniedziałek. Selcowski podał, że przeciętna dzienna liczba zgonów w Moskwie wynosi zwykle od 360 do 380, ale obecnie sięga około 700. Z 1 500 dostępnych miejsc w miejskich kostnicach, zajętych jest 1 300. Rosyjskie Ministerstwo Zdrowia i Rozwoju Społecznego poinformowało w poniedziałek na swojej stronie internetowej, że liczba zgonów bezpośrednio związanych z trwającymi pożarami lasów wynosi 52. Ponadto 62 osoby w całej Rosji są hospitalizowane w związku z chorobami wywołanymi przez pożary, a łącznie 741 osób zwróciło się po pomoc medyczną. Resort dodał, że 22 z 83 regionów Rosji, głównie w centralnych częściach kraju, zostało dotkniętych pożarami. Przewiduje się, że wysokie temperatury utrzymają się w centralnej i północno-zachodniej Rosji do 20 sierpnia, bez oznak poprawy. Według rosyjskiej służby meteorologicznej Rosgidromet, w nadchodzących dniach poziom zanieczyszczenia powietrza w Moskwie i okolicy pozostanie wysoki. Agencja poinformowała, że powietrze wciąż zawiera produkty spalania lasów i torfowisk oraz toksyczne emisje z pojazdów i przemysłu. Rosgidromet zaapelował do moskiewskich zakładów przemysłowych o redukcję emisji o 20–40 procent od poniedziałku po południu do środy po południu, by pomóc ograniczyć zanieczyszczenie powietrza. Aleksandr Frolow, szef Rosgidrometu, pojawił się w poniedziałek w rosyjskiej telewizji państwowej, zaznaczając, że wysoki poziom zanieczyszczeń stanowi poważne zagrożenie dla zdrowia mieszkańców Moskwy. Powiedział, że najwyższe stężenia pyłu zawieszonego zaobserwowano 7 i 8 sierpnia, przekraczając dopuszczalne normy 3,4-krotnie. To szczególnie niebezpieczne, ponieważ pył akumuluje się w organizmie. Frolow dodał, że poziomy tlenku węgla i ozonu także przekroczyły normy. "Najprawdopodobniej przeżyliśmy najgorszy dotąd okres, z bardzo wysokim poziomem szkodliwych substancji — najpierw przez emisje z pojazdów i przemysłu, potem przez rozległe pożary," powiedział. Większość regionu moskiewskiego i europejskiej części Rosji pozostaje w strefie bardzo wysokiego ryzyka pożarowego, według indeksu Rosgidrometu oznaczonej piątą klasą zagrożenia. Lasy na południowym zachodzie, południu i południowym wschodzie regionu moskiewskiego są szczególnie narażone na pożary, głównie z powodu torfowisk. Ministerstwo ds. sytuacji nadzwyczajnych przekazało państwowej agencji RIA Nowosti w niedzielę, że ugaszono już 276 pożarów, jednak nadal płonie 554, zajmując obszar ponad 190 tys. hektarów (ponad 730 mil kwadratowych). Frolow wskazał, że obecne trudne warunki znacząco wpływają także na rosyjskie rolnictwo. W sierpniu nie przewiduje się opadów, co utrudnia siew ozimin w wielu regionach. Rosgidromet szacuje, że zbiory zmniejszą się w tym roku nawet o 30 procent z powodu suszy. Premier Władimir Putin ogłosił w zeszłym tygodniu zakaz eksportu zboża, obowiązujący od 15 sierpnia do co najmniej 31 grudnia. Zakaz to odpowiedź na niepewność dotyczącą tegorocznej produkcji rolnej. Rząd podejmie decyzję o terminie zniesienia embarga po poznaniu wyników żniw. W niektórych regionach nie zostanie zasiana ozimina, dlatego zakaz potrwa dłużej. "To środek tymczasowy, ale mamy wyjątkową sytuację i musimy zadbać o naszych obywateli oraz rolników" — powiedział Putin podczas poniedziałkowego posiedzenia rządu transmitowanego w telewizji. Rosja potrzebuje około 78 mln ton zboża na własne potrzeby w tym roku, ale z powodu suszy może zebrać jedynie 60–65 mln ton, co zmusi do sięgnięcia po rezerwy państwowe. Frolow podkreślił w poniedziałek, że obecna fala upałów jest bezprecedensowa, mówiąc: "Ani my, ani nasi przodkowie nie zaobserwowaliśmy czegoś podobnego w ciągu tysiąca lat od założenia naszego kraju. To zjawisko jest zupełnie wyjątkowe." Współautorem materiału jest Maxim Tkaczenko z CNN.

article_content: A privately-owned Cessna 182 entered restricted Los Angeles airspace while Marine One was ferrying President Barack Obama on February 16, 2012. Two F-16 fighter jets from March Air Reserve Base in Riverside County intercepted the Cessna at around 2:30pm local time. The plane was escorted to Long Beach Airport, where authorities discovered approximately 40 pounds of marijuana onboard, according to law enforcement officials. The Secret Service reported that the president was never in danger, although emergency procedures were implemented to remove the unauthorized aircraft from the restricted zone. The Federal Aviation Administration had issued a temporary flight restriction with an eight-mile radius around Los Angeles International Airport for the day. The Cessna violated this airspace limitation, as confirmed by FAA spokeswoman Brie Sachse. After landing, the pilot was taken into custody by local police and questioned by Homeland Security Investigations. The pilot now faces prosecution, said ICE spokeswoman Virginia Kice. NORAD spokesman Michael Kucharek declined to specify how closely the Cessna approached Marine One. The incursion led to a short delay in President Obama’s departure from Los Angeles International Airport as he prepared to board Air Force One for San Francisco, where he attended three fundraising events. Upon arrival in San Francisco, President Obama met Jodi Fisher, a 44-year-old cancer patient who had recently garnered attention for handing out free ice cream as part of her personal 'bucket list.' Meeting the president was also on her list, and White House staff arranged for the meeting at the airport. Air Force One is the call sign for any U.S. Air Force aircraft carrying the President.

Dwa myśliwce F-16 z bazy March Air Reserve w hrabstwie Riverside przechwyciły Cessnę około godziny 14:30 czasu lokalnego. Samolot został eskortowany na lotnisko Long Beach, gdzie służby znalazły około 18 kilogramów marihuany na pokładzie. Federalna Administracja Lotnictwa wprowadziła tego dnia tymczasowy zakaz lotów w promieniu ośmiu mil wokół lotniska Los Angeles. Cessna naruszyła ten zakaz, co potwierdziła rzeczniczka FAA Brie Sachse. Po wylądowaniu pilot został zatrzymany przez lokalną policję i przesłuchany przez Homeland Security Investigations. Jak przekazała rzeczniczka ICE Virginia Kice, pilot odpowie przed lokalnym wymiarem sprawiedliwości. Rzecznik NORAD Michael Kucharek nie podał, jak blisko Cessna znalazła się przy Marine One. Incydent spowodował krótkie opóźnienie w odlocie prezydenta Obamy z lotniska w Los Angeles na pokładzie Air Force One do San Francisco, gdzie uczestniczył w trzech wydarzeniach fundraisingowych. Po przylocie do San Francisco prezydent Obama spotkał się z 44-letnią Jodi Fisher, pacjentką chorą na raka, która zasłynęła niedawno rozdawaniem darmowych lodów jako element swojej „bucket list”. International observers have raised concerns about Israeli airstrikes in Gaza, which have led to the deaths of over 1,100 Palestinians and caused extensive destruction to critical infrastructure, such as hospitals and schools, amidst a continuing blockade. Human rights groups argue that Israel’s decision to halt the supply of electricity, water, and fuel to Gaza—a territory home to 2.3 million residents—amounts to collective punishment, contrary to international law. Israel maintains that these vital resources will not be reinstated until Hamas frees Israeli hostages who were captured during a recent incursion, which resulted in more than 1,200 Israeli deaths and the abduction of around 150 people.

The United States, through President Joe Biden, has pledged strong support for Israel, providing military aid and munitions. Although Biden stated the US upholds the laws of war, he did not publicly call for Israeli restraint in his conversations with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Experts on international law emphasize that both Israel and Hamas are equally obligated to abide by the laws prohibiting collective punishment. Reports indicate that hundreds of women and children have been killed in the ongoing offensive, and hospitals are struggling to care for more than 5,000 injured amid dwindling supplies.

International institutions like the UN and the International Criminal Court are investigating possible breaches of international law by both parties, with the UN’s rights chief Volker Turk highlighting the illegality of sieges that endanger civilian populations. Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant’s announcement of a “complete siege” and his inflammatory comments have intensified global concern. Additionally, attempts to deliver humanitarian aid have faced obstacles, and the region is experiencing acute shortages of food, water, and medical essentials. Ongoing discussions involving Egypt, the US, and others aim to allow humanitarian access, though Egypt opposes creating safe corridors out of Gaza, citing the importance of Palestinian claims to their homeland.

As civilian suffering escalates, global scrutiny is increasing over whether the conduct of Israel and Hamas complies with international humanitarian law. The UN Human Rights Council and an independent commission are gathering evidence of alleged war crimes by both sides. Some commentators, including former Israeli lawmakers, also criticize Western leaders for their support of Israeli actions, bringing further attention to issues of accountability and the future well-being of Gaza’s civilians.

article_content: The parents of Reeva Steenkamp, who was tragically killed at Oscar Pistorius's home on Valentine's Day, have spoken about the comfort they take from seeing her on the reality TV show 'Tropika Island of Treasure.' June and Barry Steenkamp are still mourning the loss of their daughter, but say that watching her on television feels like connecting with her beyond the grave. The show began airing episodes featuring Reeva three days after her death, which led to accusations of insensitivity from some viewers. However, the Steenkamps say the weekly broadcasts have become a source of solace. 'She's alive, she's happy, she's swimming with dolphins,' June Steenkamp told Grazia magazine. 'When I saw her greet everyone and blow kisses in the first episode, it felt like she was talking to me and saying goodbye.' On the show, Reeva competed alongside South African celebrities and other contestants for a one million rand (£72,500) prize. She was seen enjoying herself, participating in challenges like swimming with dolphins, and described herself as 'brainy, blonde, bombshell.' In a farewell message filmed on the set in Jamaica, she blew kisses to the camera and said, 'I’m going to miss you all so much. I love you very, very much.' The TV network faced criticism for capitalizing on Reeva's death by selling footage to the media, but producers argued the broadcasts served as a fitting tribute to the law graduate and model. Oscar Pistorius, a Paralympic champion, was charged with premeditated murder. He claims he accidentally shot Reeva after mistaking her for an intruder at his Pretoria home. Police have disputed this explanation. The Steenkamp family now communicate with Pistorius only through lawyers as they await the outcome of the trial. June Steenkamp expressed her sorrow, stating she would never get to see her daughter’s wedding or grandchildren, while Barry Steenkamp hopes the trial will provide clarity and closure. The family plans to scatter Reeva’s ashes at sea near Bloubergstrand with Table Mountain in the background. Reeva had told her parents that Pistorius was a good man and praised his charity work. Friends and family remember her as energetic and determined to live life fully.

June i Barry Steenkamp wciąż opłakują stratę córki, ale przyznają, że oglądanie jej w telewizji pozwala im poczuć kontakt z nią zza grobu. 'Kiedy obejrzałam pierwszy odcinek, w którym Reeva wszystkich wita i przesyła buziaki, miałam wrażenie, jakby mówiła do mnie i się żegnała.' W programie Reeva rywalizowała z celebrytami z RPA oraz innymi uczestnikami o nagrodę w wysokości miliona randów (72 500 funtów brytyjskich). Była pokazana, jak świetnie się bawi, bierze udział w wyzwaniach takich jak pływanie z delfinami, a sama siebie określała jako 'inteligentna, blond bomba'. W pożegnalnym nagraniu z Jamajki przesyłała buziaki do kamery, mówiąc: 'Będzie mi was bardzo brakować. Bardzo, bardzo was kocham.' Stacja telewizyjna spotkała się z krytyką za zarabianie na śmierci Reevy poprzez sprzedaż fragmentów programu mediom, ale producenci twierdzą, że emisja była godnym upamiętnieniem modelki i absolwentki prawa. Oscar Pistorius, mistrz paraolimpijski, został oskarżony o zabójstwo z premedytacją. Twierdzi, że zastrzelił Reevę przypadkowo, biorąc ją za włamywacza w swoim domu w Pretorii. June Steenkamp mówiła o swoim bólu, przyznając, że nigdy nie zobaczy ślubu córki, ani wnuków, a Barry Steenkamp ma nadzieję, że proces przyniesie odpowiedzi i pozwoli zamknąć ten rozdział. Rodzina planuje rozsypać prochy Reevy w morzu niedaleko Bloubergstrand z widokiem na Górę Stołową. Reeva mówiła rodzicom, że Pistorius jest dobrym człowiekiem i chwaliła go za działalność charytatywną. Przyjaciele i rodzina wspominają ją jako energiczną i zdeterminowaną, by w pełni wykorzystać życie.

article_content: Hostess Brands Inc., the maker of Twinkies, announced on Friday that it would be shutting down, ending the production of its iconic snack cakes. Social media platforms were quickly filled with comments expressing sadness over the loss of Twinkies. Many people rushed to stores to buy the remaining stock, and some even turned to online marketplaces like eBay. This wave of nostalgia seems driven by the snack’s prominent place in American childhood memories and pop culture. Despite the strong reactions, sales of Twinkies and similar products had already declined for years due to health concerns and changing dietary habits. Hostess had previously filed for bankruptcy twice: once in 2004 and again in 2012. The company suffered losses of $250 million over the last three years and had accumulated more than $850 million in debt. As people became increasingly aware of the health risks associated with sugary and processed foods, many stopped buying products like Twinkies. A typical pack of two Twinkies contains about 300 calories, nine grams of fat, and 37 ingredients, including high fructose corn syrup and several preservatives. Ding Dongs, another Hostess treat, contain 368 calories and 19.4 grams of fat per serving. Twinkies have also secured a spot in pop culture, appearing in movies such as 'Ghostbusters,' 'WALL-E,' and 'Zombieland,' where characters search for the last box of Twinkies. The snack even figured in the famous 'Twinkie defense' during Dan White’s 1979 trial for the killings of San Francisco Mayor George Moscone and Supervisor Harvey Milk. Although it is possible that another company might acquire the rights to produce Twinkies, the most significant loss is the 18,500 Hostess employees who are now out of work. Losing a job is especially difficult during a tough economy and right before the holiday season. While Hostess and the Baker's Union announced plans to enter mediation, offering a glimmer of hope, Twinkies' legacy will certainly persist in pop culture—even if you can no longer buy them in stores. The opinions in this commentary belong solely to Dean Obeidallah.

Wiele osób ruszyło do sklepów, by kupić ostatnie opakowania, a niektórzy szukali ich nawet na portalach aukcyjnych, jak eBay. Ta fala nostalgii wynika z ważnego miejsca, jakie Twinkies zajmują w amerykańskich wspomnieniach z dzieciństwa i popkulturze. Mimo silnych reakcji, sprzedaż Twinkies i podobnych produktów od lat malała z powodu troski o zdrowie i zmieniających się nawyków żywieniowych. Hostess dwukrotnie ogłaszała bankructwo: raz w 2004 roku i ponownie w 2012 roku. Firma zanotowała straty w wysokości 250 milionów dolarów w ciągu ostatnich trzech lat i zgromadziła ponad 850 milionów dolarów długu. W miarę jak więcej osób zaczęło zwracać uwagę na zagrożenia zdrowotne związane ze słodką i przetworzoną żywnością, wielu przestało kupować takie produkty. Typowe opakowanie dwóch Twinkies zawiera około 300 kalorii, dziewięć gramów tłuszczu oraz 37 składników, w tym syrop glukozowo-fruktozowy i liczne konserwanty. Ding Dongs, kolejna przekąska Hostess, ma 368 kalorii i 19,4 grama tłuszczu na porcję. Twinkies umocniły swoją pozycję w popkulturze, występując w filmach jak „Pogromcy duchów”, „WALL-E” czy „Zombieland”, gdzie bohaterowie szukają ostatniego opakowania Twinkies. Przekąska pojawiła się również w słynnej „obronie Twinkie” podczas procesu Dana White’a w 1979 roku po zabójstwach burmistrza San Francisco George’a Moscone i radnego Harveya Milka. Mimo że inna firma może wykupić prawa do produkcji Twinkies, największą stratą pozostaje 18 500 pracowników Hostess, którzy stracili pracę. Utrata zajęcia jest bardzo trudna zwłaszcza w ciężkich czasach gospodarczych i tuż przed świętami. Hostess i związek Baker's Union ogłosili rozpoczęcie mediacji, co daje odrobinę nadziei, ale dziedzictwo Twinkies na pewno przetrwa w popkulturze — nawet jeśli nie można już ich kupić w sklepach. Opinie zawarte w tym komentarzu należą wyłącznie do Deana Obeidallaha.

article_content: Instagram has reached over 300 million monthly active users, overtaking Twitter’s reported 284 million users from six weeks earlier. This growth comes less than a year after reaching 200 million users, demonstrating Instagram’s rapid rise. Acquired by Facebook in 2012, Instagram sees more than 70 million photos and videos shared daily. CEO Kevin Systrom expressed pride in this milestone, with Mark Zuckerberg commemorating the event on Instagram. Facebook’s acquisition was finalized in September 2012 for about $1 billion, but due to changes in Facebook’s share price, the final value was closer to $700 million. Systrom highlighted the evolution of Instagram from an idea between two friends to a global creative platform, showcasing content ranging from river vistas to celebrity insights. Systrom reiterated Instagram's strategic importance to Facebook, emphasizing its ability to engage diverse audiences and its innovative advertising initiatives. He mentioned that Instagram, along with WhatsApp and Oculus Rift, forms a key part of Facebook’s multi-product strategy. Launched in October 2010, Instagram quickly grew to a million users by December of that year, and has added 100 million users since March 2014 alone. The company recently announced the most popular posts on the platform. Kim Kardashian’s wedding photo with Kanye West became the most liked image in Instagram’s history, earning 2.4 million likes. Justin Bieber and Selena Gomez’s selfie followed with 1.9 million likes, and Ariana Grande’s backstage photo with Miley Cyrus received 1.84 million. To enhance user experience, Instagram is introducing verified badges for celebrities, athletes, and brands, and intensifying efforts to eliminate spam by deactivating fake accounts. Systrom asserted the importance of authenticity on the platform. Top geotagged locations worldwide were Disneyland (Anaheim), Dodger Stadium (LA), and Times Square (NY). In the UK, Tower Bridge and the Tower of London were most popular, with events like the poppy installation at the Tower of London heavily featured. Additional top US locations included Madison Square Garden, Yankee Stadium, the Golden Gate Bridge, Santa Monica Pier, and Universal Studios Hollywood. The hashtag #love was Instagram’s most used this year. Regarding museums, the Louvre (Paris), MoMA, and the Metropolitan Museum of Art (NY) were the top favorites globally, supporting Instagram’s role as a digital gallery for visual history. Leading UK locations: Tower Bridge, Tower of London, Harrods, Big Ben, British Museum, London Eye, Camden Town, Hyde Park, Victoria and Albert Museum, Natural History Museum. Top US locations: Disneyland (Anaheim), Dodger Stadium (LA), Times Square (NY), Madison Square Garden (NY), Yankee Stadium (NY), AT&T Park (SF), Golden Gate Bridge, Santa Monica Pier, Universal Studios Hollywood, Fenway Park. Top global museums: Musée du Louvre, MoMA (NY), Metropolitan Museum of Art (NY), LACMA, Hermitage Museum, Centre Pompidou, British Museum, Victoria and Albert Museum, Tate Modern, Art Institute of Chicago.

Misty Upham, a 32-year-old Native American actress recognized for her roles in films such as "Frozen River" and "August: Osage County," has been missing for over a week, her family reports. She was last seen on October 5 after leaving her sister’s apartment in Muckleshoot, near Seattle, Washington. Her absence has led to a search effort by relatives and local police.

In statements to the public and on Misty’s Facebook page, her father, Charles Upham, explained that Misty has experienced bipolar disorder, anxiety, and depression, but he does not believe she is missing due to self-harm. He suspects she may have gotten lost or encountered danger and emphasizes the urgency of the search. The family has been distributing posters, checking hospitals and shelters, and searching the area around Muckleshoot.

Misty is part of the Blackfoot tribe and had her hair cut short when last seen. She was wearing a purple sweater, black T-shirt, gray sweatpants, silver tennis shoes, and was carrying an ID and a white cell phone. The Auburn Police Department is investigating and has entered her details into Washington’s missing persons database.

Upham is acclaimed for her performance in "Frozen River," and also appeared in "August: Osage County," "Django Unchained," and the upcoming film "Cake." The family asks anyone with information to email charlesupham@gmail.com or contact Auburn Police at 253-288-2121.

Ostatni raz widziano ją 5 października, kiedy opuszczała mieszkanie swojej siostry w Muckleshoot, niedaleko Seattle. Jej zaginięcie uruchomiło poszukiwania prowadzone przez bliskich i lokalną policję.

Ojciec Misty, Charles Upham, w oświadczeniach publicznych i na jej Facebooku poinformował, że córka chorowała na zaburzenie afektywne dwubiegunowe, miała stany lękowe i depresję, ale nie uważa, by jej zaginięcie wiązało się z próbą samobójczą. Podejrzewa, że Misty mogła się zgubić lub spotkać kogoś niebezpiecznego, i podkreśla, jak pilne jest jej odnalezienie. Rodzina rozwiesza plakaty, sprawdza szpitale i schroniska oraz przeszukuje okolicę Muckleshoot.

Misty należy do plemienia Blackfootów. W dniu zaginięcia miała krótkie włosy, była ubrana w fioletowy sweter, czarną koszulkę, szare spodnie dresowe i srebrne tenisówki; miała przy sobie dowód osobisty i biały telefon komórkowy. Policja w Auburn prowadzi postępowanie, jej dane są wprowadzone do stanowej bazy osób zaginionych.

Upham znana jest z nagradzanej roli w „Frozen River”, a także z występów w „Sierpniu w hrabstwie Osage”, „Django” oraz nadchodzącym filmie „Cake”. Rodzina prosi, by wszelkie informacje zgłaszać na adres charlesupham@gmail.com lub do policji w Auburn pod numerem 253-288-2121.

article_content:
This week, 37-year-old Marissa Mayer became CEO of Yahoo, an internet company facing many challenges, though attracting users is not one of them—the company states that more than 500 million people access its products each month. Mayer told The New York Times that she considers Yahoo "one of the best brands on the internet." Mayer also announced Tuesday that she is pregnant; she and her husband, Zack Bogue, are expecting a baby boy in October.

A veteran of Silicon Valley, Mayer became Google’s 20th employee in 1999 after earning a Master's in Computer Science from Stanford University. After 13 years at Google, where she led both the search team and, more recently, location and maps services, Mayer recently joined the board of Walmart. Now, as one of the most powerful women in technology, Mayer often shares her thoughts on life and work. Here are some lessons that have guided her career:

Push through your uncertainty. 
“I always did something I was a little not ready to do. I think that’s how you grow. When there’s that moment of ‘Wow, I’m not really sure I can do this,’ and you push through those moments, that’s when you have a breakthrough. Sometimes that’s a sign that something really good is about to happen. You’re about to grow and learn a lot about yourself,” she told CNN in April.

Protect what’s really important to you. 
“I have a theory that burnout is about resentment. And you beat it by knowing what it is you’re giving up that makes you resentful. I tell people: Find your rhythm. Your rhythm is what matters to you so much that when you miss it, you’re resentful of your work...So find your rhythm, understand what makes you resentful, and protect it. You can’t have everything you want, but you can have the things that really matter to you. And thinking that way empowers you to work really hard for a very long time,” Mayer said to Bloomberg Businessweek.

Work with smart people. 
“It’s really wonderful to work in an environment with a lot of smart people. I think it challenges you to think and work on a different level,” she explained during a talk at Stanford’s Entrepreneurial Thought Leader Speaker Series in 2006.

Keep some outside perspective. 
“I’ve always loved baking. I think it’s because I’m very scientific. The best cooks are chemists... I’m a businesswoman first and foremost, but my hobbies actually make me better at work. They help me come up with new and innovative ways of looking at things,” Mayer said in a 2008 interview with San Francisco magazine.

Work with a target customer in mind. 
“I always put the user first when I get ideas pitched to me. I like to think of my mom and wonder if she would understand an idea right away,” she told WetFeet.com in 2008.

Set constraints to boost your creativity. 
“People think of creativity as this sort of unbridled thing, but engineers thrive on constraints. They love to think their way out of that little box: ‘We know you said it was impossible, but we’re going to do this, this, and that to get us there,” Mayer said in Fast Company in 2008.

How do you balance career and family? Let us know on CNN iReport.

Mayer powiedziała The New York Times, że uważa Yahoo za „jedną z najlepszych marek w internecie.” Mayer ogłosiła też we wtorek, że jest w ciąży; ona i jej mąż, Zack Bogue, spodziewają się syna w październiku.

Doświadczona w branży Doliny Krzemowej Mayer została 20. pracownikiem Google w 1999 roku po uzyskaniu tytułu magistra informatyki na Uniwersytecie Stanforda. Po 13 latach pracy w Google, gdzie kierowała zespołem wyszukiwarki, a później także działem usług lokalizacyjnych i map, Mayer niedawno dołączyła do zarządu Walmart. Obecnie, jako jedna z najbardziej wpływowych kobiet w technologii, Mayer często dzieli się swoimi przemyśleniami na temat życia i pracy. Oto kilka lekcji, które kierowały jej karierą:

Przełamuj swoje niepewności. 
„Zawsze robiłam coś, na co nie byłam całkowicie gotowa. Uważam, że tak się rozwijamy. Gdy pojawia się moment: ‘Wow, nie jestem pewna, czy dam radę’, i przez to przejdziesz, to właśnie wtedy następuje przełom. Często to znak, że wydarzy się coś naprawdę dobrego. Zaraz się rozwiniesz i dowiesz się dużo o sobie,” powiedziała Mayer w kwietniu dla CNN.

Chroń to, co dla ciebie naprawdę ważne. 
„Mam teorię, że wypalenie to efekt żalu. Można go pokonać, jeśli wiesz, z czego rezygnujesz i co ten żal powoduje. Mówię ludziom: Znajdź swój rytm. To, co jest dla ciebie tak ważne, że gdy tego brakuje, żałujesz pracy... Znajdź ten rytm, zrozum, co sprawia ci żal i chroń to. Nie możesz mieć wszystkiego, ale możesz mieć to, co dla ciebie naprawdę się liczy. Takie myślenie daje siłę do długotrwałej, ciężkiej pracy,” powiedziała Mayer w Bloomberg Businessweek.

Pracuj z bystrymi ludźmi. 
„Praca w otoczeniu wielu mądrych osób jest naprawdę wspaniała. Myślę, że prowokuje cię to do myślenia i pracy na wyższym poziomie,” wyjaśniła podczas wykładu na Stanford Entrepreneurial Thought Leader Speaker Series w 2006 roku.

Zachowuj dystans i perspektywę. 
„Zawsze lubiłam piec. Myślę, że to dlatego, iż jestem bardzo naukowa. Najlepsi kucharze to chemicy... Przede wszystkim jestem bizneswoman, ale moje zainteresowania naprawdę pomagają mi w pracy. Dzięki nim znajduję nowe, innowacyjne spojrzenia na sprawy,” powiedziała Mayer w wywiadzie dla San Francisco magazine w 2008 roku.

Myśl o odbiorcy końcowym. 
„Zawsze stawiam użytkownika na pierwszym miejscu, gdy ktoś prezentuje mi nowe pomysły. Lubię myśleć o mojej mamie i zastanawiać się, czy z miejsca zrozumiałaby dany pomysł,” powiedziała w 2008 roku portalowi WetFeet.com.

Ustalaj ograniczenia, aby pobudzać kreatywność. 
„Ludzie myślą, że kreatywność to coś nieograniczonego, ale inżynierowie najlepiej radzą sobie, kiedy mają ograniczenia. Uwielbiają wymyślać wyjście z trudnych sytuacji: ‘Wiem, że powiedzieliście, że to niemożliwe, ale zrobimy to, tamto i jeszcze coś, by to osiągnąć,’” powiedziała Mayer w Fast Company w 2008 roku.

Jak łączysz pracę z życiem rodzinnym? Daj znać na CNN iReport.

Amazon is enhancing its Prime membership by offering discounted access to One Medical, a primary care service it owns. Prime members can now enroll in One Medical for $9 a month (or $99 annually), a significant reduction from the regular $199 yearly price. Members can add additional household members for $66 each. One Medical provides 24/7 virtual care, fast appointments for common health issues, and options for either in-person or online visits. All virtual services are included at no extra cost, while in-person appointments can be covered by insurance or paid directly.

Amazon acquired One Medical last year for nearly $3.9 billion, showing its increasing investment in healthcare. Research highlights the importance of primary care for better community health; for instance, a major study in JAMA Internal Medicine linked increased access to primary care to longer life expectancy. However, a shortage of primary care clinicians looms: the Association of American Medical Colleges predicts a deficit of 21,400 to 55,200 primary care doctors by 2033. The field is known for heavy workloads, the need for coordination across specialties, and growing administrative challenges.

Other retail giants—like CVS with its MinuteClinic, Walgreens with Village Medical, and Walmart Health—are also rapidly expanding primary care offerings. Amazon aims to make care more accessible and affordable by linking One Medical with Amazon Pharmacy and Amazon Clinic. With the rise of telehealth, people in rural or underserved areas can now get care more easily, provided they have internet access.

As retail companies race to expand healthcare access, patients may soon have more convenient and affordable options. While the industry continues to develop, innovative models could help millions maintain better health.

Amazon przejął One Medical w zeszłym roku za około 3,9 miliarda dolarów, pokazując swoje rosnące zaangażowanie w sektor medyczny. Badania naukowe podkreślają kluczowe znaczenie opieki podstawowej dla zdrowia społeczeństwa – np. analiza z JAMA Internal Medicine powiązała lepszy dostęp do lekarzy rodzinnych ze wzrostem długości życia. article_content: Kerry Miller, 46, a former administrative worker at Burton Albion FC, is accused of inappropriate conduct toward club players, including allegedly sending intimate photos to striker Billy Kee, 23. At her employment tribunal, it was alleged that Miller entered the players’ dressing rooms on 15 occasions, often while they were getting changed after matches. Rumors were also raised about Miller having a relationship with former goalkeeper Stuart Tomlinson, 28, who later pursued a career in WWE wrestling after leaving football due to a knee injury. Miller admitted to a casual relationship with ex-defender Ryan Austin, 29. At the Leicester tribunal, club chairman Ben Robinson testified he was aware of rumors concerning Miller and Tomlinson, and he stated that Tomlinson worked as a model and male escort while at the club. Fleur Robinson, club secretary and commercial director, as well as the chairman’s daughter, stated she warned Miller about publicly socializing with players, particularly after Miller posted a Facebook photo with Tomlinson shortly after a significant match. Robinson also recounted cautioning Miller after complaints from manager Gary Rowett regarding her entering players’ dressing rooms. Miller began working at the club in September 2011 and resigned in February 2013 following a dispute. She denies entering the dressing rooms without knocking and is claiming constructive dismissal, sexual discrimination, and harassment against the club. Burton Albion denies all allegations. Veteran defender Aaron Webster, 32, described Miller as someone who frequently flirted with staff and players and was viewed as a threat by some players’ partners. He said he saw intimate photos of Miller on players’ phones and heard rumors regarding Miller and Tomlinson, but no direct confirmation. article_content: Most dogs are content with long walks, a cozy bed, and basic treats, but Mr Darcy, a pampered pug from Ayrshire, enjoys a truly luxurious lifestyle. His owner, Julia Ashton, treats him to steak, organic chicken, and salmon, as well as a wardrobe full of designer outfits. For Christmas, he will even receive a custom-knitted Nordic sweater. Mr Darcy's indulgences also include the occasional Victoria sponge cake, and he sleeps in Julia’s queen-size bed. Julia, 48, who lives in Kilmarnock, insists that Mr Darcy is not spoiled but simply receives the level of care she believes pugs deserve. She explains that while some might see her dog as spoiled, many pet owners indulge their animals to some degree. As a dedicated breeder and the owner of a pet holiday retreat called Bed and Biscuits, Julia has several dogs, but show dog Mr Darcy is her favorite. She takes him to dog shows nationwide, which means he follows a strict regimen of diet, exercise, and grooming to stay in top condition. Mr Darcy even enjoys exercising at home on his treadmill and agility course and is groomed weekly. Julia remarks that pugs dislike cold and rain, so he owns many jackets and sweaters to keep warm throughout the winter. In addition to feeding him a first-class diet and ensuring he travels in comfort, Julia plans to launch Barkers and Bones, a clothing line for small dogs. Julia, who has bred pugs for five years, praises them as affectionate, intelligent, and charming companions, noting that their cuteness often means they get away with a lot, though discipline remains important. She emphasizes the responsibilities of pet ownership and cautions against buying from unethical breeders, advising prospective owners to seek out breed clubs or the Kennel Club. Julia's lifelong experience with animals informs her commitment to providing her pets with excellent care, even if others sometimes find Mr Darcy’s luxurious life amusing.

Adam Mosseri, Head of Instagram, has announced several new updates to Meta’s Threads app. Most notably, users can now delete their Threads profiles without affecting their Instagram accounts—an option many have requested. To do this, go to Settings, select Account, tap Delete or Deactivate Profile, and then choose Delete.

Another update allows users to easily control whether their Threads posts appear on Facebook and Instagram. This is optional and can be managed in Settings under Privacy, letting users opt out of sharing Threads content on those platforms.

Despite these improvements, Threads users continue to request more features. Some would like a drafts folder, while others want to mute specific words and phrases across the app to avoid spoilers and unwanted content. Mosseri has started responding to user feedback, indicating that additional updates may be forthcoming.

article_content: A Los Angeles jury has found that concert promoter AEG Live LLC was not negligent in hiring Dr. Conrad Murray, the physician who administered a fatal dose of propofol to Michael Jackson in 2009. The verdict follows Katherine Jackson’s lawsuit, which alleged AEG Live failed to properly investigate Murray’s background before allowing him to treat her son during preparations for the ‘This Is It’ concert series in London. Dr. Murray was convicted of involuntary manslaughter in 2011 for causing Jackson’s death. Katherine Jackson sought hundreds of millions in damages for herself and Jackson’s three children, claiming AEG Live should have vetted Murray more thoroughly. However, AEG Live denied hiring Murray, asserting that Michael Jackson personally selected his own doctor for the shows. The case, which ran over five months and included testimony from more than 50 witnesses, provided an unprecedented look into Jackson’s health, drug use, and his efforts to sustain a major comeback. Testimony revealed Jackson struggled with chronic pain and insomnia, leading him to seek nightly administration of propofol, an anesthetic not intended for non-hospital use. AEG Live’s lawyers argued the company would have canceled the tour if they had known about Jackson’s drug use. They characterized the situation as one of personal choice, insisting Jackson was responsible for his medical decisions and the doctors he employed. The defense also argued that both Jackson and Murray concealed the extent of the drug use from AEG Live. Jackson’s legal team claimed that financial motivations led AEG Live and Murray to prioritize profit over the star’s wellbeing. Evidence showed Murray stood to earn $150,000 a month—income that would help him resolve significant personal debts. AEG, for its part, aimed to launch a lucrative world tour with the King of Pop. In deliberations, jurors were first asked whether AEG Live had actually hired Murray. Although there was a draft contract with Murray’s signature, it lacked signatures from both AEG Live and Jackson, leading to debate over its binding nature. Ultimately, the jury found that AEG Live was not responsible for hiring Murray, and therefore not liable for Jackson’s death. The trial revealed sensitive details about Jackson’s history with prescription drugs and his close relationships with several doctors. Questions about Jackson’s future earning potential were also addressed, with AEG Live’s experts stating projections were speculative at best. Today, Michael Jackson’s estate continues to support his family and has alleviated past financial debts through new projects and music.
